_sources.pre_seed: derived: median pre-seed round / median pre-seed post-money (funding ladder)

dilution._note: growth uses the Series D median (7.5%, secondary source citing Carta)

_notes.acqToLastPost: derived: Crunchbase sample of 225 acquisitions, ~12% sold below capital raised (research/base_rates.json region_notes); median sale price set so ~12% of simulated acquisitions land below capital raised.
_notes.ipoToLastPost: assumption: IPO market cap centred on the last private valuation (sd 0.45 in log space), pending data.

winter._note: derived: three US venture downturns in 25 years (2001, 2008–09, 2022–23) → ~70% chance of one in a 10-year window; during it seed→A odds ×0.51 and shutdowns ×1.26 (Carta 2022–23 crunch multipliers in research/base_rates.json).

_notes.sigma: derived: Carta mid-2025 P95 seed valuation $72.2M vs ~$20M median → log-sd ≈ 0.78.
_notes.evidence: modelling choice: comps act like 8 pseudo-observations against the base rate, capped to ×0.55–×1.8.
_notes.quality: modelling choice: each universe has a hidden quality score so strong companies keep doing well (power law).
_notes.stall: modelling choice: a company that neither raises, sells nor dies at a rung (the ladder remainder) gets one more roll later in which it can only sell, shut down (at 1.6x the usual odds) or stay a zombie: the ladder graduation rates are already eventual, so stalls never add extra rounds. Calibrated so ~60-65% of pre-seed universes close within the horizon (Carta 2018 cohort: 61.9% closed after 6.5 years).

moonshotModel._note: assumption pending deep-tech base rates: harder early rounds (x0.65), longer gaps (x1.3), 2.5x bigger rounds, fatter-tailed valuations (log-sd 1.2) and one possible near-death rescue (30%). Net effect vs a normal pre-seed startup: more deaths (~76% vs ~73% in 10 years), ~1.4x the unicorns and ~10x the decacorns.

companies.o: Kai-Fu Lee's model lab that became a unicorn in eight months, then stopped training frontier models
companies.story: Founded by Kai-Fu Lee in 2023, 01.AI hit a $1B valuation within eight months with Alibaba's backing and released the Yi open models. Facing the cost of keeping up with larger rivals and DeepSeek's cheap models, in early 2025 it stopped chasing frontier pre-training, moved most of that team into a lab with Alibaba Cloud, and pivoted to selling customised enterprise deployments, often built on other companies' open models.

near.what: Stopped pre-training frontier models; much of its pre-training team moved to an Alibaba Cloud lab and it repositioned as an enterprise deployment company

companies.o: AI digital sales workers (Alice SDR) sold to revenue teams
companies.story: 11x raised $24M led by Benchmark and a reported $50M Series B led by a16z in 2024. TechCrunch reported in 2025 that it claimed customers it did not have, and the CEO later stepped down amid retention problems.

companies.o: Online travel agency selling cheap tickets built on airline miles and prepaid flexible-date promo trips
companies.story: 123milhas sold discounted air tickets sourced from frequent-flyer miles, then pushed 'Promo123' flexible-date tickets and packages paid upfront for future travel, effectively betting that fares would fall without any hedge. When fares stayed high it suspended the Promo line in August 2023 and on 29 August filed for judicial recovery in Belo Horizonte, declaring R$2.308bn (~$462M at 2023 rates) of debt owed to around 700,000 creditors, most of them customers. Peer Maxmilhas also filed for judicial recovery as the Brazilian online travel sector's prepaid model unravelled.

companies.o: Norwegian-born maker of the NEO humanoid sold as a $20,000 home helper
companies.story: Founded in Norway in 2014 as Halodi Robotics, the company spent nearly a decade building the wheeled EVE robot for security guarding before renaming itself 1X in 2023 after an OpenAI Startup Fund-led round. It raised $100M led by EQT in January 2024 and in October 2025 opened preorders for the NEO home humanoid at $20,000 (or $499/month), which relies partly on remote human teleoperators; reports in September 2025 of talks to raise up to $1B at a $10B+ valuation were not confirmed by the company.

companies.o: African genomics company building a biobank of African DNA for drug discovery
companies.story: 54gene raised about $45M to sequence under-represented African genomes for pharma partners and expanded into COVID testing and a diagnostics arm. Its founder-CEO stepped down in 2022 amid layoffs and a valuation cut of over $100M, and the company wound down in 2023 while seeking buyers for its biobank.

companies.o: Collaborative warehouse picking robots bought by Shopify, then sold on to Ocado
companies.story: Founded by former Kiva Systems executives after Amazon bought Kiva and stopped selling it to others, 6 River built 'Chuck' collaborative robots that guide warehouse pickers. Shopify bought it in 2019 for about $450M in cash and stock to power its fulfilment network, then exited logistics and sold 6 River to Ocado in 2023, a reminder that strategic owners can change course.

companies.o: Small-launch startup (RS1 rocket) that quit orbital launch after failures and pivoted to missile-defense test vehicles as Long Wall.
companies.story: ABL raised nearly half a billion dollars, including a 2021 round at a $2.4B valuation, to fly the containerised RS1 rocket; its first launch failed in January 2023 and another RS1 was destroyed in a 2024 ground fire. In November 2024 it abandoned orbital launch to repurpose its rockets and ground systems for missile defense, renaming itself Long Wall in February 2025 and later unveiling an interceptor.

near.what: First RS1 launch failed shortly after liftoff from Kodiak, Alaska
Second RS1 destroyed in a ground fire; company exited orbital launch

companies.o: Ambient AI clinical documentation for health systems
companies.story: Abridge raised a $250M Series D in February 2025 at $2.75B post-money, led by Elad Gil and IVP, then a $300M Series E in June 2025 led by Andreessen Horowitz at $5.3B. It is the valuation leader among AI scribes.

companies.o: AI agents built around each revenue account, positioned as an alternative to failed AI SDRs
companies.story: Actively raised a $22.5M round in April 2025 ($17.5M Series A from Bain Capital Ventures) while saying AI SDRs had failed. A later $45M Series B was co-led by TCV and First Harmonic; the date is unclear.

companies.o: AI agents that operate software on a user's behalf
companies.story: Adept was founded by ex-OpenAI and Google researchers to build AI agents that click and type in software for users, raising about $415M. In June 2024 Amazon hired CEO David Luan, four co-founders and a large share of staff and took a non-exclusive license to its technology, with terms undisclosed.

companies.o: Single global payments platform for large merchants, built on its own stack
companies.story: Adyen's founders had already sold payments firm Bibit and rebuilt payments as one in-house platform, winning clients like Uber, Spotify and eBay. Profitable early, it raised little and listed in Amsterdam in 2018 at about €7.1B (~$8.4B), roughly doubling on day one.

companies.o: Streamed over-the-air TV to subscribers using thousands of tiny antennas
companies.story: Backed by Barry Diller's IAC, Aereo assigned each subscriber a dime-sized antenna to stream broadcast channels, arguing it did not need to pay networks. In June 2014 the US Supreme Court ruled against it in ABC v. Aereo, and it filed for bankruptcy that November.

companies.o: Chinese humanoid maker founded in 2023 that bought control of a listed company within two years
companies.story: Ex-Huawei engineer and tech influencer Peng Zhihui co-founded AgiBot in February 2023, and it moved quickly into mass production of humanoids, reporting 1.05B yuan of revenue for 2025. In July 2025 it agreed to buy 63.62% of Shanghai-listed Swancor Advanced Materials for about 2.1B yuan (~$289M), which it denied was a backdoor listing; by October 2026 it was reported to be near a new round at about 50B yuan (~$7B) ahead of a planned Hong Kong IPO.

companies.o: Maker of Digit, a bipedal humanoid that moves totes in warehouses and factories
companies.story: Spun out of Oregon State's legged-robotics lab in 2015, Agility built the ostrich-like Cassie and then Digit, and focused narrowly on moving totes for paying customers like GXO, Schaeffler and Toyota. It had raised only $29M by 2020, then $150M in 2022 with Amazon's fund and a $400M Series C in 2025 at about $2.1B; in June 2026 it agreed to go public via a SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI at a $2.5B pre-money value, later cutting expected proceeds from $620M to about $465M.

companies.o: IIT Madras-incubated rocket startup flying the Agnibaan launcher on Agnilet, the world's first single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine.
companies.story: Agnikul, incubated at IIT Madras's National Centre for Combustion R&D in Chennai and led by co-founder/CEO Srinath Ravichandran, bet that an entire rocket engine could be 3D-printed as a single piece. On 30 May 2024 its Agnibaan SOrTeD flew from India's first private launchpad after a run of scrubs since March (one 28 May attempt was called off seconds before lift-off), which ISRO called the first controlled flight of an additively manufactured semi-cryogenic engine. A ~Rs150 crore (~$17M) round in November 2025 valued it at $500M; total raised is reported as over $78M by Inc42 (CB Insights lists ~$61M).

near.what: Agnibaan SOrTeD launch scrubbed repeatedly from March to May 2024 (including a 28 May abort less than a minute before lift-off) before flying on the fifth attempt on 30 May.

companies.o: Israeli LLM lab behind the Jurassic and Jamba models and the Wordtune writing app
companies.story: Founded in 2017 by Yoav Shoham, Ori Goshen and Mobileye's Amnon Shashua, AI21 was an early GPT-3 rival and later shipped the Jamba hybrid Transformer/Mamba models. It reached $1.4B in 2023 but was squeezed by far larger labs. Calcalist reported in December 2025 that Nvidia was in advanced talks to buy it for $2-3B; the deal did not happen, and in 2026 it was reported in talks with Nebius.

companies.o: Clinical AI platform for imaging triage and hospital workflows
companies.story: Aidoc raised a $150M Series E in 2026 led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives with General Catalyst, SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and NVentures; total funding exceeds $500M. Earlier rounds include $110M and $66M.

companies.o: Marketplace letting people rent out spare rooms and homes to travelers.
companies.story: Founded in 2008 as AirBed & Breakfast, the idea of paying to sleep on a stranger's air mattress was dismissed by most investors; in June 2008 seven investors were offered 10% for $150,000 and none bit, and the founders kept the company alive by selling Obama O's and Cap'n McCain's cereal (about $30,000) before Y Combinator and Sequoia backed them in 2009. After a $31B private valuation fell to about $18B when COVID-19 crushed travel and it took a high-interest $1B Silver Lake/Sixth Street lifeline in April 2020, Airbnb IPO'd on Nasdaq in December 2020 at $68 (about $47B fully diluted) and closed day one at $144.71 for a roughly $86.5B market cap (peak_valuation_usd uses that first-day cap; later intraday highs not verified).

near.what: Out of money and in credit card debt, founders sold ~800 boxes of novelty election cereal (Obama O's, Cap'n McCain's) at $40 each, netting about $30,000.
COVID-19 collapsed bookings; Airbnb took $1B in debt and equity from Silver Lake and Sixth Street at over 10% interest as its valuation reportedly fell from $31B to $18B.

dismissed.quote_or_fact: Fact: offered 10% of the company for $150,000 (a $1.5M valuation); five sent rejection emails and two never replied, per Brian Chesky's 2015 post '7 Rejections'.
"They have an interesting business. I'm just not sure how big it's going to be."
Paraphrase: USV passed because it could not picture air mattresses on living-room floors becoming a substitute for hotel rooms; Wilson later kept the cereal boxes as a reminder of the miss.

companies.o: Enterprise drone operating system and analytics platform that shut down after burning $118M
companies.story: Airware raised about $118M from Kleiner Perkins, Andreessen Horowitz, Google Ventures and others to build an enterprise 'operating system' for commercial drones, first making its own autopilot hardware and then pivoting to analytics for insurers and mines. Cheap DJI hardware and slow enterprise adoption undercut it, and it shut down abruptly in September 2018.

companies.o: Digital health insurer for companies and their employees
companies.story: Alan became the first new French insurer licensed in decades and sells top-up health cover through employers in France, Belgium and Spain. A €173M round led by Belfius in 2024 valued it at €4B (~$4.3B).

companies.o: Tried to sell airplane-quality 10 cm satellite imagery from very low Earth orbit, then pivoted to selling VLEO satellite buses.
companies.story: Albedo raised $97M to fly satellites low enough (very low Earth orbit) to capture 10 cm visible imagery, a resolution previously limited to aircraft and spy satellites. Its first satellite, Clarity-1, launched in March 2025 and went into a protective mode after first contact; per Wikipedia it lacked thrust, decayed and reentered in June 2026, and the company pivoted to building VLEO satellite buses for other operators.

companies.o: French maker of the Pepper and NAO humanoids that ended in receivership
companies.story: Aldebaran's small NAO humanoid became a standard research and education robot, and SoftBank took control in 2012 and launched the Pepper 'emotional' robot in 2014 for shops and banks. Pepper never found a lasting job, production was paused in 2021, and SoftBank sold the unit to United Robotics Group in 2022; Aldebaran filed for insolvency in February 2025 after two buyers fell through, and Shenzhen-based Maxvision bought the core Pepper and NAO assets in mid-2025.

companies.o: Germany's sovereign-LLM hope that quit the frontier race and was folded into Cohere
companies.story: Founded by Jonas Andrulis in 2019, Aleph Alpha was pitched as Europe's answer to OpenAI and announced a '$500M' Series B in 2023 from Schwarz Group, Bosch and SAP, although much of it was reportedly grants and commitments rather than cash. By 2024 it had stopped trying to compete on frontier models and repositioned around its PhariaAI enterprise software. In April 2026 Cohere agreed to take it over with Schwarz Group as the key backer and both governments' blessing, closing later in 2026.

companies.o: AI coding assistant for Xcode
companies.story: A three-person team, Alex's founders joined OpenAI's Codex group in September 2025. It is unclear whether everyone moved or what happened to the product.

companies.o: AI market intelligence and search platform for investors and corporates
companies.story: AlphaSense announced a $350M round in June 2026 led by Vitruvian Partners, Accenture Ventures and J.P. Morgan Asset Management. Valuation reportedly rose to $7.5B from $4B in 2024.

companies.o: Online bookstore that became the everything store
companies.story: Amazon started selling books online in 1995 and went public in May 1997 at $18 a share, raising $54M at a valuation of about $438M. It raised more debt before the 2000 crash, survived while peers like eToys and Pets.com died, and became one of the world's most valuable companies.

companies.o: UC Berkeley Dex-Net spinout whose AI robots sort parcels for shippers
companies.story: Ambi was spun out of Ken Goldberg's UC Berkeley lab, where the Dex-Net project trained robot grasping on millions of simulated objects. It launched in 2021 with a $6.1M seed and a $26M Series A led by Tiger Global, and sells AmbiSort parcel-sorting systems to shippers such as Pitney Bowes, later raising further growth money.

companies.o: AI platform for clinical documentation and point-of-care coding
companies.story: Ambience raised a $243M Series C in July 2025 co-led by Oak HC/FT and Andreessen Horowitz at a $1.25B valuation, after a $70M Series B in February 2024. It has raised $345M to date.

companies.o: Marketplace placing vetted African (now global) software engineers in remote roles
companies.story: Andela started by training developers in Lagos and placing them with US companies, then went fully remote and global in 2020, closing its African campuses. Remote work demand drove a $200M Series E led by SoftBank at $1.5B in 2021.

companies.o: Arabic-first music streaming service
companies.story: Anghami launched in Beirut in 2012, years before Spotify entered the Middle East, licensing Arabic catalogues and billing through telcos. It became the first Arab tech company to list on Nasdaq via a 2022 SPAC at roughly $220M; OSN+ later took majority control.

companies.o: Maker of the Cozmo and Vector AI toy robots that shut down after a last-minute funding failure
companies.story: Carnegie Mellon robotics graduates founded Anki, which launched to fanfare at Apple's 2013 developer event and sold millions of Overdrive cars and Cozmo robots, raising close to $200M from Index Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz and others. Toy-like products with $180-$250 price tags and seasonal sales never covered the cost of its AI, and when a new financing fell through at the last minute it shut down in April 2019, laying off nearly 200 staff; Digital Dream Labs later bought its assets.

companies.o: Frontier AI lab behind the Claude models, sold mainly to enterprises and developers via API
companies.story: Founded in 2021 by Dario and Daniela Amodei and other ex-OpenAI researchers around a safety-first pitch. Its 2022 Series B was led by Sam Bankman-Fried, whose FTX collapse months later left the stake in a bankruptcy estate, but Amazon and Google then committed billions in compute-linked investment. Claude's lead in coding and enterprise use took it from a $61.5B valuation in March 2025 to $380B in February 2026 and a reported $965B in May 2026 (AP), above OpenAI's last reported $852B.

companies.o: Maker of Cursor, an AI-first code editor
companies.story: Founded by four MIT students, Anysphere forked VS Code into Cursor and built AI editing directly into the editor, arriving just as models became good enough. It grew to a $9.9B valuation by mid-2025 with reported later rounds far higher, while earlier AI coding startup Kite had shut down in 2022 and rival Windsurf was split up.

companies.o: Mass-produces standardized satellite buses so customers can buy a spacecraft off the shelf instead of custom-building it.
companies.story: Apex was founded in 2022 to turn satellite buses, traditionally custom-built over years, into a standard product shipped in months, and flew its first bus within about two years. Riding US defense constellation demand, it raised $200M at a $2.3B valuation in June 2026; a single aggregator reports a later $500M round at $4B that is unconfirmed.

companies.o: Giant high-tech greenhouses growing tomatoes in Kentucky
companies.story: AppHarvest promised to bring agtech jobs to Appalachia with huge greenhouses and went public via SPAC in early 2021. Crop yields and quality fell short and costs ran high, and it filed for Chapter 11 in July 2023.

companies.o: Programmatic advertising exchange and ad-buying platform
companies.story: AppNexus built one of the largest independent real-time ad exchanges as an alternative to Google's ad stack. AT&T bought it in 2018 for a reported $1.6B to build its own advertising business.

companies.o: UT Austin spinout building the Apollo general-purpose humanoid
companies.story: Apptronik spun out of UT Austin's Human Centered Robotics Lab in 2016 and spent years on contract work, including NASA's Valkyrie, before launching the Apollo humanoid in 2023. It raised a $350M Series A in February 2025 (extended to $403M) with Google participating, then a $520M extension in February 2026 that valued it at more than $5.5B, about triple a year earlier, bringing total funding to nearly $1B.

companies.o: Self-driving technology company backed by Ford and Volkswagen
companies.story: Argo got a $1B commitment from Ford in 2017 and $2.6B in cash and assets from Volkswagen, reaching a reported $7.25B valuation. When it failed to attract outside investors and Ford decided fully driverless cars were too far off to pay back, both backers pulled out and Argo shut down in October 2022; Ford took a $2.7B write-down.

companies.o: AI tutoring platform for Indian school students
companies.story: Arivihan raised a $10.2M Series A co-led by Accel and Prosus Ventures, reported in September 2026. Funds go to expansion beyond its current states and into CBSE.

companies.o: Electric vans and buses built in low-cost 'microfactories'
companies.story: Arrival listed via SPAC in 2021 and briefly hit a ~$13B market value on a UPS order and its microfactory concept, without having produced vehicles at scale. Production targets slipped repeatedly, cash ran out, its UK units entered administration in 2024 and assets were sold off.

companies.o: AI employee 'Ava' for outbound sales, famous for the 'stop hiring humans' campaign
companies.story: Artisan raised a $25M Series A in April 2025 led by Glade Brook Capital, bringing total funding above $35M. Secondary sites report a LinkedIn ban over scraped data in late 2025 or early 2026, later reportedly reversed, which is unconfirmed.

companies.o: Building giant satellites that connect directly to ordinary unmodified smartphones (space-based cellular broadband).
companies.story: Abel Avellan founded AST in 2017 to beam broadband from huge phased-array satellites straight to normal phones, an idea many in the industry doubted, and it listed via a SPAC in 2021. After its BlueWalker 3 prototype in 2022, its shares sank in early 2024 amid funding worries until AT&T, Google and Vodafone invested; the first five BlueBird satellites launched in September 2024 and the stock became one of the biggest space winners as direct-to-cell rivals such as Starlink and Lynk raced in.

near.what: Shares fell sharply on cash worries before strategic investment from AT&T, Google and Vodafone

companies.o: Aimed to build cheap, mass-produced small rockets for daily launches to orbit.
companies.story: Astra promised low-cost rockets built like consumer products to enable daily launch, and in July 2021 became the first space launch company listed on Nasdaq via a SPAC merger with Craig McCaw's Holicity at a $2.1B deal valuation, with market value peaking near $3.9B (Bloomberg). Its small rocket reached orbit only twice amid repeated failures, and launches were paused after a June 2022 failure. In 2024 co-founders Chris Kemp and Adam London took it private for $0.50 per share, cut from a $1.50 proposal, when the board said the alternative was Chapter 7; market value had fallen to roughly $12M.

near.what: June 2022 launch failure (lost NASA TROPICS satellites) after earlier failures; rocket launches put on hiatus
Board special committee said the $0.50/share founder buyout was the only alternative to Chapter 7 bankruptcy; deal closed July 2024

dismissed.quote_or_fact: Paraphrase: TechCrunch labelled Astra's March 2024 take-private the space industry's first SPAC bust of 2024.

companies.o: Space debris removal and satellite servicing company that inspected a spent rocket stage up close in orbit.
companies.story: Nobu Okada founded Astroscale in 2013 to clean up orbital debris, a market with no paying customer at the time; it built government demand in Japan, the UK and US and in 2024 its ADRAS-J craft approached a discarded Japanese rocket stage. It listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Growth market in June 2024, closing its first day at about 155B yen ($1B), and later traded below that (about $935M in August 2026).

companies.o: Premium connected electric scooter maker with its own fast-charging grid
companies.story: IIT Madras graduates Tarun Mehta and Swapnil Jain founded Ather in 2013 and spent years engineering a premium connected scooter and charging grid, backed by Hero MotoCorp. It listed in May 2025 with a Rs 2,981 crore IPO (~$345M at 86.5) priced at Rs 321, the first Indian EV-maker listing after Ola Electric, and gained share as Ola's service problems mounted.

companies.o: Tech-enabled law firm for startups from Twitch co-founder Justin Kan
companies.story: Justin Kan's Atrium paired an in-house law firm with software to make startup legal work cheaper and faster, raising $75.5M. Legal work proved hard to automate, it laid off its lawyers in early 2020 to pivot to advisory services, and shut down weeks later.

companies.o: Self-driving software company focused on long-haul trucks
companies.story: Founded by veterans of Google's, Tesla's and Uber's self-driving efforts, Aurora absorbed Uber's autonomy unit in 2020 and went public via SPAC in 2021 at about $11B. It focused on highway trucking rather than city robotaxis and began driverless commercial runs in Texas in 2025, while Argo shut down and GM closed Cruise.

companies.o: Used-car wholesale marketplace for dealers, later adding online retail (Autohero)
companies.story: Auto1 bought cars from consumers and resold them to dealers across Europe within days, avoiding long inventory risk, before launching consumer site Autohero. It listed in Frankfurt in February 2021 at about €8.3B (~$9.8B) and survived the used-car downturn that killed Cazoo and Vroom.

companies.o: Freemium consumer antivirus software
companies.story: Avast gave antivirus away free to hundreds of millions of users and sold premium upgrades, listing in London in 2018. NortonLifeLock bought it in 2022 for about $8.6B, after a 2020 scandal over its Jumpshot unit selling browsing data.

companies.o: Flexible workspace operator using landlord revenue-share partnerships to grow capital-light
companies.story: Amit Ramani's Awfis built Indian coworking largely through managed-aggregation deals in which landlords fund fit-outs and share revenue, rather than WeWork-style long leases it paid for itself. While WeWork filed for US bankruptcy in 2023, Awfis listed in May 2024 with a Rs 599 crore IPO (~$72M at 83.7) at Rs 383 and opened about 13% higher.

companies.o: Flies private astronaut missions to the ISS and is building a commercial space station to replace it.
companies.story: Axiom flew four private crews to the ISS from 2022 to 2025 (Ax-4 carried astronauts from India, Poland and Hungary) and holds NASA contracts for an ISS-attached module and Artemis moonwalk suits. In 2024 it was reported to be missing supplier payments, laying off staff and cutting pay, and it went through three CEOs in about a year; it pushed its free-flying station to 2028 or later and closed a round of more than $525M in June 2026, with secondary-market valuations around $2-2.5B.

near.what: Reported missed supplier payments, layoffs and pay cuts; CEO Michael Suffredini stepped down

companies.o: AI symptom checker and video-GP service that ran NHS practices and US value-based care
companies.story: Babylon raised a record $550M in 2019 and went public via SPAC in 2021 at about $4.2B, promising AI-driven primary care. Losses from taking on full risk for US patients under value-based contracts ballooned while its AI claims drew scrutiny; in 2023 its US arm went bankrupt and the UK business was sold for a nominal sum.

companies.o: Production inference platform for AI models
companies.story: Baseten climbed from a $200M valuation in 2024 to $2.15B in September 2025 and $5B in January 2026, with a $1.5B Series F reported in June 2026. Sacra puts the latest valuation near $13B.

companies.o: AI agents that automate accounting work for accounting firms
companies.story: Basis raised a $34M Series A led by Khosla in December 2024 and a $100M Series B at $1.15B in February 2026 led by Accel. Its agents plug into ledgers such as QuickBooks and Xero.

companies.o: $50 AI wristband that transcribes everything you say
companies.story: Amazon announced it would acquire Bee in July 2025, with terms undisclosed and a team reported at only 2 to 10 people. Coverage raised privacy concerns because the device records conversations.

companies.o: Peer-to-peer online marketplace for inspected used cars
companies.story: Beepi inspected private sellers' cars and sold them online, raising about $150M at a peak valuation near $560M. Spending stayed high, sales to Fair.com and dealer group DGDG both collapsed, and it shut down in February 2017 with its parts sold to repay creditors.

companies.o: Online bookkeeping and tax service for small businesses that shut down abruptly in late 2024
companies.story: Bench shut down on Dec 27, 2024 and locked customers out just before tax season, then was acquired by self-funded Employer.com three days later on undisclosed terms. Customers later complained about data-handoff consent and Employer.com's lack of accounting expertise.

companies.o: UK AI drug discovery company that shrank and went private
companies.story: BenevolentAI cut about 180 staff in 2023 after a mid-phase flop, cut 30% more in 2024, and merged into Osaka Holdings to delist from Euronext Amsterdam in March 2025. Runway was projected into 2027.

companies.o: AI robotic picking and sorting systems that went public via SPAC and were taken private by SoftBank
companies.story: Founded by roboticist Tom Wagner, Berkshire Grey sold large robotic picking and sorting systems to retailers and parcel carriers and went public in July 2021 via a SPAC at about $2.7B. Lumpy system sales, heavy losses and the SPAC crash drove the stock under $1, and in 2023 its largest shareholder SoftBank took it private at $1.40 a share, roughly $375M, about 85% below the listing value.

near.what: Shares fell below $1 after SPAC listing; heavy losses and lumpy orders

companies.o: EV charging and battery-swap network that leased batteries to drivers of swappable electric cars.
companies.story: Founded by ex-SAP executive Shai Agassi, Better Place was formally US-based but ran its main operations in Israel, aiming to make EVs cheaper than gasoline cars by owning the batteries and swapping them in minutes at robotic stations; it raised roughly $850M from investors including Israel Corp., HSBC, Morgan Stanley, GE and UBS, peaking at a $2.25B post-money private valuation in its 2011 Series C. Only one car, the Renault Fluence Z.E., ever supported its swap system and other automakers such as Tesla saw no reason to build swappable packs, so after Agassi was ousted in late 2012 the company filed for bankruptcy in Israel on 26 May 2013 and receivers sold the remaining assets in November 2013 for about $450,000.

near.what: Founder-CEO Shai Agassi was ousted about seven months before the bankruptcy as Renault Fluence sales in Israel fell far short of plan.

dismissed.quote_or_fact: Paraphrase: most EV makers, Tesla included, saw no reason to build or install swappable batteries, leaving Better Place dependent on a single Renault model.

companies.o: Plant-based burgers and sausages sold in grocery stores and restaurants
companies.story: Beyond Meat placed plant-based burgers in the grocery meat aisle and raised $240M in a May 2019 IPO that jumped 163% on day one, one of the best debuts in years. Demand faded in later years and the stock fell far below its IPO price.

companies.o: mRNA immunotherapy company that co-developed the first approved COVID-19 vaccine
companies.story: Uğur Şahin and Özlem Türeci spent a decade on mRNA cancer therapies, backed by the Strüngmann family office, and listed on Nasdaq in October 2019 at about $3.4B. Partnering with Pfizer in 2020 it delivered the first approved COVID-19 vaccine and its market value briefly topped $100B in 2021; it later bought InstaDeep.

companies.o: Dockless shared electric scooters rented by app
companies.story: Bird became one of the fastest startups ever to reach a $1B valuation by dropping scooters on city sidewalks, reaching a $2.5B valuation in 2019. Scooters wore out fast and cities capped fleets; after a 2021 SPAC listing it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 2023 to sell itself.

companies.o: Retail platform for buying crypto, stocks and metals under EU licences
companies.story: Bitpanda was profitable early and collected EU financial licences before most crypto rivals, helping it survive the 2022 crash. A Valar-led $263M round in 2021 valued it at $4.1B.

companies.o: One of the oldest licensed bitcoin exchanges, started in Slovenia
companies.story: Two Slovenians founded Bitstamp in 2011 as a European alternative to Mt. Gox and it survived a 2015 hack and several crypto crashes by securing licences early. Korean group NXC bought it in 2018 and Robinhood acquired it for about $200M, closing in 2025.

companies.o: Long-distance carpooling marketplace matching drivers with passengers sharing costs

rounds.lead: Insight Venture Partners, Lead Edge Capital

companies.story: BlaBlaCar spent years before finding a business model (booking fees), then grew across Europe, Russia, India and Latin America, buying German rival Carpooling.com in 2015. A $200M round in 2015 valued it at $1.6B, and it later added buses (OuiBus, Busfor). In the US, long-distance carpooling startup Zimride never scaled and its team pivoted to Lyft.

companies.o: Maker of the FLUX image generation models
companies.story: Black Forest Labs raised a $300M Series B at $3.25B post-money in December 2025. The press release names AMP and Salesforce Ventures as leads, while one data site lists Creandum.

companies.o: Runs a constellation of small high-revisit imaging satellites plus AI analytics sold mainly to defense and intelligence agencies.
companies.story: BlackSky went public through a merger with Osprey Technology Acquisition Corp in 2021 and sold rapid-revisit imagery and AI-based monitoring mostly to the US government and allies. Like other 2021 space SPACs its shares fell heavily, and it bet on a third-generation satellite fleet starting in 2025 to win larger defense contracts.

companies.o: Grocery marketplace that pivoted to 10-minute delivery from dark stores
companies.story: Grofers spent years as a slow, cash-burning grocery marketplace (valued at just $300M in 2018) before rebranding as Blinkit in late 2021 and pivoting to 10-minute delivery from dark stores. Zomato, already a ~9% holder, bought it in an all-stock deal for Rs 4,447 crore (~$568M) in 2022, below its $1B 2021 valuation because Zomato's own shares had fallen. Under Zomato, quick commerce became the group's main growth engine.

companies.o: Augmented-reality app letting brands make products and ads interactive
companies.story: Blippar was valued around $1.5B in 2016, one of the UK's first unicorns, selling AR campaigns to brands and pivoting toward visual search. Revenue stayed small, a shareholder dispute blocked new funding and it went into administration in December 2018.

companies.o: Crypto lender offering interest accounts and loans backed by bitcoin
companies.story: BlockFi paid interest on crypto deposits and reached a $3B valuation in 2021, then paid $100M in early 2022 to settle SEC and state charges over its interest product. After losses tied to Three Arrows Capital it took a rescue credit line from FTX, and when FTX collapsed in November 2022 BlockFi filed for bankruptcy within weeks.

companies.o: Subscription meal kits with recipes and pre-portioned ingredients
companies.story: Blue Apron led the US meal-kit boom and was valued at about $2B privately, but went public in 2017 at a cut price the week Amazon agreed to buy Whole Foods. High customer churn and marketing costs left it losing money, and Wonder Group bought it for $103M in 2023, while Germany's HelloFresh became the global leader.

companies.o: China's third-largest dockless bike-sharing service
companies.story: Bluegogo put about 700,000 bikes on Chinese streets and planned a Seattle launch, but burned through roughly 600M yuan (~$119M at 2017 rates) and ceased operations in November 2017, the first major casualty of the bike-sharing bubble. Users struggled to recover deposits; Green Bike-Transit took over operations and Didi absorbed some assets and staff. Reported funding differs ($90M per TechCrunch, $58M per Bloomberg).

companies.o: All-electric ride-hailing service owning its fleet and charging superhubs
companies.story: BluSmart ran an all-EV cab service in Delhi NCR and Bengaluru, with cars leased largely from its promoters' listed firm Gensol Engineering, and raised about $180M in equity and debt from bp ventures and others. In April 2025 SEBI found the Jaggi brothers had diverted loan money meant for EVs (Gensol bought only 4,704 of the 6,400 cars it borrowed Rs 978 crore for) into personal luxuries, barred them from markets, and BluSmart halted bookings almost overnight. Its asset-light app sat on top of a fleet it did not control, so the promoter fraud took the operator down with it.

companies.o: AI-powered construction takeoffs and estimating
companies.story: Bobyard raised a $35M Series A led by 8VC, reported December 11, 2025. It automates construction takeoffs for contractors.

companies.o: Lower-cost ride-hailing, scooter and delivery super-app (formerly Taxify)
companies.story: Founded by teenager Markus Villig as Taxify, it undercut Uber's commissions in Eastern Europe and Africa. Its 2017 London launch was shut down by the regulator within days for lacking a licence, but it relaunched in 2019 and raised €628M in 2022 at €7.4B (~$7.8B).

companies.o: Dot-com era online fashion store with 3D product views in 18 countries
companies.story: Swedish founders raised about $135M from backers including JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs and Bernard Arnault and launched simultaneously in many countries with a heavy, slow website when most users were on dial-up. It burned through the money in about six months and was liquidated in May 2000; online fashion later worked for Zalando and ASOS once broadband and logistics existed.

companies.o: Online hotel booking site charging hotels commission (agency model)
companies.story: Started as Bookings.nl in Amsterdam, it let independent European hotels pay commission only on stays rather than pre-buying rooms. Priceline bought it in 2005 for $133M, and it became the core of what is now Booking Holdings, worth well over $100B.

companies.o: Indoor vertical farms growing greens near cities
companies.story: Bowery grew lettuce in automated indoor farms near East Coast cities, reaching a $2.3B valuation in 2021. Energy costs made its greens expensive to produce, crop problems hit its farms, and it shut down in November 2024.

companies.o: Observability and evaluation layer for AI apps
companies.story: Braintrust raised an $80M Series B in February 2026 to become the observability layer for AI. Lead was not in the snippet.

companies.o: Online store selling unbranded household goods at $3 each
companies.story: Brandless launched in 2017 selling food and household items for $3 each without brand names, and took $240M from SoftBank's Vision Fund in 2018. Low prices on small orders left little margin after shipping, leadership churned, and it shut down in early 2020.

companies.o: Software-defined robotic assembly cells for electronics such as AI servers
companies.story: Bright Machines spun out of contract manufacturer Flex's automation group in 2018 with $179M to replace hand-built assembly lines with software-controlled robotic 'microfactories'. A 2021 SPAC merger with SCVX was called off in 2022 as the SPAC market collapsed; it regrouped around assembling AI servers and raised a $126M Series C (about $106M equity) in June 2024 with Nvidia and Microsoft, bringing total funding to around $400M.

near.what: SPAC merger with SCVX terminated after the SPAC market collapsed

companies.o: AI weather forecasting from ex-Google X founders
companies.story: Brightband raised a $10M Series A led by Prelude Ventures, reported September 2024.

companies.o: Startup planning a £3.8B EV battery gigafactory in northern England
companies.story: Britishvolt promised a £3.8B gigafactory at Blyth with government support but had no proven cell technology or anchor customer. It failed to raise funding as markets turned and entered administration in January 2023; Australia's Recharge Industries bought the remains for about £8.6M.

companies.o: 'AI-powered' platform promising to assemble custom apps like ordering a pizza
companies.story: Builder.ai raised over $450M, including from Microsoft and Qatar's sovereign fund, marketing AI that would build software while relying heavily on human developers. In 2025 reports that it had overstated sales led a lender to seize cash, and it filed for insolvency in May 2025.

companies.o: Cheap, simple green-energy supplier for UK households
companies.story: Bulb grew to about 1.7M customers by undercutting incumbents, but it had not hedged wholesale energy and the UK price cap stopped it passing on costs. When gas prices spiked in 2021 it collapsed into special administration, the largest UK state rescue since RBS, and its customers were transferred to Octopus Energy in 2022.

companies.o: Language-learning app with native-speaker community feedback
companies.story: Busuu was founded in Madrid in 2008 by Bernhard Niesner and Adrian Hilti and moved to London, growing a freemium language app where native speakers correct learners. Chegg bought it in 2021 for $436M, while US rival Duolingo went public the same year.

companies.o: Phone-battery maker that turned itself into the world's largest electric-vehicle maker.
companies.story: Wang Chuanfu founded Shenzhen BYD Battery Co. in February 1995 with CN¥2.5M to make nickel-cadmium batteries, listed in Hong Kong in July 2002 (raising about HK$1.6B, ~$205M at the HKD peg) and then moved into cars, which Elon Musk openly laughed off in a 2011 Bloomberg TV interview. Berkshire Hathaway, via MidAmerican Energy, bought about 10% in September 2008 for roughly $230M; by late 2023 BYD had taken Tesla's EV sales crown and its 2024 revenue passed $100B. Peak valuation here is the record A-share market cap of about CN¥1.22T on 21 May 2025 (~$169B at ~7.2 CNY/USD); a 2025 Hong Kong placement raised $5.59B.

dismissed.who: Elon Musk (Tesla CEO), Bloomberg TV interview, 2011
dismissed.quote_or_fact: "Have you seen their car?" (laughing, when asked whether BYD was a threat to Tesla)

companies.o: K-12 and test-prep learning app with video lessons, sold on financed tablets by a large field sales force
companies.story: Byju's became India's most valuable startup at $22B in 2022 after raising roughly $5.5B and spending billions on acquisitions (Aakash, WhiteHat Jr, Great Learning, Epic) during the pandemic edtech boom. As schools reopened demand fell, audits were delayed, it defaulted on a $1.2B US term loan and Prosus marked it to $5.1B in 2023; a 2024 rights issue was priced at about $220-250M. Lenders pushed its US unit into Chapter 11 and the parent into Indian insolvency in 2024, and the founder said it was 'worth zero'.

companies.o: Ride-hailing app using licensed private-hire drivers in Spain and Latin America
companies.story: Cabify launched in Madrid in 2011 using licensed VTC drivers and expanded early into Latin America, absorbing Easy Taxi in 2017. When Uber was banned from Spain in 2014 Cabify kept growing, and a Rakuten-led $160M round in 2018 made it Spain's first unicorn.

companies.o: EV startup building pod-shaped vans on a 'skateboard' platform
companies.story: Canoo went public via SPAC in December 2020 promising subscription EVs on a modular platform, then churned through strategies and executives without reaching volume production. It filed for Chapter 7 liquidation in January 2025.

companies.o: Browser-based drag-and-drop design platform that makes graphic design easy for non-designers.
companies.story: Melanie Perkins, Cliff Obrecht and Cameron Adams launched Canva in Australia in 2012 out of Perkins and Obrecht's Perth yearbook-design business Fusion Books; Perkins was rejected by about 100 VCs, wary of a design startup from Perth taking on Adobe, and it took roughly three years to land the first investment, a $3.6M seed in 2013 (Matrix Partners, InterWest, 500 Startups; reported figure, currency not confirmed). Canva hit $40B in a $200M September 2021 round and $42B in an August 2025 employee share sale (peak_valuation_usd, private; a SmartCompany claim of a $65B peak could not be verified), before investors Blackbird and Airtree marked it down to about $34.9B in August 2026, with an IPO targeted for 2027. Total raised is unresolved: trackers range from $597M (Multiples.vc) to $979M (CB Insights).

dismissed.quote_or_fact: Fact: Perkins was rejected by roughly 100 VCs and took about three years to land Canva's first investment.

companies.o: US synthetic-aperture radar satellite operator, bought by quantum-computing company IonQ.
companies.story: Payam Banazadeh founded Capella in 2016 to build high-resolution commercial radar satellites for US defense and commercial customers. IonQ agreed in May 2025 to buy it in a mostly-stock deal valued at about $318M at signing to build space-based quantum networking; by the July 2025 close IonQ's rising share price lifted the consideration to about $424.8M ($48.3M cash plus $376.5M stock).

companies.o: B2B e-commerce supplying Egyptian corner shops with groceries and goods
companies.story: Capiter raised a $33M Series A in 2021 to digitise ordering for Egypt's informal retailers and expanded into Saudi Arabia. In September 2022 the board fired the founder brothers amid financial-mismanagement allegations (denied and never proven in court), leaving the company in arrears to staff and creditors.

companies.o: Middle East ride-hailing app built for local payment and safety norms
companies.story: Careem started as a corporate car booking service and adapted ride-hailing to the region with cash payments and local drivers, beating Uber in many Middle Eastern and Pakistani cities. Uber bought it for $3.1B ($1.7B in convertible notes and $1.4B cash), closing in January 2020, the region's largest tech deal at the time.

companies.o: State-space-model lab from Stanford whose first product is ultra-low-latency voice AI
companies.story: Founded by the Stanford researchers behind state-space models (including Albert Gu and Karan Goel), Cartesia bets on SSMs as a more efficient alternative to Transformers. It monetised first through Sonic, a fast text-to-speech model sold to voice-agent builders, and had raised about $191M by October 2025. No valuation has been disclosed.

companies.o: Ex-Google team's sidewalk robots that moved from food delivery to factory and lab campuses
companies.story: Former Google engineers founded Cartken to build sidewalk delivery robots, running campus food deliveries with Grubhub and pilots with DPD and Mitsubishi in Japan. Finding consumer food delivery hard to make pay, it shifted toward moving materials around factory and biotech campuses, a niche TechCrunch summarised as going 'from burritos to biotech'.

companies.o: Buy a used car online and pick it up from a car vending machine
companies.story: Spun out of used-car dealer DriveTime, Carvana owned and reconditioned its inventory rather than matching private sellers like Beepi, and it went public in 2017 raising $225M. It nearly collapsed under debt in 2022, then cut costs and recovered.

companies.o: AI-powered loan origination platform for lenders
companies.story: Casca raised a $29M Series A led by Canapi Ventures in August 2025, bringing total funding to $33M. It builds AI loan origination for lenders.

companies.o: AI legal research and the CoCounsel lawyer assistant
companies.story: Casetext spent a decade building legal research tools, then used early access to GPT-4 to launch CoCounsel, an AI legal assistant, in 2023. Months later Thomson Reuters bought it for $650M in cash.

companies.o: Direct-to-consumer mattress shipped in a box
companies.story: Casper popularized mattresses shipped compressed in a box and hit a $1.1B private valuation in 2019, but dozens of copycats drove up ad costs. Its February 2020 IPO priced at about half that valuation, and it was taken private in early 2022 for about $300M.

companies.o: Spin-off of a phone-battery maker that became the world's biggest EV battery supplier.
companies.story: Robin Zeng's team set up CATL in Ningde, Fujian in December 2011 with RMB1M of registered capital, spinning out the EV-battery business of his consumer-battery maker ATL in response to Chinese policy changes, a bet that a provincial newcomer could become the core supplier for a car industry that barely existed yet. It listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in June 2018 (code 300750), raising about CN¥5.46B (~$850M), and its market cap passed CN¥1T by 2021; a February 2026 snapshot valued it at about $240.7B. Peak market cap was not verified in this session, so peak_valuation_usd is left null.

companies.o: Buy a used car fully online and get it delivered to your door
companies.story: Zoopla founder Alex Chesterman launched Cazoo in 2019 as a UK Carvana and listed via SPAC in 2021 at about $7B, then expanded into five EU countries. Holding thousands of cars, heavy marketing and rising rates produced huge losses; it retreated from Europe in 2022, its shares fell over 99% and it entered administration in 2024.

companies.o: Crypto lending platform paying high yields on customer deposits
companies.story: Celsius promised retail customers high double-digit yields on crypto deposits and lent and traded the funds in risky strategies. When crypto prices crashed it froze withdrawals in June 2022 and filed for Chapter 11 a month later; founder Alex Mashinsky pleaded guilty to fraud and was sentenced to 12 years in prison in 2025.

companies.o: Wafer-scale AI processors and inference cloud
companies.story: Cerebras raised a $1.1B Series G led by Fidelity and Atreides, with Tiger Global and Valor participating. It leads the AI chip startup funding tables.

companies.o: Foundation models for de novo molecule and antibody design
companies.story: Chai raised a $70M Series A led by Menlo Ventures in August 2025 and a $130M Series B at $1.3B in December 2025 co-led by Oak HC/FT and General Catalyst. Total financing is about $225M per Bloomberg.

companies.o: Defense sensing and radar company
companies.story: Chaos raised a $275M Series C in 2025 led by NEA and Accel, then a $510M Series D led by Valor Equity Partners.

companies.o: Chatbots that role-play as celebrities, fictional characters and companions
companies.story: Ex-Google researchers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas built Character.AI into one of the most-used consumer AI apps and raised $150M at a $1B valuation in 2023. In August 2024 Google paid a reported $2.7B, mostly as a non-exclusive license fee, and rehired the founders into DeepMind, while the remaining company kept running the app.

companies.o: Online pet food and supply retailer known for customer service
companies.story: Chewy sold the same heavy pet food that sank Pets.com, but a decade later with cheaper shipping, repeat 'Autoship' subscriptions and obsessive customer service. PetSmart bought it for $3.35B in 2017, then the largest e-commerce acquisition ever, and Chewy went public in 2019.

companies.o: Fee-free mobile bank account with early paycheck access
companies.story: Chime offered no-fee checking and early direct-deposit access through partner banks, earning mostly from card interchange fees. It hit a $25B private valuation in 2021 and went public in June 2025 at $27 a share, well below that private peak.

companies.o: Public-transport journey planner app for big cities
companies.story: Citymapper became a favourite transit app in London and dozens of cities but struggled to monetise, trying its own bus routes and a travel pass. It was acquired by Via in 2023 for an undisclosed sum, while rivals Waze and Moovit had sold to Google and Intel for about $1B each.

companies.o: Remotely supervised sidewalk robots delivering restaurant orders in dense city neighbourhoods
companies.story: UCLA students Zach Rash and Brad Squicciarini started Coco by having remote human pilots drive its sidewalk robots, adding autonomy gradually rather than waiting for full self-driving. It raised a $36M Series A in 2021 and an $80M round in June 2025 backed by Sam Altman and others, taking total funding past $120M, and operates in Los Angeles, Chicago, Miami and Helsinki.

companies.o: YC-backed AI tool for generating code
companies.story: CodeParrot raised $500K in seed funding but reached only about $1,500 in MRR after its final pivot. In July 2025 the founders shut down rather than continue with limited runway.

companies.o: AI code review platform
companies.story: CodeRabbit raised $143M at a $1.5B valuation as AI-generated code volume grew. One source says Atomico and Smash Capital led; reports date the round to 2026.

companies.o: Enterprise-focused large language models
companies.story: Co-founded by Aidan Gomez, a co-author of the Transformer paper, Cohere sold models to enterprises that wanted private deployments rather than chasing consumers. Unlike Inflection and Adept, it kept raising independently, reaching a $6.8B valuation in 2025.

companies.o: Regulated US exchange for buying and holding crypto
companies.story: Coinbase, a Y Combinator company, made buying bitcoin simple and chose to work within US regulation while rival exchanges cut corners. It survived several crypto crashes and went public by direct listing in April 2021, closing its first day at a valuation of about $86B.

companies.o: Proximity-based photo-sharing app that raised $41M before launch
companies.story: Color raised $41M before launching an app that showed photos from strangers nearby, one of the largest pre-launch raises of its era. Users found the app confusing and empty, a pivot failed, and Apple hired much of the team in 2012 while the app shut down.

companies.o: MIT spinout building compact tokamak fusion reactors using high-temperature superconducting magnets.
companies.story: CFS spun out of MIT in 2018 and in 2021 demonstrated a 20-tesla high-temperature superconducting magnet, then raised $1.8B, the largest private fusion round at the time. It added $863M in 2025 and about $1B more in July 2026 (roughly $4B in total; one profile cites a larger 2026 figure that could not be reconciled), signed power deals with Google and Eni for its planned ARC plant in Virginia, and targets net energy from its SPARC device in 2027.

companies.o: Vehicle telematics and navigation company on Germany's Neuer Markt
companies.story: ComROAD was a Neuer Markt star after its 1999 IPO, reporting fast-growing sales of traffic-telematics systems. In 2002 it emerged that about 97% of its revenue came from a fictitious Hong Kong customer; the CEO was convicted and the company collapsed.

companies.o: Tool that coordinates work across competing AI coding agents
companies.story: Meta acquired Conductor in November 2026, gaining its multi-agent coding orchestration technology. The local version keeps getting updates until early 2027, then begins winding down.

companies.o: GV-backed LLM evaluation platform
companies.story: In April 2025 OpenAI hired the Context.ai co-founders, and the company planned to wind down its products. Deal terms were not disclosed.

companies.o: Enterprise language-model and RAG company
companies.story: In May 2026 Google DeepMind agreed to hire 20+ Contextual AI researchers and license its technology for a reported roughly $100M. It follows the reverse-acquihire template used for Inflection and Character.AI.

companies.o: Open-source AI coding assistant with 34K GitHub stars
companies.story: Cursor quietly acqui-hired Continue in June 2026, shutting the product's hosted Hub on July 15, 2026 (the extension code stays Apache 2.0). Terms were not disclosed in the results seen.

companies.o: Digital freight brokerage matching shippers with truckers by app
companies.story: Convoy used software to match shippers and truckers, backed by investors including Jeff Bezos, and raised $260M at a $3.8B valuation in April 2022. A freight recession crushed brokerage margins and capital dried up; it shut down in October 2023, and Flexport bought its technology but not its liabilities.

companies.o: Agent-based e-commerce for rural and middle-income African consumers
companies.story: Copia sold groceries and household goods to rural Kenyans through a network of local agents and raised over $100M, including a $50M Series C in 2022. It exited Uganda in April 2023 cutting 350+ jobs, then Copia Global filed for administration in 2024 when it could not raise on acceptable terms.

companies.o: Generative AI platform for sales and marketing workflows
companies.story: Fullcast acquired Copy.ai on October 15, 2025 per Dealroom, which lists about $28M raised and roughly $23.7M ARR (CB Insights shows $19.82M raised). Price was not disclosed, so whether it sold below capital raised is unknown.

companies.o: AI-driven care platform for payers, employers and consumers
companies.story: Counsel raised a $25M Series A in October 2025 led by Andreessen Horowitz and GV and launched a consumer chatbot.

companies.o: AI foundation models for warehouse picking robots
companies.story: Founded by Berkeley robotics researchers Pieter Abbeel, Peter Chen and Rocky Duan, Covariant built AI that let warehouse robots pick unfamiliar items, last valued at a reported $625M. In August 2024 Amazon hired its three founders and about a quarter of staff and licensed its models, with terms undisclosed.

companies.o: End-to-end AI ad agent that creates video ads
companies.story: Creatify raised a $15.5M Series A in May 2025 co-led by WndrCo and Kindred Ventures after crossing $9M ARR, bringing total funding to $23M. Its AdMax product automates the ad creation lifecycle.

companies.o: Ad retargeting platform showing shoppers products they viewed
companies.story: Criteo pivoted from movie recommendations to retargeting ads paid per click and listed on Nasdaq in 2013, raising about $250M at roughly $1.7B. It later suffered as Apple and Google restricted third-party cookies and tracking.

companies.o: Cloud-native endpoint security platform
companies.story: CrowdStrike delivered endpoint protection from the cloud while incumbents sold on-premise antivirus, and gained fame investigating high-profile breaches. Its June 2019 IPO raised $612M at about $6.7B and it grew into one of the largest security companies.

companies.o: Self-driving robotaxi startup bought by General Motors
companies.story: Y Combinator company Cruise started with highway autopilot kits and was bought by GM in 2016 in a deal reported at around $1B, a great outcome for its founders. Under GM it launched driverless robotaxis in San Francisco, but after a 2023 crash in which a car dragged a pedestrian, its permit was suspended and GM shut the robotaxi program in December 2024.

companies.o: Energy-first AI data center and GPU cloud builder
companies.story: Crusoe built the Stargate campus in Abilene and was valued above $10B by October 2025 after a $600M Series D in December 2024. It later sold an unfinished Wyoming data center project to Google.

companies.o: At-home molecular COVID-19 test reader
companies.story: Cue Health's home molecular COVID test sold heavily during the pandemic and it went public in 2021. When COVID testing demand collapsed and the FDA issued a warning letter about its test, it could not replace the revenue and shut down in 2024.

companies.o: In-memory compute inference accelerator
companies.story: d-Matrix raised a $110M Series B led by Temasek with Microsoft, then a $275M Series C led by BullhoundCapital, Triatomic and Temasek. It targets low-latency inference.

companies.o: Self-learning AI that detects cyber threats inside company networks
companies.story: Darktrace sold AI anomaly detection to enterprises and listed in London in April 2021 at about £1.7B (~$2.3B). Despite short-seller criticism of its accounting, Thoma Bravo took it private in 2024 for about $5.3B.

companies.o: Pan-African wallet linking mobile money and bank accounts across countries
companies.story: Dash pitched itself as the 'Alipay for Africa' and reportedly raised $86.1M in five years (TechCrunch counted ~$50M including $20M venture debt), claiming $1B in transactions. The Bank of Ghana flagged it in 2022 for operating without approval; the founder was suspended in 2023 over alleged financial impropriety (allegations, not court findings) and the company shut in October 2023.

companies.o: German marketplace for handmade and craft goods
companies.story: DaWanda launched a year after Etsy and became the leading handmade marketplace in German-speaking Europe. As Etsy localised and grew its global network of buyers, DaWanda's growth stalled; it closed in August 2018 and pointed its sellers to Etsy.

companies.o: AI agents that automate enterprise customer service conversations
companies.story: Decagon raised a $35M Series A in 2024, a $131M Series C at $1.5B in June 2025 (a16z and Accel reported leading), and $250M at $4.5B in January 2026. Valuation tripled in about seven months.

companies.o: AI research lab building general-purpose learning algorithms
companies.story: Demis Hassabis, Shane Legg and Mustafa Suleyman founded DeepMind in London with early backers including Peter Thiel and Elon Musk. Google bought it in January 2014 for a reported ~£400M (~$500M+); it went on to build AlphaGo and AlphaFold, which won a Nobel Prize in 2024.

companies.o: Quant-fund-backed Chinese lab whose cheap open-weight R1 model shook global markets
companies.story: Spun out of the High-Flyer quant fund by Liang Wenfeng in 2023 and funded entirely by it, DeepSeek claimed a roughly $5.6M final training run for V3; its R1 reasoning model in January 2025 helped wipe about $589B off Nvidia's market value in a day. It shipped V4 in April 2026 and took its first outside money in June 2026, about $7.4B at a valuation above $50B, routed through a partnership controlled by Liang. A further ~$16B round and a STAR-market IPO were reported later in 2026 but are unconfirmed.

companies.o: AI for military logistics
companies.story: DEFCON AI raised a $44M seed in August 2024 for military logistics.

companies.o: Tech-led express parcel and supply-chain network built for Indian e-commerce
companies.story: Delhivery began in 2011 delivering restaurant food in Gurugram, then pivoted to parcel logistics for e-commerce sellers and built one of India's largest express networks with SoftBank's 2019 backing. It listed in May 2022 in a weak market with a Rs 5,235 crore IPO (~$666M at 78.6) priced at Rs 487 and closed day one roughly 10% higher.

companies.o: Restaurant food delivery app using self-employed riders
companies.story: Deliveroo won the UK and several cities by signing restaurants others did not deliver for, but exited Germany (2019), Spain (2021), the Netherlands and Australia (2022) where local leaders were entrenched. It IPO'd in 2021 at £7.6B (~$10.5B), traded far below that, and DoorDash bought it in 2025 for £2.9B (~$3.9B).

companies.o: Deliveroo's restaurant delivery operation in Germany
companies.story: Deliveroo launched in Berlin in 2015 but Germany consolidated into one dominant player when Takeaway.com bought Delivery Hero's German brands (Lieferheld, Pizza.de, Foodora) in 2018. With Lieferando owning the market, Deliveroo pulled out of Germany in August 2019.

companies.o: Deliveroo's restaurant delivery operation in Spain
companies.story: Deliveroo entered Spain in 2015 but stayed a distant player behind homegrown Glovo and Just Eat. When Spain's 2021 'Ley Rider' required riders to be employees, Deliveroo decided it could not reach scale and left the country in November 2021, while Glovo stayed and fought.

companies.o: Global food-delivery group built by buying local leaders in 70+ countries
companies.story: Delivery Hero grew by acquisition: Yemeksepeti (Turkey, $589M), Talabat (Gulf), Woowa (Korea) and a majority of Glovo (Spain). It listed in Frankfurt in 2017 at about €4.4B (~$5B), but sold its own German brands to Takeaway.com in 2018 and later lost money on many expansions.

companies.o: AI-driven robot arms that load and unload trucks and handle parcels for FedEx and UPS
companies.story: Stanford robotics PhD Samir Menon founded Dexterity to make robot arms handle the messy physical work of parcel logistics, like stacking boxes into trucks, and sold first to FedEx, UPS and GXO. After a 2021 round valued it around $1.4B, it raised $95M in March 2025 at $1.65B led by Lightspeed and Sumitomo, to scale Mech, a two-armed 'superhumanoid' on wheels where one human supervises ten or more robots.

companies.o: Social news site where users voted stories to the front page
companies.story: Digg was one of the web's biggest traffic sources in the late 2000s and held acquisition talks with Google. A 2010 redesign that favored publishers over its community triggered a user revolt to Reddit, and in 2012 its remains sold to Betaworks for about $500,000.

companies.o: AI platform for home builders, partnered with building products giant Builders FirstSource
companies.story: Digs raised a $25.3M Series A led by Builders FirstSource, per a 2026 GeekWire report, after pre-Series A funding of about $20M. The strategic lead is also a distribution partner.

companies.o: Shenzhen giant that dominates the world consumer and commercial drone market
companies.story: Frank Wang started DJI in 2006 from his Hong Kong university dorm and used Shenzhen's supply chain to make drones better and cheaper than anyone, taking most of the global market and crushing Western rivals such as 3D Robotics. It is the benchmark any drone startup is judged against; US policy turned against it, and on 22 December 2025 the FCC added foreign-made drones to its Covered List, blocking new DJI models from US authorization.

companies.o: Online doctor appointment booking plus practice-management software
companies.story: Doctolib charges doctors a monthly subscription for scheduling software and gives patients free online booking, spreading across France, Germany and Italy. It ran France's COVID vaccine bookings and raised €500M in 2022 at €5.8B (~$6.1B).

companies.o: AI-first telehealth practice with human doctors on video
companies.story: Doctronic raised a $20M Series A led by Lightspeed in September 2025 for AI triage and 24/7 care. Some outlets dated it October.

companies.o: Razor blades by monthly subscription
companies.story: Dollar Shave Club launched in 2012 with a cheap, profane YouTube video that went viral and brought thousands of subscribers in its first days. It undercut Gillette's pricing, and Unilever bought it for a reported $1B in 2016.

companies.o: Consumer 'robot lawyer' subscription service fined by the FTC over unsubstantiated claims
companies.story: DoNotPay marketed itself as the world's first robot lawyer. The FTC settled with it in September 2024 for $193,000 without admission of liability and the order was finalized in early 2025, barring unsupported claims that it can replace legal services.

companies.o: Restaurant delivery marketplace
companies.story: Stanford students started DoorDash by delivering from Palo Alto restaurants themselves, then focused on suburbs that rivals ignored. Unlike Sprig and Munchery, it never cooked food, only delivered it; it went public in December 2020 raising $3.37B and became the US delivery leader.

companies.o: Ad-serving technology for online display advertising
companies.story: DoubleClick built the ad-serving plumbing for early web publishers and went public in 1998. It survived the dot-com crash, was taken private in 2005, and was bought by Google for $3.1B in 2007, becoming the core of Google's display ad business.

companies.o: Deep-learning self-driving startup acquired by Apple as it neared closure
companies.story: Drive.ai was once valued at $200M and was acquired by Apple in 2019 as it prepared to shut down after four years. It is an early sign of the AV talent-for-capital squeeze.

companies.o: Drone delivery operator built around Walmart, which later dropped it
companies.story: DroneUp became Walmart's main drone delivery partner after Walmart invested in it in 2021, and it absorbed drone-airspace software startup AirMap. Deliveries per hub stayed low; in 2024 it closed hubs in three states and cut jobs, and in January 2025 Walmart ended the partnership in favour of Wing and Zipline, a textbook single-customer risk.

near.what: Walmart, its main customer and investor, ended the partnership after DroneUp closed hubs and cut staff in 2024

companies.o: Hyperlocal app that would pick up and deliver anything in the city, later a 15-30 minute grocery dark-store service
companies.story: Dunzo began as a WhatsApp concierge that would fetch anything, won Google's first direct investment in India (2017) and a $240M Reliance-led round in 2022 at roughly $775M. It pivoted into 15-minute dark-store grocery delivery just as Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart out-spent it; salaries were delayed through 2023, buyout talks with Swiggy and BigBasket failed, and the app went dark in January 2025. Reliance wrote off its entire ~$200M stake (about Rs 1,645 crore) in FY25.

companies.o: Easy two-factor authentication for businesses
companies.story: Built in Ann Arbor, Michigan, Duo made two-factor login simple enough for any company to deploy. Cisco bought it for $2.35B in cash in 2018, one of the largest exits for a Midwest startup.

companies.o: Robot foundation-model startup that deploys paying robots on simple chores like folding laundry
companies.story: Dyna was started by the founders of smart-cart company Caper AI (sold to Instacart) with robot-learning researcher Jason Ma, and chose to put its model to work commercially early, starting with folding napkins and towels for hotels and laundries. It raised a $23.5M seed and then a $120M Series A in September 2025 with Robostrategy, CRV and First Round Capital.

companies.o: Low-cost small city electric car from an Aachen university spinout
companies.story: Professor Günther Schuh, who earlier built the StreetScooter van sold to Deutsche Post, founded e.GO to make cheap city EVs. Production stayed tiny, a planned SPAC listing fell apart, and after a first insolvency in 2020 it filed again in 2024.

companies.o: Online person-to-person auction marketplace
companies.story: eBay started as AuctionWeb in 1995 and was profitable early because it never held inventory. Benchmark's $6.7M investment became one of the best venture returns of the era after eBay's 1998 IPO, and eBay later bought PayPal.

companies.o: Facebook-style social network for teachers and students
companies.story: Edmodo spread through schools as a free classroom network adopted teacher by teacher, reaching tens of millions of users. China's NetDragon bought it for $137.5M in 2018, but it never found a strong business model and was shut down in 2022 after Google Classroom took over.

companies.o: Live online tutoring and exam-prep app for African secondary students
companies.story: Edukoya raised a record $3.5M pre-seed in 2021 for live synchronous tutoring. Poor connectivity, device access and low disposable income stopped it scaling; after failed merger and pivot talks it shut in February 2025 and returned capital to investors.

companies.o: IoT fish feeders plus feed supply, financing and fish trading for Indonesian aquaculture farmers
companies.story: eFishery sold automatic fish feeders and built feed, financing and fish-trading businesses for farmers, raising a $200M Series D in 2023 and reaching a reported $1.4B valuation. A whistleblower-triggered probe in late 2024 estimated management had inflated revenue by almost $600M in the nine months to September 2024 (about $752M reported vs about $157M actual), with two sets of books reportedly kept since 2018. In early 2025 it cut about 90% of staff while backers weighed liquidation, and an FTI report said investors might recover up to 10 cents on the dollar.

companies.o: Montreal AI lab co-founded by Yoshua Bengio selling AI to enterprises
companies.story: Element AI raised a record US$102M Series A in 2017 and about US$151M more in 2019 to sell AI products to big companies. Enterprise demand was early and projects looked like costly consulting; ServiceNow bought it in late 2020 for a price reported well below the more than US$250M raised.

companies.o: Voice AI company with text-to-speech, dubbing and music generation
companies.story: ElevenLabs raised $180M at a $3.3B valuation in January 2025 and a $500M Series D at $11B in February 2026 led by Sequoia. A later employee tender reportedly lifted its valuation to $22B.

companies.o: Self-driving long-haul truck software company that went public via SPAC
companies.story: Embark went public via SPAC and Crunchbase tracked its slide from a $5B valuation to wind-down in 16 months, laying off most staff in 2023. One report says Applied Intuition bought what remained for $71M.

companies.o: Maker of Moxie, an $799 AI companion robot for children, which went dark when the company shut down
companies.story: Founded by former iRobot CTO Paolo Pirjanian, Embodied sold Moxie, a $799 robot that used cloud AI to help children, including autistic children, practise social and emotional skills. When a critical funding round fell through it shut down in December 2024, and because Moxie depended on the company's cloud, the robots stopped working within days, leaving families with tearful goodbyes.

companies.o: Software to tame AI data center power demand
companies.story: Emerald AI raised a $150M Series A at a $1.05B valuation in August 2026 for data center power-demand software. Lead was not in snippets.

companies.o: Vibe-coding platform for small businesses and entrepreneurs
companies.story: Emergent raised $7M seed, a $23M Series A led by Lightspeed (September 2025) and a $70M Series B in January 2026. That is one of the fastest A-to-B gaps cited in AI.

companies.o: Analog in-memory AI accelerator chips
companies.story: EnCharge raised over $100M in a Series B led by Tiger Global in February 2025 to commercialize analog memory chips for AI.

companies.o: AI networking silicon connecting 100,000 GPUs
companies.story: In September 2025 Nvidia reportedly spent over $900M in cash and stock to hire CEO Rochan Sankar and license Enfabrica's technology. Valuation was uncertain, with one PitchBook-based estimate near $600M.

companies.o: RISC-V based AI inference chip developer
companies.story: Per a July 2025 EE Times Japan report, Esperanto shrank its chip business, cut roughly 90% of Mountain View staff and sought a buyer for its technology or IP-licensing partners. Press-reported only, no company statement seen.

companies.o: Lab from two Transformer co-authors that pivoted from enterprise agents to open base models
companies.story: Founded in 2023 by Ashish Vaswani and Niki Parmar, two authors of the Transformer paper, Essential raised a $56.5M Series A from investors including Google, Nvidia and AMD to build enterprise automation. Parmar left for Anthropic in late 2024 and the company pivoted to open research models, releasing the 8B-parameter open-weight Rnj-1 in December 2025.

companies.o: Premium Android phone maker founded by Android co-creator Andy Rubin
companies.story: Andy Rubin raised about $330M at a valuation near $1B to take on Apple and Samsung with the Essential Phone, launched in 2017. Sales were small, a planned follow-up was cancelled, and the company shut down in February 2020.

companies.o: Transformer-specific inference ASIC

rounds.lead: Primary Venture Partners, Positive Sum Ventures

companies.story: Etched raised $120M in 2024 and a reported $500M led by Stripes at about $5B, with later reports citing a $10.3B valuation and over $1B in contracts before first shipments. It bets everything on transformers.

companies.o: Online toy retailer that briefly out-valued Toys R Us
companies.story: eToys went public at $20 a share in 1999 and its stock hit about $85, implying a market value near $7.8B. Big warehouse build-outs and costly holiday seasons left it with about $247M in debt, and it filed for bankruptcy in early 2001; its brand later sold at auction for about $3.35M.

companies.o: French maker of Skypod robots that climb storage racks to fetch goods for pickers
companies.story: Founded near Lille by Romain Moulin and Renaud Heitz, Exotec built Skypod, robots that drive and climb up to 12m racks to bring totes to human pickers, and sold it to retailers such as Decathlon, Uniqlo and Carrefour. Its $335M Series D in January 2022 at $2B made it France's first industrial unicorn, and by its tenth anniversary in October 2025 it had more than 10,000 robots at over 200 customer sites.

companies.o: AI-driven drug discovery company designing small-molecule drugs
companies.story: Exscientia put what it called the first AI-designed drug molecule into clinical trials in 2020 and listed on Nasdaq in 2021. Pipeline setbacks and the 2024 dismissal of its founder-CEO preceded an all-stock merger into US rival Recursion in 2024 valuing it at about $688M, well below its IPO-era value.

companies.o: Flash-sale site for design products
companies.story: Fab pivoted from a social network into design flash sales in 2011 and grew so fast it reached a roughly $1B valuation, expanding into Europe and its own inventory. Growth stalled and costs ballooned, and after several pivots it was sold to manufacturing firm PCH in 2015 for a small fraction of the money raised.

companies.o: Real-identity social network that started at Harvard
companies.story: Facebook launched at Harvard in 2004 and expanded one college at a time, so each campus reached critical mass before the next opened, while Friendster's servers buckled and MySpace filled with spam. It raised $16B in its May 2012 IPO at a $104B valuation.

companies.o: HR software for small and mid-sized businesses
companies.story: Factorial started with free HR software for small companies in Spain and upsold paid modules, expanding to Latin America and the US. A $120M Series C led by Atomico in 2022 made it a unicorn.

companies.o: Inference platform for generative media models
companies.story: fal raised a $140M Series D led by Sequoia at $4.5B in December 2025 and was reported exploring another round.

companies.o: Online luxury fashion marketplace aggregating boutiques worldwide
companies.story: Portuguese founder José Neves built Farfetch in London with engineering in Porto and listed on the NYSE in 2018 at about $6.2B; its value peaked near $23B in 2021. Costly acquisitions and losses as luxury demand cooled left it near insolvency, and in December 2023 Coupang rescued it with a $500M loan that wiped out shareholders.

companies.o: One-click checkout button for online stores
companies.story: Fast raised a $102M Series B led by Stripe in 2021 to sell a one-click checkout, then hired aggressively and spent heavily on marketing. The Information reported it made only about $600,000 in revenue that year; unable to raise again, it shut down in April 2022 and Affirm offered jobs to most of its engineers.

companies.o: Egypt's electronic bill-payment network running through retail agents
