companies.story: Fawry let Egyptians pay bills and government fees in cash at hundreds of thousands of shops and points, digitising payments in a cash economy. Its 2019 listing on the Egyptian Exchange was heavily oversubscribed and its market value later crossed $1B, Egypt's first tech unicorn.

companies.o: Cloud-managed autonomous mobile robots for warehouses, bought by Zebra Technologies
companies.story: Melonee Wise, formerly of Willow Garage, co-founded Fetch to build mobile robots that move carts and materials around warehouses, managed from the cloud. Zebra Technologies, already a roughly 5% investor, bought the remaining stake in 2021 for about $290M, a modest exit that shows how many AMR makers ended up inside larger automation vendors.

companies.o: Courier app delivering to a phone's GPS location instead of a street address
companies.story: Fetchr solved the Gulf's lack of street addresses by delivering to a smartphone's location, raising NEA's first Middle East investment and a 2017 round at almost $300M valuation. After nearly collapsing in 2019 it pivoted to Saudi Arabia, where a disputed ~$100M VAT and zakat bill left it insolvent in 2021.

companies.o: Ex-NASA JPL team selling a 'physics-first' autonomy brain for robots in unmapped industrial sites
companies.story: Founded by former NASA JPL autonomy lead Ali Agha, FieldAI sells one software 'brain' that lets wheeled, legged and humanoid robots work at construction and industrial sites without maps or GPS. In August 2025 it announced $405M raised across two back-to-back rounds (Bezos Expeditions, Khosla, Gates, NVentures, Temasek), lifting its valuation to about $2B from $500M a year earlier.

companies.o: Platform for creating and chatting with custom AI characters
companies.story: Figgs ran from 2023 to 2024 and drew more than 1M users. The developers said keeping the service free became too expensive to sustain, so they shut it down.

companies.o: General-purpose humanoid robot built for factory and home work, run by its own Helix AI model
companies.story: Serial founder Brett Adcock (Archer, Vettery) self-funded Figure in 2022 and pitched a humanoid before it could do much. Microsoft, OpenAI, Nvidia and Jeff Bezos backed a $675M Series B at $2.6B in 2024; Figure then dropped its OpenAI deal to build its own Helix model and raised over $1B at a $39B post-money valuation in September 2025, roughly 15x in 19 months, on pilots such as BMW's Spartanburg plant rather than revenue at scale.

companies.o: Texas launch and lunar-lander company (Alpha rocket, Blue Ghost lander) reborn from a 2017 bankruptcy.
companies.story: Firefly Space Systems went bankrupt in 2017, was revived by Ukrainian-born investor Max Polyakov, and in 2022 US regulators forced him to sell his stake, after which AE Industrial took control. Its Blue Ghost lander made a fully successful Moon landing in March 2025 and it listed on Nasdaq in August 2025 at about $6.3B, closing day one near $9.8B; an April 2025 Alpha launch failure and a September 2025 booster loss in testing then cut the stock about 35% in a month.

near.what: Firefly Space Systems filed for bankruptcy after a key investor pulled out; assets bought by Noosphere Ventures
CFIUS forced owner Max Polyakov to divest over national-security concerns
Alpha launch failure in April and a booster destroyed in a September ground test

companies.o: Inference and fine-tuning platform for generative AI
companies.story: Fireworks raised a $52M Series B led by Sequoia at $552M in July 2024, then a $250M Series C at $4B in October 2025. Reports say it explored a raise near $15B.

companies.o: Asset-light EV maker that outsourced production of its Ocean SUV
companies.story: Designer Henrik Fisker's second EV company went public via SPAC in 2020 and had Magna build its Ocean SUV, which reached customers in 2023 with software and quality problems. Sales and cash fell short and it filed for Chapter 11 in June 2024, about a decade after his first company, Fisker Automotive, also went bankrupt.

companies.o: Clip-on and wrist fitness trackers
companies.story: Fitbit won the fitness-tracker market against Jawbone with reliable devices and strong retail distribution, and raised $732M in a 2015 IPO. Apple Watch later squeezed it, and Google bought it for $2.1B in 2021.

companies.o: Marketplace for freelance services, originally all priced at $5
companies.story: Fiverr packaged freelance work as fixed-price 'gigs' starting at $5, making services browsable like products. It listed on the NYSE in June 2019 raising about $111M and boomed during the remote-work era of 2020-21 before falling back.

companies.o: Software-driven international freight forwarder
companies.story: Flexport became a licensed freight forwarder and customs broker and ran it with modern software, booming during the 2021 shipping crunch to an $8B valuation in 2022. It survived the freight downturn that killed Convoy and bought Convoy's technology in 2023.

companies.o: AI tutors built for schools
companies.story: Flint raised a $15M Series A, reported by Axios in November 2025. The lead was not named in the snippet.

companies.o: Asset-light intercity bus network where partners own the buses and Flix runs brand, pricing and tech
companies.story: FlixBus launched right after Germany deregulated long-distance buses in 2013, letting local operators run green-branded buses while Flix handled booking and pricing. It consolidated Europe, bought Greyhound in the US in 2021 and raised $650M at about $3B the same year.

companies.o: Online gift currency spendable at partner retailers, advertised by Whoopi Goldberg
companies.story: Flooz tried to create a private internet currency that people could gift and spend at partner merchants, backed by a Whoopi Goldberg ad campaign. Consumers never adopted it beyond gifting, and it folded in 2001 as dot-com funding dried up.

companies.o: Converts mining sites into AI data centers and GPU cloud
companies.story: Fluidstack raised a reported $830M Series A at roughly $7.5-8B, but pulled out of a marquee EUR10B French AI project in March 2026. Round date and lead were not in snippets.

companies.o: Payments infrastructure letting businesses accept and send money across Africa
companies.story: Flutterwave (YC 2016) built rails for merchants to accept cards, bank transfers and mobile money across dozens of African currencies. It became a unicorn in 2021 and was valued at $3B in a $250M Series D in 2022, Africa's most valuable startup at the time, though it later faced regulatory probes in Kenya and down-market pressure.

companies.o: AI software that automates support ticket handling with self-learning agents
companies.story: Founded in 2017, Forethought sold agentic support AI before Zendesk announced it would acquire it on March 11, 2026. Terms were not disclosed.

companies.o: Rents factory robots to small US manufacturers by the hour instead of selling them
companies.story: Formic, founded by Saman Farid, does not build robots; it buys standard arms and integrates them, then charges small and mid-size manufacturers an hourly fee so they avoid upfront capital costs. It raised a $26.5M Series A led by Lux Capital in 2022, a $27.4M extension in 2024 and a $50M Series B in 2026.

companies.o: Tech-heavy membership primary care that pivoted to self-serve 'CarePod' kiosks
companies.story: Ex-Google executive Adrian Aoun built Forward as a $149-a-month high-tech doctor's office, then bet on CarePods, booths where patients ran their own checkups; early pods reportedly cost over $1M each to build. Reported funding ranges from $400M to about $657M; it closed all locations and its app with no notice in November 2024, cutting nearly 200 jobs.

companies.o: Shanghai rehab-robot maker that pivoted into GR-series humanoids
companies.story: Fourier spent its first years selling rehabilitation exoskeletons and therapy robots to hospitals, then used that hardware base to launch the GR-1 humanoid in 2023 and later an open-source N1 model. It raised nearly 800M yuan (~$109M) in a Series E announced January 2025 with Prosperity7 and Shanghai state funds; a May 2025 deal reportedly priced it at about 8B yuan (~$1.1B) pre-money.

companies.o: UK inference chip startup

rounds.lead: Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed, Redpoint

companies.story: Fractile went from a $15M seed to a $220M Series B in May 2026 and a reported $720M Series C in November at about $7B. An Anthropic chip deal was reported alongside the valuation climb.

companies.o: App to help students fill out federal college financial-aid forms
companies.story: JPMorgan Chase bought Frank for $175M in 2021 based on claims of more than 4 million users, while the real figure was closer to 300,000; prosecutors said founder Charlie Javice had a fake customer list generated. JPMorgan shut the product, a jury convicted Javice of fraud in 2025, and she was sentenced to more than seven years in prison.

companies.o: AI scribe for individual clinicians and small practices
companies.story: Freed raised a $30M Series A led by Sequoia Capital in March 2025, taking total funding to $34M. It targets independent clinicians rather than health systems.

companies.o: The first mainstream social network of friends-of-friends
companies.story: Friendster grew to millions of users in 2003 and reportedly turned down a $30M offer from Google, then raised $13M from Kleiner Perkins and Benchmark. Pages took so long to load that US users left for Myspace and Facebook while its board focused elsewhere; it survived on Asian users and was sold to Malaysia's MOL Global in 2009 before shutting in 2015.

companies.o: B2B app supplying fresh produce and groceries to restaurants and small shops in Colombia, Mexico and Brazil
companies.story: Frubana let restaurants and corner shops order produce and groceries wholesale through an app, cutting out middlemen, and expanded from Colombia to Mexico and Brazil. After layoffs in 2022, it announced in February 2024 that it would close Colombia and Mexico to concentrate on Brazil, then shut its last active market there, joining Merqueo among Colombia's high-profile startup closures. Analyses citing CB Insights grouped it with Jüsto as a LatAm example of the post-2022 funding crunch.

companies.o: AI workspace for insurance covering submissions, claims and underwriting audits
companies.story: FurtherAI raised a $25M Series A led by a16z on October 7, 2025, after an earlier $5M seed. Nexus Venture Partners and Y Combinator also participated.

companies.o: Celebrity-booking app that promoted the luxury Fyre Festival
companies.story: Billy McFarland and Ja Rule's Fyre Media marketed a luxury music festival in the Bahamas with influencer posts, but guests in April 2017 found disaster-relief tents and cheese sandwiches. McFarland pleaded guilty to defrauding investors and ticket buyers and was sentenced to six years in prison.

companies.o: Cloud streaming of instant-play video game demos
companies.story: Gaikai streamed playable game demos inside websites and sold the service to publishers rather than charging consumers. Sony bought it for $380M in 2012, the same year rival OnLive collapsed, and used its technology for PlayStation Now.

companies.o: Chinese private launcher whose solid-fuel Ceres-1 became the country's most-flown commercial rocket.
companies.story: Galactic Energy flew more than 20 successful Ceres-1 missions after its 2020 debut, but a November 2025 fourth-stage failure lost three satellites, its second failure in about two years, shortly after it raised 2.4B yuan (about $335M) and while preparing an A-share IPO. Its larger Ceres-2 failed on its January 2026 debut, and a single source reports its liquid Pallas-1 reached orbit on its first attempt in September 2026.

companies.o: Autonomous box trucks for middle-mile freight

rounds.lead: Qatar Investment Authority, Koch Disruptive Technologies

companies.story: Gatik raised a $4.5M seed, a $25M Series A (2020), an $85M Series B led by Koch Disruptive Technologies, and a $200M Series D led by Qatar Investment Authority and Koch Disruptive Technologies. It focuses on short fixed routes rather than long-haul.

companies.o: Network of gossip and tech blogs including Gawker.com
companies.story: Gawker Media built a profitable network of blogs without much outside funding. A jury awarded Hulk Hogan $140M in 2016 over Gawker's publication of his sex tape in a lawsuit secretly funded by Peter Thiel; the company went bankrupt and sold its sites to Univision for $135M, shutting Gawker.com.

companies.o: Chinese warehouse-robot maker that became the first listed AMR company
companies.story: Geek+ built Kiva-style shelf-moving robots for warehouses just as Amazon stopped selling Kiva to others, and grew into a global supplier with customers across Asia, Europe and the US. It listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on 9 July 2025, raising about HK$2.7B (~$346M) with the retail tranche 133x oversubscribed, billed as the world's first listed AMR company.

companies.o: Canadian magnetized-target fusion pioneer that nearly ran out of money in 2025 after two decades of work.

rounds.lead: SPAC: Spring Valley Acquisition Corp III (announced)

companies.story: Founded in 2002 and backed by Jeff Bezos, General Fusion raised about $440M but in May 2025 its CEO published an open letter citing an 'unexpected and urgent financing constraint', laid off about a quarter of its 140 staff, scaled back its LM26 machine and sought $125M. A $22M lifeline kept it alive, and it then announced a reverse merger with SPAC Spring Valley III valuing the combined company at about $1B with up to $335M in proceeds; completion was not confirmed in the sources.

near.what: Open letter on an urgent financing gap, ~25% layoffs and LM26 scaled back; saved by a $22M lifeline and a SPAC deal

companies.o: Apple spinout that designed a smartphone-like handheld communicator in the early 1990s
companies.story: Former Apple engineers founded General Magic to build Magic Cap, a touchscreen communicator OS, and its 1995 IPO doubled on day one. Devices launched before cheap wireless data existed and sold poorly; after a pivot to voice services it liquidated in 2002, while alumni went on to lead the iPhone and Android projects.

companies.o: Ex-Google DeepMind team training large robot models on huge real-world manipulation data
companies.story: Founded by former Google DeepMind robotics researchers including Pete Florence, Generalist trains large robot models on hundreds of thousands of hours of real manipulation data and released its GEN-1 model in April 2026. Two months later it raised $400M at a $2B valuation led by Radical Ventures (with Nvidia and Bezos reported as backers), taking total funding past $500M.

companies.o: Physics-simulation-first lab generating synthetic data to train robot foundation models
companies.story: Genesis AI grew out of the open-source Genesis physics simulator led by CMU's Zhou Xian and co-founder Theophile Gervet, betting that cheap synthetic simulation data can solve robotics' data shortage. It emerged from stealth in July 2025 with a $105M seed co-led by Eclipse and Khosla Ventures, one of the largest seed rounds in robotics, with teams in Palo Alto and Paris.

companies.o: Munich GPU-as-a-service cloud on green energy
companies.story: Genesis Cloud GmbH is listed as in liquidation (i.L.), with about $6.6M raised per Crunchbase. Bizety speculates falling GPU rental prices and the cost of renewing hardware squeezed margins; no official notice found.

companies.o: Turkish pioneer of 10-minute grocery delivery from dark stores
companies.story: Getir invented 10-minute delivery in Istanbul in 2015, where dense neighbourhoods and lower wages made it work, and was valued at $11.8B in 2022. Its international expansion failed and it quit all markets outside Turkey by 2024; its valuation fell to about $2.5B and Mubadala took control of the core Turkish business.

companies.o: Getir's 10-minute grocery delivery expansion outside Turkey
companies.story: Getir launched in London in January 2021 and spread to the Netherlands, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Portugal and the US, buying rival Gorillas in 2022. High wages, low order density and price competition made dark stores unprofitable; it quit France, Spain, Italy and Portugal in 2023 and the UK, Germany, Netherlands and US in April 2024, cutting thousands of jobs to refocus on Turkey.

companies.o: Deepfake and impersonation attack detection
companies.story: GetReal raised a $17.5M Series A in March 2025 led by Forgepoint Capital with Ballistic Ventures, Evolution Equity and K2 Access Fund. It targets deepfake-driven impersonation fraud.

companies.o: OpenAI-backed self-driving software startup that shut down in 2024
companies.story: Ghost Autonomy, backed by OpenAI's startup fund, shut down in April 2024. Reported funding conflicts: $63.7M in one source, about $220M per S&P Global, so total is left null.

companies.o: Australian startup building Eris, the first Australian-designed orbital rocket, and its own spaceport in Queensland.
companies.story: Brothers Adam and James Gilmour started the company in 2012 and spent years on hybrid rocket motors and a private spaceport at Bowen, Queensland. The first Eris rocket lifted off in July 2025 and fell back about 14 seconds later; the company said it was not giving up and aimed for a second flight at the end of 2026, with trackers showing slippage into 2027.

near.what: Maiden Eris flight fell back to the pad area 14 seconds after liftoff

companies.o: Hosting and collaboration platform for code built on Git
companies.story: GitHub's founders ran it profitably without venture money for four years before taking a $100M Series A from Andreessen Horowitz in 2012. It became the default home for open-source code, and Microsoft bought it for $7.5B in stock in 2018.

companies.o: AI software that assists radiologists reading X-rays
companies.story: Gleamer raised a EUR27M (about $29.5M) Series B in June 2023 co-led by Supernova Invest and Heal Capital.

companies.o: On-demand courier app delivering anything from local stores and restaurants in under 30 minutes
companies.story: Glovo started in Barcelona delivering 'anything' and won Spain, Italy, Portugal, Eastern Europe and Africa where it arrived first. It lost Latin America to the better-funded Rappi and sold those operations to Delivery Hero in 2020 for about €230M (~$272M); Delivery Hero then took majority control in 2022 valuing Glovo at €2.3B (~$2.4B). Spain's 2021 rider law forced it toward employing couriers by 2025.

companies.o: Network of branded partner workshops for app-booked car servicing and repair
companies.story: GoMechanic built a franchise network of car-service workshops and raised about $62M from Sequoia (Peak XV), Tiger Global, Orios and Chiratae, hitting a $285M valuation in 2021 and negotiating with SoftBank at up to $1B. In January 2023 the founders admitted inflating revenue; the SoftBank deal collapsed, 70% of staff were laid off and investors filed a police complaint. In March 2023 its assets went in an undisclosed slump sale to a Lifelong Group-led consortium (Servizzy), with founders left out.

companies.o: Delivers snacks and essentials from its own micro-warehouses in about 30 minutes
companies.story: Two Drexel students started Gopuff delivering snacks to college students, owning inventory in small warehouses and charging a delivery fee, which gave it retail margins that Kozmo never had. It grew slowly for years before raising $1.15B at a $15B valuation in 2021.

companies.o: 10-minute grocery delivery from dark stores with employed riders
companies.story: Gorillas became a unicorn in about nine months and raised around $1.3B, expanding to 60+ cities in Europe and New York during the zero-rate era. Rider strikes, low order values and costly dark stores burned cash; it exited several countries in 2022 and Getir bought it in December 2022 in an all-stock deal reported at about $1.2B, below its capital raised.

companies.o: Online one-to-one tutoring marketplace for school students
companies.story: GoStudent became Europe's most valuable edtech after a €300M round in 2022 at €3B (~$3.15B) backed by DST, Tencent and SoftBank. After schools reopened, growth slowed and it cut staff and wrote down acquisitions, but kept operating unlike India's BYJU'S.

companies.o: UK maker of IPU processors for AI training and inference
companies.story: Once valued at $2.8B, Graphcore cut about 20% of staff, pulled out of China and closed offices before SoftBank bought it in July 2024 for a reported $500M-$600M. It could not dent Nvidia's software ecosystem and ran short of funding.

companies.o: Supply-chain finance firm packaging invoices into investment funds
companies.story: Greensill advanced cash against invoices (and future receivables) and sold the loans through Credit Suisse funds worth about $10B, backed by SoftBank's ~$1.5B investment. When its credit insurer refused to renew cover in March 2021 it collapsed into insolvency, sparking investigations and a lobbying scandal involving former UK PM David Cameron.

companies.o: India-born warehouse robots and orchestration software company now based near Atlanta
companies.story: Samay Kohli and Akash Gupta founded GreyOrange in Gurgaon in 2011 to build sorting and goods-to-person robots for Indian e-commerce, then moved headquarters to the Atlanta area to sell to US retailers and 3PLs. It raised $140M in 2018 led by Mithril Capital and $135M in a December 2023 Series D, and has shifted its pitch toward orchestration software that coordinates robots from many vendors; total funding is put at roughly $425M-$590M depending on the source.

companies.o: AI platform forecasting crop supply and climate risk for agribusiness and governments
companies.story: Kenyan-born founder Sara Menker built Gro (offices in Nairobi and New York) into a high-profile agri-data platform with roughly $120M raised. After emergency funding and 60% layoffs in March 2024, the board replaced the founder and the company shut in June 2024 after failing to find a buyer.

companies.o: Free on-demand music streaming built on user-uploaded songs
companies.story: Grooveshark let users upload and stream almost any song free, without licenses from most major labels. After years of label lawsuits and a court finding of liability, it settled and shut down in April 2015, while licensed services like Spotify and Pandora grew.

companies.o: Inference chip maker (LPU) with its own cloud
companies.story: On Christmas Eve 2025 Nvidia struck a reported $20B deal to license Groq's technology and hire most of its team without buying the company. Groq had raised $750M led by Disruptive; some sources date its valuation at $2.8B in 2024.

companies.o: Daily group-buying discounts at local businesses
companies.story: Groupon pivoted from a collective-action site called The Point into daily deals and became one of the fastest-growing companies ever, turning down a reported $6B offer from Google in 2010. It raised $700M in a November 2011 IPO at about $12.7B, but merchant fatigue and copycats sent the stock far lower within a few years.

companies.o: Mobile-first investing app for mutual funds and stocks aimed at first-time Indian investors
companies.story: Four ex-Flipkart employees started Groww in 2016 to sell mutual funds to first-time investors, then added stocks and rode India's post-2020 retail-investing boom to become the country's largest broker by active clients. It moved its domicile from the US back to India before listing in November 2025 (IPO about Rs 6,632 crore, ~$767M at 86.5 INR/USD); the stock closed ~29% above issue on day one for a market cap of about Rs 795 billion (~$9B).

companies.o: Direct-to-consumer gym clothing brand built on social-media influencers
companies.story: Ben Francis started Gymshark at 19, sewing clothes and sponsoring early YouTube fitness creators, and grew it without outside capital. General Atlantic bought 21% in 2020, valuing it at over £1B (~$1.3B), unlike UK D2C peer Made.com which collapsed in 2022.

companies.o: On-demand marketplace for home cleaning and handyman jobs
companies.story: Handy competed directly with Homejoy in cleaning and handyman bookings and even held talks to buy it in 2015. It outlasted its rival and was acquired by ANGI Homeservices in October 2018; ANGI's filing valued the 8.6M shares it issued at $165.8M plus cash.

companies.o: Generative AI platform for law firms and legal departments
companies.story: Harvey raised $300M at $3B (Feb 2025, Sequoia) and $300M at $5B (Jun 2025, Kleiner and Coatue), then $200M at $11B in March 2026 co-led by GIC and Sequoia. Later rounds are labeled inconsistently across trackers.

companies.o: AI document analysis platform for finance firms answering complex queries
companies.story: Hebbia raised about $130M in a mid-2024 Series B led by a16z with Index Ventures, GV and Peter Thiel. CB Insights lists a Series B-II in February 2026 without a named lead; The Information says Rogo has overtaken it on revenue.

companies.o: Generative video platform for digital characters
companies.story: Hedra raised a $10M seed and then a $32M Series A in May 2025 led by a16z Infrastructure, with a reported $200M valuation from one source.

companies.o: AI clinical scribe used across several countries
companies.story: Heidi raised a $16.6M Series A extension led by Headline with Anthology (Menlo Ventures and Anthropic), then a $65M Series B led by Point72 in October 2025. Round dates before the Series B were not shown in snippets.

companies.o: Pulsed magneto-inertial fusion company that promised Microsoft fusion electricity by 2028.
companies.story: Helion signed the first fusion power purchase agreement in 2023, promising Microsoft electricity by 2028, and began building its Orion plant in Malaga, Washington in 2025 though no fusion device anywhere had yet produced net electricity. Backed by Sam Altman, it raised $425M at about $5.2B in January 2025 and a $465M Series G led by Thrive Capital at $15.5B in June 2026 (about $1.5B raised), reporting deuterium-tritium operation of its Polaris prototype.

companies.o: Ant-backed bike-sharing and mobility app that started in smaller Chinese cities
companies.story: Hellobike survived the bike-sharing war that killed ofo and Bluegogo by backing from Ant Financial, which co-led a $582M round in December 2018 reportedly valuing it at $2.3B, and by expanding into e-bikes and carpooling. It filed for a US IPO in April 2021 but withdrew in July 2021 after Beijing tightened overseas listing rules, and remains private.

companies.o: Subscription meal-kit boxes with recipes and pre-portioned ingredients
companies.story: Rocket Internet-backed HelloFresh launched in Berlin in 2011 and expanded into the US and a dozen markets, outlasting US pioneer Blue Apron. It listed in Frankfurt in 2017 at about €1.7B (~$1.9B) and boomed during COVID, while Blue Apron was sold for $103M in 2023.

companies.o: AI software and drones for European defence ministries
companies.story: Helsing sells AI battlefield software and strike drones to European governments, a category VCs avoided until Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Spotify founder Daniel Ek's fund led its 2025 €600M round at €12B (~$13.6B), making it one of Europe's most valuable startups.

companies.o: AI runtime and model security platform
companies.story: HiddenLayer raised a $100M Series B led by Delta-v Capital on September 2, 2026, after a $50M Series A. Its CEO says ARR grew more than 10x in a year.

companies.o: AI video platform for social media marketers
companies.story: Higgsfield raised a $50M Series A led by GFT Ventures in September 2025, then an $80M extension in January 2026 at over $1.3B. Social media marketers make up about 85% of usage.

companies.o: Indian messaging app (Hike Messenger) that pivoted to the Rush real-money casual-gaming app
companies.story: Kavin Bharti Mittal's Hike became a unicorn in 2016 ($175M Series D at $1.4B from Tencent, Foxconn, Tiger and SoftBank) as India's answer to WhatsApp, but WhatsApp won the market and Hike shut its messenger in January 2021. It pivoted to Rush, a real-money ludo and carrom app that drew 10M+ users and reportedly $500M+ gross revenue. India's 2025 ban on real-money online games cut its runway from seven months to four and Hike shut down entirely in September 2025.

companies.o: Rocket Internet's online furniture and home retailer
companies.story: Home24 was a Rocket Internet clone of Wayfair for Germany and Brazil and listed in Frankfurt in 2018. Bulky-goods logistics and thin margins kept it loss-making; furniture giant XXXLutz took it over in 2023 at a share price far below the IPO price.

companies.o: Seattle-area online grocery delivery service backed by Amazon
companies.story: HomeGrocer ran online grocery delivery in the Pacific Northwest and went public in March 2000. Months later it was swallowed by rival Webvan in a stock deal valued at $1.2B, and that stock became worthless when Webvan collapsed in 2001.

companies.o: Book a vetted home cleaner online in a few clicks
companies.story: Homejoy used cheap first-clean promotions to expand fast across US cities, but customers and cleaners often left the platform after a booking, so retention never paid back acquisition costs. Facing lawsuits over whether its cleaners were contractors or employees and unable to raise a Series C, it shut down in July 2015 after raising about $40M.

companies.o: House of online-first personal-care brands that started with toxin-free baby products
companies.story: Varun and Ghazal Alagh launched Mamaearth in 2016 selling toxin-free baby products online, then used influencer marketing to spin up a portfolio of D2C brands and became a unicorn in 2022. It listed in November 2023 with a Rs 1,701 crore IPO (~$206M at 82.6) at a valuation of about Rs 10,400 crore, far below the ~$3B once floated, and opened only ~2% above issue.

companies.o: Virtual events platform that boomed during COVID lockdowns
companies.story: Hopin went from founding to a $7.75B valuation in about two years as conferences moved online, raising roughly $1B and buying multiple startups. When in-person events returned demand collapsed; in 2023 it sold its events business to RingCentral for $15M upfront (up to $50M), under 1% of its peak value.

companies.o: Mobile travel app that predicts when flight and hotel prices will drop
companies.story: Hopper spent years building price-prediction data before launching a mobile-only booking app, then made money selling add-ons like price freezes and flexible cancellation. A 2021 round valued it at about $3.5B.

companies.o: Inbound marketing and CRM software for small and mid-size businesses
companies.story: HubSpot popularized 'inbound marketing', teaching businesses to attract customers with content and selling them the software to do it. It went public in 2014 and grew into a large CRM platform for smaller companies.

companies.o: Screenless AI Pin wearable meant to replace the smartphone
companies.story: Founded by ex-Apple staff, Humane raised more than $230M and launched its $699 AI Pin in 2024 to poor reviews about heat, battery and slow answers. It reportedly sold about 10,000 units against a 100,000 goal; after seeking a $750M-$1B sale, it sold its software, patents and most staff to HP for $116M in February 2025 and bricked the pins.

companies.o: Cloud-hosted GPU marketplace
companies.story: Hyperbolic raised a $7M seed and a $12M round in December 2024 led by Variant and Polychain, sources split on calling it Series A. It runs a marketplace renting spare GPUs.

companies.o: Company developing near-vacuum tube 'hyperloop' transport
companies.story: Inspired by Elon Musk's 2013 hyperloop paper, the company (renamed Virgin Hyperloop after Richard Branson invested) ran the first passenger test in a tube in Las Vegas in 2020. No government signed a full route, a pivot to cargo did not help, and it shut down at the end of 2023.

companies.o: Dutch social network that dominated the Netherlands before Facebook
companies.story: Hyves had more Dutch users than Facebook in the late 2000s and was sold to Telegraaf Media Groep in 2010 for about €44M (~$59M). Facebook overtook it within two years and the social network shut in December 2013.

companies.o: Precision liquid cooling for AI racks

rounds.lead: Barclays Climate Ventures, Two Seas Capital

companies.story: Iceotope raised a $26M Series B in May 2026 led by Barclays Climate Ventures and Two Seas Capital as AI rack densities outgrow air cooling.

companies.o: Finnish operator of the largest synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) small-satellite constellation, imaging through clouds and at night.
companies.story: Two Aalto University students started ICEYE in 2014 to shrink radar satellites, which most experts thought too power-hungry for small spacecraft. Wartime demand after Russia's invasion of Ukraine turned it into Europe's defense-intelligence darling: it raised at about EUR2.4B in December 2025 and then a EUR450M primary Series F (over EUR1B with secondaries) led by General Atlantic in June 2026 at more than EUR10B (about $11.5B), roughly quadrupling in six months.

companies.o: Spain's leading online property listings portal, also in Italy and Portugal
companies.story: Founded by the Encinar brothers during the dot-com boom, Idealista became the dominant Spanish property portal and expanded to Italy and Portugal. It passed between private-equity owners (Apax, then EQT for €1.3B in 2020) and Cinven bought it in 2024 for €2.9B (~$3.1B).

companies.o: Orbital transfer vehicles (Mira, Helios) that move satellites between orbits, founded by SpaceX's first engine chief Tom Mueller.
companies.story: Tom Mueller, who designed SpaceX's Merlin engine, founded Impulse in 2021 to give satellites a last-mile ride between orbits. Its Mira vehicle flew three missions by 2026, and it raised a $300M Series C in June 2025 and a $500M Series D at about $4.26B in June 2026, extended by $308M in September (Series D figures from Sacra); the larger Helios stage slipped to 2027.

companies.o: Builds diffusion-based large language models (Mercury) that generate text in parallel
companies.story: Founded by Stanford professor Stefano Ermon with Aditya Grover and Volodymyr Kuleshov, Inception applies the diffusion approach used in image models to text, so its Mercury models generate many tokens at once and run several times faster than autoregressive LLMs. It raised a $50M seed led by Menlo Ventures in November 2025; online claims of a $10B valuation are unsupported.

companies.o: Modular vertical farms inside supermarkets and urban hubs
companies.story: Infarm put vertical farms in supermarkets across Europe, the US and Japan and became a unicorn with a $200M round in 2021. When energy prices spiked after 2022 its unit economics broke; it exited most markets, laid off most staff and its operating units went insolvent in 2023, mirroring US failures like AeroFarms.

companies.o: Commercial company behind the vLLM inference engine
companies.story: Inferact announced a $150M seed in January 2026 led by a16z at an $800M post-money to commercialize vLLM.

companies.o: AI lab behind the Pi personal assistant chatbot
companies.story: Founded by DeepMind co-founder Mustafa Suleyman and Reid Hoffman, Inflection raised about $1.5B, including $1.3B in 2023 from Microsoft and Nvidia, to build the Pi chatbot. Unable to compete with OpenAI and Google on cost, in March 2024 it let Microsoft hire its founders and most staff and pay about $650M to license its models, a 'reverse acquihire' later probed by the FTC and UK CMA.

companies.o: Network of 24/7 parcel lockers for e-commerce deliveries
companies.story: Rafał Brzoska built a dense network of parcel lockers across Poland, making e-commerce delivery cheaper and faster than couriers to the door. After Advent took it private in 2017, InPost listed in Amsterdam in January 2021 at about €8B (~$9.4B) and expanded into the UK and France.

companies.o: Same-day grocery delivery by personal shoppers from existing stores
companies.story: Instacart revived Webvan's idea without warehouses or trucks, sending gig shoppers into existing supermarkets and partnering with grocers. Pandemic demand pushed its private valuation to $39B in 2021, and it went public in September 2023 at about $9.9B.

companies.o: Tunisian-founded AI company building decision-making and biology AI
companies.story: Karim Beguir and Zohra Slim started InstaDeep in Tunis in 2014 with two laptops and about $2,000, later moving headquarters to London. After a $100M Series B in 2022, BioNTech bought it in 2023 for up to £562M (~$682M), Africa's largest AI exit.

companies.o: Mobile photo-sharing app with filters
companies.story: Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger stripped their check-in app Burbn down to one feature, photo sharing with filters, and launched on iPhone in 2010. About 18 months later, with 13 employees, Facebook bought it for $1B in April 2012, days after it raised at a $500M valuation, the same era in which Color burned $41M on a similar idea.

companies.o: Nigeria's payment switch and Verve card scheme
companies.story: Interswitch connected Nigerian banks' ATMs and cards from 2002 and launched the Verve card scheme. Visa took a minority stake (reported ~20% for ~$200M) in 2019, valuing it at about $1B and making it one of Africa's first fintech unicorns; its long-planned IPO has repeatedly slipped.

companies.o: Lunar lander and data-relay company that made the first US Moon landing since 1972.
companies.story: Intuitive Machines listed via a SPAC in February 2023 at about $1B; its Odysseus lander touched down near the lunar south pole in February 2024, the first US landing since Apollo, but tipped onto its side, and its second lander tipped over in a crater in March 2025. It won a NASA lunar data-relay contract worth up to $4.82B in 2024 and in January 2026 closed the $800M purchase of Lanteris (formerly Maxar's satellite unit), guiding to $920-950M of 2026 revenue.

near.what: Odysseus landed but tipped over, cutting the mission short
Second lander, Athena, also tipped over in a crater

companies.o: Peer-to-peer lending marketplace funding working-capital and invoice loans for Indonesian SMEs
companies.story: Investree matched lenders with Indonesian SMEs needing working-capital and invoice loans, and in October 2023 announced a ~$231M (EUR 220M) Series D anchored by Qatar's JTA International Holdings, structured through a joint venture. Regulator OJK revoked its licence on 21 October 2024 after it failed to meet the Rp 7.5B minimum-equity requirement and ignored warnings to inject capital and fix governance, sending it into liquidation. OJK then pursued ex-CEO Adrian Gunadi over alleged misuse of funds, and he was reportedly placed on Interpol's wanted list.

companies.o: 66-satellite constellation for global satellite phone calls
companies.story: Motorola-backed Iridium spent about $5B launching a low-earth-orbit satellite network, but its bulky handsets cost thousands of dollars and calls several dollars a minute while cheap cell networks spread. It filed for bankruptcy in 1999, less than a year after launching service, and the satellites were sold for about $25M.

companies.o: Roomba maker that went public in 2005, lost its Amazon deal to regulators and ended in Chapter 11
companies.story: MIT roboticists founded iRobot in 1990, survived on military and toy contracts, and created the home-robot category with the Roomba in 2002 before a 2005 IPO. Cheaper, better-featured Chinese vacuums from Roborock and Ecovacs eroded its share, Amazon's $1.7B takeover was abandoned in January 2024 under EU antitrust pressure, and on 14 December 2025 it filed a pre-packaged Chapter 11 in which its Chinese contract manufacturer and lender Picea took ownership and shareholders were wiped out.

near.what: Amazon's $1.7B acquisition abandoned under EU antitrust pressure; 31% layoffs and CEO exit

companies.o: Network cyber-defense company founded by a former NSA director
companies.story: Founded by former NSA director Gen. Keith Alexander, IronNet sold collective cyber-defense software and went public via SPAC in 2021. Sales lagged its forecasts and losses mounted, and it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October 2023.

companies.o: Mobile app monetisation and advertising platform for game developers
companies.story: ironSource went public via a Thoma Bravo SPAC in 2021 at about $11.1B, one of the few profitable SPAC listings. After Apple's privacy changes hit mobile ads it merged into Unity in 2022 in an all-stock deal worth about $4.4B.

companies.o: Munich rocket startup building the Spectrum small launcher, Europe's best-funded private launch company.
companies.story: Founded by Technical University of Munich graduates, Isar's first Spectrum launch from Norway in March 2025 failed about 30 seconds after liftoff. It raised a EUR150M convertible in 2025 and a EUR270M Series D in June 2026 (total about EUR870M, roughly $1B at ~1.15 USD/EUR; Bloomberg reported talks at a EUR2B valuation), and its second flight reached orbit on 5 September 2026, the first commercial orbital launch from continental Europe.

near.what: Maiden Spectrum flight failed about 30 seconds after liftoff

companies.o: Alphabet spinout designing drugs with AI
companies.story: Isomorphic raised $600M in its first external round in March 2025 led by Thrive Capital, then a $2.1B round in May 2026 reported as led by Thrive. A further $5bn raise was reported but unclear in snippets.

companies.o: Japanese lunar lander company (Hakuto-R) aiming at commercial Moon delivery and resources.
companies.story: Born from Team Hakuto in the Google Lunar XPRIZE, ispace raised a then-record $90M Series A for a Japanese startup in 2017 and listed on the Tokyo Growth market in April 2023, just before its first lander crashed on the Moon after misjudging its altitude. Its second lander, Resilience, also crashed in June 2025 after a laser rangefinder problem, and the company's market value was about 50B yen in late 2024.

near.what: First Hakuto-R lander crashed on the Moon weeks after the IPO
Second lander, Resilience, crashed during landing

companies.o: Beijing launcher that became the first Chinese private company to reach orbit, with Hyperbola-1 in 2019.
companies.story: iSpace's solid-fuel Hyperbola-1 reached orbit in July 2019, a first for a Chinese private firm, but a string of later failures stalled it while it developed the reusable methane-fuelled Hyperbola-3. It reportedly raised a 1B yuan (about $148M) first tranche of a Series E after a large D++ round and finished IPO tutoring, targeting a STAR Market listing in the second half of 2027.

near.what: Two consecutive Hyperbola-1 failures after its 2019 success

companies.o: Mobile card reader and point-of-sale app for small merchants
companies.story: iZettle brought Square's idea to Europe with chip-and-PIN readers and spread across Europe and Latin America. PayPal bought it for $2.2B in 2018, days before its planned IPO.

companies.o: AI content platform for marketing teams
companies.story: Jasper raised $125M in October 2022 and labeled it a Series A at about $1.5B (TechCrunch's URL says $1.7B). A site claiming a 2025 $125M Series B is unverified, and I found no later round.

companies.o: Maker of Bluetooth headsets, Jambox speakers and UP fitness trackers
companies.story: Jawbone raised around $1B and was valued at about $3B on headsets, speakers and UP fitness bands. Faulty trackers, costly lawsuits with Fitbit and competition from Fitbit and Apple Watch led to a down round in 2016 and liquidation in July 2017.

companies.o: Developer IDEs (IntelliJ, PyCharm) and the Kotlin language, built without VC
companies.story: Three engineers started JetBrains in Prague in 2000 and grew it with paid developer tools, never raising outside capital. Its Kotlin language became Google's preferred language for Android in 2019.

companies.o: Expressive social robot for the home from MIT's Cynthia Breazeal
companies.story: Jibo was crowdfunded in 2014 and shipped in 2017 at $899 after delays, by which time far cheaper Amazon Echo and Google Home speakers did more. The company's assets went to a lender in 2018, and when its servers were shut down the robots told owners goodbye.

companies.o: Digital temp-staffing agency matching workers with warehouse, logistics and retail shifts
companies.story: Jobandtalent started as a job board, then became a tech-run temp agency that employs workers directly, avoiding the gig-classification fights hitting Uber and Glovo. E-commerce logistics demand during COVID drove a $500M SoftBank-led round in 2021 at $2.35B.

companies.o: 15-minute grocery delivery from dark stores; after exiting five markets it survives only as Daki in Brazil
companies.story: Ralf Wenzel's JOKR launched in 2021 promising 15-minute grocery delivery from dark stores in New York and Latin America, merged with Brazil's Daki and became a unicorn with a $260M round at a $1.2B valuation in December 2021 (after a R$870M / $170M first round). As funding dried up it pulled out of the US (June 2022), Santiago and Medellin (November 2022) and Mexico (February 2023), then raised about $50M in 2023 at an $800M valuation to focus only on Brazil. Daki kept operating and later reports describe it as breakeven, with iFood taking a minority stake; total_raised counts only the reported rounds.

companies.o: Internet TV service from the Skype founders using peer-to-peer streaming
companies.story: Joost raised $45M from CBS, Viacom, Sequoia and Index to stream licensed TV through a downloadable P2P app. Users preferred YouTube and Hulu in the browser and studios held back content; it abandoned its app in 2008 and was sold to ad network Adconion in 2009.

companies.o: Foundation model for weather and energy supply-demand forecasting
companies.story: Jua raised a $16M seed in February 2024 co-led by 468 Capital and the Green Generation Fund, then a EUR10M Series A co-led by Ananda Impact Ventures and Future Energy Ventures (undated in snippets).

companies.o: LLM-powered candidate search and AI recruiting agent
companies.story: Juicebox raised a $30M Series A from Sequoia in September 2025 and an $80M Series B at $850M led by DST Global in March 2026. Total is the $36M reported after Series A plus the Series B.

companies.o: Wi-Fi-connected juice press that squeezed proprietary produce packs
companies.story: Juicero raised about $120M from investors including Google Ventures to sell a $699 connected juice press with subscription produce packs. In April 2017 Bloomberg showed the packs could be squeezed by hand just as well, and the company shut down that September.

companies.o: Rocket Internet's pan-African Amazon-style marketplace
companies.story: Rocket Internet launched Jumia in Lagos in 2012 and rolled it across Africa with MTN and other backers. It listed on the NYSE in April 2019 at about $1.1B, the first African tech IPO in New York, but has never been profitable, and in December 2023 it shut its food delivery arm in all 7 markets.

companies.o: Jumia's restaurant food-delivery service across seven African countries
companies.story: Started under Rocket Internet's Hellofood brand and later run as Jumia Food, the service offered restaurant delivery in Nigeria, Kenya, Morocco and four other markets. Low order values and high delivery costs kept it loss-making and Jumia shut it in all seven countries in December 2023 to focus on e-commerce.

companies.o: Mexico's store-less digital supermarket delivering groceries from its own warehouses
companies.story: Ricardo Weder's Jüsto sold groceries online in Mexico with no physical stores, raising a $152M Series B led by General Atlantic in 2022 that El Financiero billed as minting a new Mexican unicorn, and expanding to Peru. After a $70M equity-plus-debt raise in October 2024 it wound down Peru, then announced it would stop operating in Mexico on 15 December 2025, citing financial, operating and strategic factors and struggling to make the model profitable. Weeks later, in January 2026, OMNi took over the brand and relaunched it, so the original venture ended in a rescue rather than an exit.

companies.o: Builds very large, high-power satellite buses designed for the cheap heavy-lift launch era.
companies.story: Brothers Karan and Neel Kunjur left SpaceX in 2022 betting that Starship-class launch would make big, powerful satellites cheap to fly, so the bottleneck would become the satellites themselves. Its valuation went from about $1.5B in February 2025 to $3B with a $250M Series C in December 2025 and $6.8B with a $500M Series D co-led by Kleiner Perkins and ICONIQ in July 2026, taking funding to about $1B.

companies.o: Agentic AI credit intelligence platform for small business lending
companies.story: Kaaj raised a $3.8M seed led by Kindred Ventures in November 2025. It automates credit risk analysis for small business lenders.

companies.o: Builds fluoride-salt-cooled advanced reactors; signed the first corporate SMR deal with Google.
companies.story: Founded by UC Berkeley nuclear engineers, Kairos took an iterative, build-and-test approach and won NRC construction permits for its Hermes test reactors in Oak Ridge, Tennessee in 2023 and 2024. In October 2024 Google agreed to buy up to 500MW from Kairos reactors by 2035, the first corporate deal of its kind; its funding has been largely undisclosed.

companies.o: AI for insurance underwriting, pricing and portfolio management
companies.story: Kalepa raised a $75M Series B at $470M led by Updata Partners, announced in November 2026. Customers include W.R. Berkley, Bowhead Specialty and AmRisc.

companies.o: Tech-driven construction company that tried to own the whole building supply chain
companies.story: Katerra tried to vertically integrate construction, from design to its own factories for building components, raising about $2B mostly from SoftBank. It expanded factories and acquisitions faster than it could deliver projects profitably, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in June 2021.

companies.o: Peer-to-peer file-sharing app used to swap music and video
companies.story: Built by Niklas Zennström and Janus Friis with Estonian developers, Kazaa became one of the most downloaded programs in the world after Napster's fall. Lawsuits from music and film companies led its owner to pay about $100M in a 2006 settlement and the service faded; its founders reused the P2P tech to create Skype.

companies.o: Anonymous messaging app popular with teens that bet on its own crypto token
companies.story: Founded by University of Waterloo students, Kik grew to hundreds of millions of registered users and took $50M from Tencent at a $1B valuation in 2015. Losing ground to WhatsApp and Snapchat, it raised about $100M selling its Kin crypto token in 2017; the SEC sued over the sale in 2019, and Kik sold the messenger app to MediaLab that year.

companies.o: Teleoperation-plus-AI picking robots for e-commerce warehouses, bought by Ocado
companies.story: Started by D-Wave veterans Suzanne Gildert and Geordie Rose (who later founded Sanctuary AI), Kindred used human teleoperators to train robot arms with reinforcement learning, then deployed its SORT robots to sort e-commerce orders for customers like Gap. UK online grocer Ocado bought it in November 2020 for about $262M to add AI picking to its warehouse platform.

companies.o: Converted wood chips into renewable crude oil
companies.story: Khosla Ventures-backed KiOR went public in 2011 promising cheap gasoline and diesel from wood biomass. Its Mississippi plant produced far less fuel than planned at uncompetitive cost, and it filed for bankruptcy in November 2014.

companies.o: AI-powered code completion for programmers
companies.story: Kite offered machine-learning code completion years before ChatGPT and gained hundreds of thousands of users. Its founder said in a 2022 farewell post that the AI was not yet good enough to change how developers work and that developers would not pay; it shut down months before AI coding tools like Cursor took off.

companies.o: CAR-T cell therapies for blood cancers
companies.story: Founded by serial entrepreneur Arie Belldegrun, Kite licensed CAR-T technology from the National Cancer Institute and went public in 2014. Strong lymphoma trial results led Gilead to buy it for $11.9B in 2017, just before its first therapy was approved.

companies.o: Cloud kitchen operator cooking for partner restaurant brands
companies.story: Kitopi runs shared kitchens that cook for established restaurant brands (and its own) across the Gulf, using software to manage many menus in one kitchen. SoftBank led a $415M round in 2021 that made it a unicorn, while many US and African cloud-kitchen startups shut.

companies.o: Colombian-founded maker of cheap campus food-delivery robots
companies.story: Colombian founders started Kiwibot at UC Berkeley, keeping costs low with simple robots and remote supervisors based in Colombia, and found its niche delivering food on US college campuses, including through Sodexo. It drew criticism when that remote-piloting model became public, and it has stayed small; CB Insights lists the company, now trading as Robot, raising about $18M in February 2026.

companies.o: Buy-now-pay-later checkout and shopping app
companies.story: Klarna started in 2005 letting Swedes pay online by invoice after delivery, then became Europe's BNPL leader with a banking licence for cheap funding. Valued at $45.6B in 2021, it raised at just $6.7B in 2022 as rates rose, then listed on the NYSE in September 2025 at about $15B.

companies.o: Adaptive-learning engine that personalized digital coursework
companies.story: Knewton raised well over $100M promising an adaptive-learning engine that would personalize education, licensed through publishers like Pearson. The publisher partnerships disappointed, a pivot to its own courseware did not grow fast enough, and Wiley bought its assets in 2019 for a reported fraction of the money raised.

companies.o: Autonomous trucking company that listed via de-SPAC
companies.story: Kodiak went public through a de-SPAC that secured more than $275M including $145M PIPE at a reported $2.5B valuation. It is one of the few AV truck survivors that reached public markets.

companies.o: Nigerian online marketplace that raced Jumia to be the Amazon of Africa
companies.story: Backed by Naspers and Kinnevik (reported totals $78-108M), Konga was valued at $383M in 2015 while burning cash against Rocket Internet's Jumia. In 2018 both investors sold to local electronics firm Zinox for an undisclosed price that Naspers filings imply was at most ~$32M, booking a loss.

companies.o: Multilingual Indian microblogging app positioned as a homegrown Twitter alternative
companies.story: Koo surged in 2021 when Indian ministers adopted it during the government's spat with Twitter, raising $50-65M from Tiger Global, Accel, Kalaari and Blume and peaking at about $285M. Monthly actives fell from 9.4M in mid-2022 to about 3.1M by April 2023 as political interest faded and ads never paid for the servers. After buyout talks with Dailyhunt and others collapsed, it shut down in July 2024.

companies.o: Serverless AI inference platform
companies.story: Mistral AI agreed in February 2026 to acquire Koyeb, an independent serverless inference platform. Price not found.

companies.o: Free one-hour bike-courier delivery of snacks, videos and convenience goods
companies.story: Kozmo promised free delivery of small items like ice cream and DVDs within an hour, expanding to multiple US cities with about 1,100 staff. It raised about $280M, including $60M from Amazon, but small orders with no delivery fee never covered courier costs, and it shut down in April 2001 after a planned IPO was cancelled.

companies.o: Ola founder Bhavish Aggarwal's Indic AI lab, India's first AI unicorn, later shrunk to an AI cloud
companies.story: Krutrim became India's first AI unicorn in January 2024 after a $50M round at $1B, promising Indic-language LLMs and an AI cloud. The models drew little use; Aggarwal pledged Ola Electric shares to raise debt for it, and by 2026 it had pulled its Kruti assistant, cut most of its staff and pivoted to AI cloud infrastructure.

near.what: Headcount fell from 550+ (Aug 2025) to about 150; consumer assistant Kruti pulled from app stores and a second layoff round cut almost half of remaining staff

companies.o: Foundation models for business predictions
companies.story: Nvidia acquired the roughly four-year-old Kumo AI in June 2026, per Fortune. Price was not disclosed.

companies.o: Nairobi cloud kitchen selling affordable ready-to-eat meals by delivery
companies.story: Kune raised a $1M pre-seed (with a launch PR controversy over its founder's comments on Kenyan food culture) and ran cloud kitchens in Nairobi. When a promised follow-on investment was withdrawn in 2022 it ran out of money and shut after 10 months, laying off 90 staff.

companies.o: Generative AI tutoring with interactive video
companies.story: Kyron raised a $14.6M Series A in December 2023 led by Global Silicon Valley Ventures.

companies.o: LLM security and prompt-injection defense acquired by Check Point
companies.story: Check Point announced its acquisition of Lakera in September 2025 for a reported $300M. Forrester counts it among eight vendors that spent over $2B buying AI-security startups in about 18 months.

companies.o: GPU cloud for AI training and inference
companies.story: Lambda raised a $320M Series C in 2024, a $480M Series D with Nvidia participating, then over $1.5B in late 2025, and exited GPU hardware sales in August 2025 to prioritise its cloud. Leads were not named in snippets.

companies.o: Chinese private launcher that flew the world's first methane-fuelled rocket to orbit and is chasing reusability with Zhuque-3.
companies.story: LandSpace's first rocket, Zhuque-1, failed in 2018 and Zhuque-2 failed on its December 2022 debut, but in July 2023 Zhuque-2 became the first methane-fuelled rocket to reach orbit, ahead of SpaceX and Blue Origin. Zhuque-3 reached orbit on its first flight in December 2025 though the booster landing failed, and the company, having raised more than 7B yuan (about $1B), filed to raise about 7.5B yuan on Shanghai's STAR Market after the exchange waived profitability rules for rocket makers; no listing was confirmed by late 2026.

near.what: Zhuque-1, the first orbital attempt by a Chinese private company, failed
Zhuque-2 failed on its debut before succeeding in 2023

companies.o: Builds small, factory-made pressurized-water microreactors for industrial and data-center customers.
companies.story: Founded by Bret Kugelmass, Last Energy shrinks conventional pressurized-water reactor technology into 20MW units built in factories, initially pitching European customers. It raised $40M in 2024 ($64M total) and a $100M+ Series C led by the Astera Institute in December 2025, aiming for its PWR-5 pilot at Texas A&M to go critical in 2026.

companies.o: Swedish legal AI platform and Harvey's main rival
companies.story: Legora raised a $550M Series D led by Accel at $5.55B in 2026 and made its fifth acquisition of the year by September. Crunchbase reported it tripled its valuation to become a legal tech unicorn.

companies.o: App-based renters and home insurance with an AI claims bot
companies.story: Lemonade sold renters insurance to young customers through a chatbot and promised to give unclaimed premiums to charity. Its July 2020 IPO raised $319M and more than doubled on day one; it later bought struggling car insurer Metromile.

companies.o: Vertically integrated eyewear brand selling online and through thousands of own stores
companies.story: Peyush Bansal started Lenskart online in 2010 but won by building its own lens manufacturing and a large chain of stores, turning a fragmented optician market into a branded D2C business. It listed on 10 November 2025 via a Rs 7,278 crore IPO (~$841M) that valued it at about Rs 69,700 crore (~$8.1B) at the issue price; the stock swung sharply on debut and closed roughly flat.

companies.o: Speech-recognition and translation software company
companies.story: Lernout & Hauspie was Belgium's tech champion of the 1990s, buying Dragon Systems and others to lead speech recognition. In 2000 the Wall Street Journal exposed fake revenue in its Korean unit; it went bankrupt, its founders were later convicted and its technology passed to ScanSoft, later Nuance.

companies.o: Barcelona-built second-hand marketplace app that bet on the US market
companies.story: Letgo was built in Barcelona by OLX founder Alec Oxenford and others and raised close to $1B, mostly from Naspers, to take on OfferUp and Craigslist in the US with heavy TV advertising. Facebook Marketplace launched in 2016 and squeezed it; in 2020 Letgo's US business was merged into OfferUp and the app shut down.

companies.o: Long-range solar electric car from an Eindhoven solar-racing team
companies.story: Lightyear built the Lightyear 0, a solar car priced around €250,000, planning a cheaper mass-market model later. It could not fund production of the second car and its main operating company went bankrupt in January 2023; a smaller successor now sells solar roof technology.

companies.o: Electric vertical take-off jet for regional air-taxi routes
companies.story: Lilium listed via SPAC in 2021 at about $3.3B with a novel ducted-fan jet that had not yet been certified. It repeatedly missed milestones, filed for insolvency in October 2024 after the German government refused a €50M loan guarantee, revived briefly, then ceased operations in February 2025 when a rescue deal collapsed.

companies.o: Dockless shared e-scooters and e-bikes in cities worldwide
companies.story: Lime raced Bird with the same dockless scooter model and hit a $2.4B valuation in 2019. In the 2020 crash Uber led a $170M rescue round at a reported $510M valuation and handed Lime its Jump bike unit; Lime cut costs and kept operating while Bird went bankrupt.

companies.o: AI memory pendant and app (ex-Rewind) recording meetings and conversations
companies.story: Meta acquired Limitless in December 2025 for undisclosed terms, aiming at AI wearables. Limitless stopped selling the $99 pendant and promised a year of support to existing customers.

companies.o: Kenyan buy-now-pay-later provider for electronics and retail purchases
companies.story: Lipa Later raised a $12M pre-Series A (equity plus debt) in 2022 to expand BNPL into Tanzania, Ghana and Nigeria, part of over $15M total. Lending needs constant fresh capital; after failing to raise in 2024 it could not pay staff and suppliers and entered administration in March 2025.

companies.o: MIT spinout building non-Transformer 'liquid' foundation models for efficient on-device AI
companies.story: Spun out of MIT CSAIL in 2023 by Ramin Hasani, Mathias Lechner, Alexander Amini and Daniela Rus, Liquid AI builds 'liquid' foundation models based on dynamical-systems research rather than Transformers. AMD Ventures led a $250M Series A in December 2024 that valued it at over $2B (trackers range from $2.28B to $2.4B). Its LFM models target phones, cars and other edge devices where memory and power are tight.

companies.o: Daily-deals rival to Groupon backed by Amazon
companies.story: LivingSocial was Groupon's closest US rival and took a $175M investment from Amazon in 2010, reaching a multibillion-dollar valuation. As the daily-deals boom faded it shrank through layoffs, and Groupon bought it in 2016 for an undisclosed price far below its peak.

companies.o: Autonomous mobile robots that guide warehouse pickers, rented per robot per month
companies.story: Locus began as the in-house robotics team of 3PL Quiet Logistics, then spun out to sell cart-like mobile robots that lead human pickers through warehouses, charged as a subscription. The e-commerce boom carried it to a $117M Series F at about $2B in late 2022, but it cut staff in 2023 and 2024 as warehouse spending cooled, and trackers report an August 2026 Series G of about $41.6M at roughly $1.35B, a down round.

companies.o: Electric pickup maker in a former GM plant in Ohio
companies.story: Lordstown bought a former GM plant and went public via SPAC in 2020 on claims of strong preorders for its Endurance pickup, which a short seller said were largely non-binding. It sold the plant to Foxconn in 2022, built only a handful of trucks, and filed for bankruptcy in June 2023 while suing Foxconn over a failed investment deal.

companies.o: Free AI-led primary care
companies.story: Lotus raised a $35M Series A in February 2026 co-led by Kleiner Perkins and CRV, for $41M total. It offers its care free to patients.

companies.o: Prompt-to-app builder for non-developers
companies.story: Lovable raised a $330M Series B at $6.6B in December 2025 after tripling revenue, then $400M at $13.3B. Both rounds were led by named investors including CapitalG and Menlo Ventures.

companies.o: Digital home and renters insurance with app-based claims
companies.story: Luko grew fast selling home insurance online in France, Spain and Germany. High claims costs and losses led its carrier and regulators to step in; it entered receivership in late 2023, Allianz Direct took over the policies and German insurtech Getsafe bought the company in early 2024.

companies.o: AI video and 3D generation company
companies.story: Luma AI announced a $900M Series C in November 2025 at a $4B valuation. The sources seen did not name the lead.

companies.o: Pioneered satellite-to-ordinary-phone texting, then merged with Omnispace after a failed SPAC to form Elveo Mobile.
companies.story: Lynk sent what it called the first text from a satellite to a standard phone and signed dozens of mobile operators, but as SpaceX's Starlink and AST SpaceMobile moved into direct-to-cell, its 2024 SPAC deal with Slam Corp dragged on and was cancelled amid a legal dispute. In October 2025 it agreed to merge with SES-backed Omnispace, and the combined company closed in August 2026 as Elveo Mobile.

companies.o: SMS-based mobile money service run by Safaricom that became Kenya's default payment rail
companies.story: Safaricom (part-owned by Vodafone) launched M-Pesa in 2007 after a UK-aid-funded pilot, letting people send money by SMS and cash in or out at agents. In a country with few bank branches and a dominant telco it spread fast, but the same product failed in South Africa (shut 2016) where banks were already everywhere.

companies.o: Vodacom's attempt to bring Kenya's M-Pesa mobile money to South Africa
companies.story: Vodacom launched M-Pesa in South Africa in 2010 and relaunched it in 2014 with a Visa card, targeting 10M users. It reached only about 1M registered and 76,000 active users, because South Africans already had bank branches and cards and regulation was stricter than Kenya's; Vodacom shut it on 30 June 2016.

companies.o: Online designer furniture made to order in Asia and shipped direct to buyers
companies.story: Made.com listed in London in June 2021 at £775M (~$1.07B) after a lockdown sales boom. Container shipping costs from Asia soared and demand fell, it failed to raise more money and collapsed in November 2022, with Next buying the brand for £3.4M.

companies.o: AI coding startup training long-context models
companies.story: Magic closed a $320M round in August 2024 from Eric Schmidt, CapitalG, Atlassian, Sequoia and others, bringing total funding to about $465M. Its valuation is reported inconsistently, with a $1.5B figure only reported as a target.

companies.o: First Arabic-language email service and web portal
companies.story: Samih Toukan and Hussam Khoury built Arabic webmail and a portal in Amman. Yahoo bought Maktoob in 2009 for about $164M, the Arab world's first big tech exit, and its founders spun off Souq.com, later sold to Amazon.

companies.o: Irish drone delivery service flying food and groceries to suburban homes
companies.story: Founded by serial entrepreneur Bobby Healy, Manna runs on-demand drone delivery from hubs in Dublin's suburbs, carrying takeaways, coffee and groceries in a few minutes. It is one of the few European operators flying at commercial volume and has faced local pushback over noise and planning permission; funding details were not confirmed in sources checked.

companies.o: German laser-driven fusion startup using nanostructured fuel targets and short-pulse lasers.
companies.story: Marvel Fusion bets that ultra-short laser pulses on nanostructured targets can trigger fusion without the huge facilities of government laser labs. Backed by Siemens Energy Ventures and Deutsche Telekom among others, it raised a Series B in 2025 (totals reported at roughly $160-208M) and is building a demonstration facility with Colorado State University for 2027.

companies.o: Pioneering vertical-landing rocket company that went bankrupt trying to deliver a NASA Moon lander.
companies.story: Masten won NASA's Lunar Lander Challenge in 2009 and flew hundreds of vertical-landing test flights, then in 2020 won a $75.9M fixed-price NASA CLPS contract to land its XL-1 at the lunar south pole. Costs and delays outran the contract, and it filed for Chapter 11 in July 2022; rival Astrobotic bought its assets for about $4.5M.

companies.o: Ex-Google/Nest team's camera-based home robot that vacuums and mops with on-device AI
companies.story: Founded as Matician by former Google and Nest engineers Mehul Nariyawala and Navneet Dalal, Matic spent years building a vision-only home robot that maps rooms in 3D and processes everything on the device for privacy, launching at about $1,500. Trackers put its funding at roughly $90M-$107M after a 2025 round and its valuation near $650M; it says it aims to replace the Roomba just as iRobot collapsed.

companies.o: Drone delivery network for hospital lab samples and, later, home delivery
companies.story: Matternet began with drone deliveries in places without roads, then focused on moving lab samples between hospital buildings, including a UPS Flight Forward partnership in the US and hospital networks in Switzerland. It won FAA type certification for its M2 drone in 2022 and has since tried suburban home delivery in Silicon Valley; funding totals were not confirmed in sources checked.

companies.o: LLM-focused accelerator founded by Google alumni
companies.story: MatX raised about $80M in 2024 at a reported $300M-plus valuation and a $500M Series B led by Jane Street and Situational Awareness in Q1 2026. Sources conflict on whether the 2024 round was A or B.

companies.o: Bosch-backed maker of the Kuri home robot, closed before it shipped widely
companies.story: Mayfield came out of Bosch's startup platform to build Kuri, a cute $700 camera-equipped robot meant to roam the home, record family moments and act as a watchful nanny. Bosch could not find a buyer or partner to keep funding it, and Mayfield stopped manufacturing and shut down in 2018, months before Anki and Jibo also collapsed.

companies.o: Zero-commission value e-commerce marketplace that began as a WhatsApp reseller app
companies.story: Meesho started in 2015 as an app for housewives and small resellers to sell products over WhatsApp, then dropped reselling and seller commissions to become a low-price marketplace for smaller-town shoppers. Unlike social-commerce peers such as DealShare that shrank after 2022, it cut burn hard and listed in December 2025 with a Rs 5,421 crore IPO (~$627M); shares jumped about 46% on debut.

companies.o: AI recruiting platform founded by 21-year-olds that matches talent to jobs
companies.story: Mercor raised a $30M Series A at $250M in September 2024, then a $100M Series B at $2B in February 2025. Valuation rose eightfold in five months.

companies.o: Online supermarket delivering groceries from its own dark stores in Colombia, Mexico and Brazil
companies.story: Merqueo built a Bogotá online supermarket with its own warehouses and expanded to Mexico and Brazil while talking up a US IPO. It closed Mexico in June 2022, entered Colombian business reorganisation in May 2023 with about COP 25.2bn (~$5.8M at 2023 rates) of pending obligations, and in July 2025 shut its stores and switched off its app after failing to secure new financing. Total raised is CB Insights' estimate; it also had a reported $22M IDB financing for Brazil.

companies.o: Pay-per-mile car insurance using a plug-in tracking device
companies.story: Metromile charged drivers by the mile using a device in their car and went public via SPAC in early 2021. High claims losses and a crashing share price led it to sell to Lemonade in an all-stock deal announced at about $500M, far below its SPAC valuation, which closed in 2022.

companies.o: Shanghai lab behind Hailuo video, the Talkie companion app and open-weight MiniMax models
companies.story: Founded in 2021 by ex-SenseTime executive Yan Junjie, MiniMax earned unusually much from consumer apps abroad (Talkie) and its Hailuo video model. It listed in Hong Kong on 9 January 2026, a day after Zhipu, at a pre-listing value of more than HK$50B, and its shares jumped as much as 100% on debut. By June 2026 it traded at about HK$180B (about $23B) and had fallen behind Zhipu.

companies.o: Free app that pulled all your bank accounts into one budget view
companies.story: Mint automatically synced users' bank and card accounts through an aggregator and categorized spending, while rival Wesabe asked users to upload data manually. Intuit bought Mint for $170M in 2009, about two years after launch; Intuit shut the app in 2024 and moved users to Credit Karma.

companies.o: ICQ, one of the first mass-market internet instant messengers
companies.story: Four young Israelis and investor Yossi Vardi launched ICQ in 1996 and it reached tens of millions of users without revenue. AOL bought Mirabilis in 1998 for $407M, a landmark exit that helped launch Israel's startup ecosystem.

companies.o: European foundation-model lab releasing open-weight and commercial LLMs
companies.story: Founded by ex-DeepMind and Meta researchers, Mistral raised a then-record €105M seed four weeks after founding in 2023. Positioned as Europe's sovereign AI champion, it raised €1.7B led by chipmaker ASML in 2025 at €11.7B (~$13.7B).

companies.o: Dockless smart-lock bike-sharing app with GPS-connected orange bikes

rounds.lead: Hillhouse Capital, Warburg Pincus, Sequoia China

companies.story: Mobike built GPS-tracked smart-lock bikes and fought ofo city by city, raising five rounds in three years led by Tencent. Bleeding cash in the subsidy war, it was sold in April 2018 to Tencent-backed Meituan Dianping for a reported $2.7B equity value plus about RMB4.5B ($700M) of assumed debt, a deal brokered by Tencent's Pony Ma; Meituan later folded it into Meituan Bike.

companies.o: Camera-based driver-assistance chips and computer vision for carmakers
companies.story: Professor Amnon Shashua's Mobileye spent a decade getting its vision chips designed into cars, then had the largest Israeli IPO on the NYSE in 2014 at about $5.3B. Intel bought it in 2017 for $15.3B and spun it back out in a 2022 IPO.

companies.o: mRNA medicines platform company
companies.story: Created by Flagship Pioneering, Moderna raised billions privately to build an mRNA platform before any product was approved, then raised $604M in a December 2018 IPO, the largest biotech IPO at the time. Its platform let it design a COVID-19 vaccine within days in 2020, turning it into one of the pandemic's biggest winners.

companies.o: Indie studio behind Minecraft, bootstrapped from game sales
companies.story: Markus Persson sold Minecraft while it was still in alpha and funded Mojang entirely from sales, turning down VC. Microsoft bought Mojang in 2014 for $2.5B.

companies.o: Orbital 'space tug' startup whose SPAC listing unravelled amid SEC charges, national-security issues and failed missions.
companies.story: Momentus promised water-plasma-powered space tugs and merged with SPAC Stable Road in 2021 at about $1.2B, but its Russian-born co-founder Mikhail Kokorich was forced out over US national-security concerns, and the SEC charged the company, Kokorich and the SPAC with misleading investors about its technology tests (settled). Its Vigoride missions underperformed, the stock lost over 99% of its value, it flagged going-concern doubts in 2025 and did a 1-for-17.85 reverse split in December 2025 while raising money in $4-5M slices.

near.what: SEC charges and CFIUS-driven exit of the founders during the SPAC process
Going-concern warning; reverse split to keep its Nasdaq listing

companies.o: Visual work-management platform for teams
companies.story: Started as an internal tool at Wix, monday.com (originally dapulse) grew with heavy online advertising into a horizontal work OS. It was valued at $1.9B in 2019 and listed on Nasdaq in June 2021 at about $6.8B.

companies.o: Payments and banking platform for Nigerian small businesses and POS agents
companies.story: Started as TeamApt building bank software, Moniepoint pivoted to POS terminals and business accounts for Nigerian merchants and agents. It says it processes over 800M transactions a month while profitable, and its $110M Series C in 2024 (with Google's Africa fund) valued it at $1B.

companies.o: Beijing lab behind the Kimi chatbot and the open-weight Kimi K2 models
companies.story: Founded in 2023 by Yang Zhilin, Moonshot won early users with Kimi's long context window, then lost ground in China's 2024 chatbot ad war. Its open-weight Kimi K2 (July 2025) became a global favourite for agentic coding, and its valuation went from $4.3B at the end of 2025 to about $35B by July 2026 as annualised revenue reportedly reached $300M. A Hong Kong IPO is reported for 2027.

companies.o: AI video startup
companies.story: SEC filings showed Moonvalley raising $43M in April 2025 and about $53M in total by May 2025. Investors were not named in the snippets seen.

companies.o: Public-transit journey planner covering thousands of cities
companies.story: Moovit used crowdsourcing and local volunteer 'Mooviters' to map transit in far more cities than rivals like Citymapper. Intel bought it in 2020 for about $900M to pair with Mobileye's robotaxi plans.

companies.o: Tools for companies to train their own large language models cheaply
companies.story: MosaicML helped companies train their own language models efficiently and released open models just as generative AI took off. Databricks bought it for $1.3B in June 2023, about two years after its founding.

companies.o: Monthly subscription for going to the movies in theaters
companies.story: After data firm Helios and Matheson took control in 2017, MoviePass cut its price to $9.95 a month for a movie a day while paying theaters full ticket price, and subscribers jumped past 3 million. Losses exploded, the service shut down in 2019 and its parent filed for bankruptcy in early 2020; a co-founder later bought back the brand and relaunched it.

companies.o: Japanese maker of a universal robot controller that lets any industrial arm pick and palletize without programming
companies.story: Founded in Tokyo in 2011 by Issei Takino and CMU-trained motion-planning researcher Rosen Diankov, Mujin sells MujinController, which lets robot arms from any maker plan their own motions to pick, depalletize and pack.
