It raised an $85M Series C in 2023 (extended to $104M) led by SBI, then announced a first close of about 36.4B yen (~$233M, equity plus debt) in December 2025 co-led by NTT Group and Qatar Investment Authority to move from integration projects to a product-led model.

companies.o: Delivery of chef-prepared meals cooked in central kitchens
companies.story: Munchery cooked meals in its own kitchens and expanded to Seattle, Los Angeles and New York before pulling back and laying off 257 people in 2018. It shut down abruptly in January 2019 after raising about $125M, leaving some suppliers unpaid.

companies.o: Customizable-profile social network popular with musicians
companies.story: Myspace became the most visited US social network by letting anyone customize profiles and by courting bands, and News Corp bought its parent Intermix for $580M in 2005. Spam, clutter and an ad-heavy redesign pushed users to Facebook, and News Corp sold Myspace for about $35M in 2011.

companies.o: Company behind the open-source MySQL database
companies.story: MySQL became the default database of the early web through free open-source distribution, earning money from dual licences and support. Sun Microsystems bought MySQL AB for $1B in 2008, a landmark open-source exit.

companies.o: Mobile-only bank account with a German banking licence passported across the EU
companies.story: N26 got a German banking licence and grew across the eurozone, reaching a $9B valuation in 2021. It left the UK in 2020 after Brexit and the US in January 2022, and German regulator BaFin capped its customer growth in 2021 over anti-money-laundering failings.

companies.o: N26's mobile bank account offering in the United States
companies.story: N26 launched in the US in 2019 through a partner bank, without its own US licence, into a market already crowded with Chime, Varo and big banks' apps. It closed US accounts in January 2022 to focus on Europe, having already quit the UK in 2020.

companies.o: Peer-to-peer MP3 file-sharing service
companies.story: Napster let tens of millions of people swap MP3s for free, becoming one of the fastest-growing apps ever. Record labels sued for copyright infringement, a court injunction shut the service in 2001, and the company went bankrupt in 2002 with its brand sold off.

companies.o: Diversified mobile gaming, esports and kids-learning games group
companies.story: Nitish Mittersain started Nazara in 2000 making mobile games for feature-phone carriers, then bought into esports (Nodwin) and kids' learning (Kiddopia) rather than betting on real-money gaming. Backed by Rakesh Jhunjhunwala, it became India's first listed gaming company in March 2021 with a Rs 583 crore IPO (~$79M at 73.9) at Rs 1,101 and listed roughly 80% higher.

companies.o: Lidar robot-vacuum pioneer bought by Vorwerk and shut down six years later
companies.story: Neato brought low-cost laser navigation to robot vacuums years before it became standard, competing with iRobot from Silicon Valley. German appliance maker Vorwerk bought it in 2017 on undisclosed terms, but as cheaper Chinese rivals took the market, Vorwerk shut Neato down in 2023.

companies.o: Ad-free, subscription search engine from Google's former ads chief
companies.story: Former Google ads head Sridhar Ramaswamy built Neeva as a private, ad-free search engine and added AI answers early. Few users paid to switch from Google, it shut its consumer search in 2023 and Snowflake acquired the company; Ramaswamy became Snowflake's CEO in 2024.

companies.o: Chinese maker of small driverless delivery vans used by couriers and retailers
companies.story: Neolix builds small Level-4 driverless vans that run on Chinese city roads for couriers, supermarkets and retailers, helped by local governments granting road permits that US sidewalk-robot firms lacked. In October 2025 it raised over $600M in a Series D led by UAE-based StoneVenture, a record private round for China's autonomous-driving sector, after delivering more than 10,000 vehicles and over 2,000 a month.

companies.o: Lead-cooled small fast reactors that run on recycled nuclear waste fuel.
companies.story: Founded in London in 2021 by physicist-entrepreneur Stefano Buono and later headquartered in Paris, Newcleo raised hundreds of millions of euros unusually early (totals reported at EUR487-645M) and was valued at about EUR1.5B in 2024 (about $1.6B). It raised a EUR75M (about $88M) Series B in early 2026 and was reported to be pursuing a Nasdaq listing through a SPAC at about $2.4B, a figure not confirmed by primary sources.

companies.o: Hydrogen and battery-electric semi-truck startup
companies.story: Nikola went public via SPAC in June 2020 and was briefly worth more than Ford before a Hindenburg Research report showed a promotional video of its truck had been rolled down a hill. Founder Trevor Milton was convicted of fraud in 2022 (and later pardoned in 2025), and the company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in February 2025.

companies.o: Builds fully robotic fulfillment centers that pick and pack e-commerce orders
companies.story: Stanford PhD dropout Simon Kalouche started Nimble to build warehouses run by its own picking robots, with remote humans stepping in when the AI fails. In October 2024 it closed a $106M Series C led by FedEx, also a customer, and co-led by Cedar Pine, at a $1B post-money valuation.

companies.o: Security and governance platform for AI applications and autonomous agents
companies.story: Noma, founded in 2023, left stealth in 2024 with a $32M Series A led by Ballistic Ventures (another source says $25M). It raised a $100M Series B led by Evolution Equity Partners on July 31, 2025.

companies.o: Israeli no-code AI analytics platform
companies.story: Noogata raised about $28M (one roundup's figure). It missed key business milestones, could not raise another round and announced in May 2025 it would shut down and try to sell its technology.

companies.o: Swedish lithium-ion battery maker building gigafactories to give Europe its own green EV-battery champion.
companies.story: Co-founded by ex-Tesla executive Peter Carlsson, Northvolt set out to build Europe's answer to Asian battery giants with a flagship gigafactory (Northvolt Ett) in Skellefteå, raising more than $14 billion in equity, debt and public funding (Sifted counts about EUR 15bn) from backers led by Volkswagen (about 21%) and Goldman Sachs. With liquidity described as dire in its own petition and roughly $5.8bn of debt, it filed for US Chapter 11 on 21 November 2024 as Carlsson resigned, then filed for bankruptcy in Sweden in March 2025; US startup Lyten agreed in August 2025 to buy the remaining Swedish and German plants and IP for undisclosed terms. Peak private valuation was not confirmed in sources checked, so it is left null.

near.what: Filed for Chapter 11 in the Southern District of Texas on 21 Nov 2024 with about $145M of cash collateral and $100M of DIP financing; co-founder and CEO Peter Carlsson resigned; Volkswagen and Goldman Sachs wrote down their stakes.

companies.o: AI accounting automation for finance teams' close and reporting
companies.story: Numeric raised $10M in May 2024, a $28M Series A led by Menlo in October 2024, and a $51M Series B led by IVP in November 2025. Total funding is reported at about $89M.

companies.o: Mobile bank account combining euro banking with bitcoin trading
companies.story: Bitwala rebranded as Nuri in 2020 and grew to roughly half a million customers by mixing a bank account (via partner Solarisbank) with bitcoin. When crypto prices crashed and fundraising froze in 2022 it filed for insolvency that August and wound down.

companies.o: Driverless delivery-pod maker that pivoted to licensing its self-driving stack for Uber robotaxis
companies.story: Ex-Waymo engineers Dave Ferguson and Jiajun Zhu founded Nuro to build small driverless pods for groceries and takeout, raised $940M from SoftBank in 2019 and peaked at $8.6B in 2021. Deliveries never scaled; it laid off staff in 2022 and 2023, pivoted in 2024 to licensing its Nuro Driver software, and in 2025 closed a $203M Series E at $6B (a 30% markdown) with Uber and Nvidia while agreeing to power at least 20,000 Lucid robotaxis on Uber's network.

near.what: Second round of layoffs and paused vehicle production; pivot from operating delivery pods to licensing its driving software

companies.o: Small modular reactor developer with the first US NRC-approved SMR design.
companies.story: NuScale spun out of Oregon State University in 2007, became the first SMR design certified by the NRC, and listed via SPAC in 2022 at about $1.9B. Its flagship Utah project with UAMPS was cancelled in November 2023 when estimated power prices rose and utilities pulled out; after an uprated design approval in 2025 and a 6GW agreement involving TVA the stock soared, then fell nearly 80% from its July 2025 high to about a $3.6-4B market cap in 2026.

near.what: First customer project (UAMPS Carbon Free Power Project) cancelled; layoffs followed

companies.o: Inventory-led online beauty and personal-care retailer with its own brands and stores
companies.story: Former banker Falguni Nayar launched Nykaa in 2012 to sell authentic beauty products online by holding inventory, avoiding the counterfeit problem of open marketplaces, and it was profitable before listing. Its November 2021 Rs 5,352 crore IPO (~$724M at 73.9) listed ~79% above issue and closed day one at a market cap of about Rs 1.04 lakh crore (~$14B), making Nayar India's richest self-made woman.

companies.o: Online-only supermarket with robotic warehouses, later licensed to grocers worldwide
companies.story: Founded in 2000 by ex-Goldman bankers just as Webvan was collapsing in the US, Ocado partnered with Waitrose for products and spent a decade building automated central warehouses in one dense market. It listed in London in 2010 at about £937M (~$1.45B), then sold its robotics platform to grocers like Kroger from 2018.

companies.o: Inference API and model optimization platform (formerly OctoML)
companies.story: OctoAI raised $132M at a $900M valuation in late 2021, then sold to Nvidia at roughly 18 cents on the dollar of that peak by one review's estimate. Its inference API was sunset after the deal.

companies.o: Green energy supplier running on its own Kraken billing and operations platform
companies.story: Founded the same year as Bulb, Octopus built its own Kraken software and licensed it to other utilities, and survived the 2021 energy crisis that killed dozens of UK suppliers. It absorbed Bulb's customers in 2022 and became the UK's largest household supplier, raising $800M at $7.8B in 2023.

companies.o: Dockless yellow bike-sharing app unlocked by smartphone, started on Peking University campus
companies.story: ofo raised more than $2.2B in eight rounds from 2015-2018 (Alibaba, Didi, DST) and flooded Chinese and foreign cities with millions of cheap bikes in a subsidy war with Mobike. Bikes were vandalised and lost, rides were nearly free, and a takeover by investor Didi was resisted by the founder; by 2018-19 a Tianjin court found it had basically no assets while roughly 12 million users queued for deposit refunds worth about $170M. Seed/Series C figures from Pandaily; C post-money is the reported $370M pre-money plus $130M.

companies.o: Advanced fast-reactor company (Aurora powerhouse) backed by Sam Altman, listed via his SPAC.
companies.story: Oklo's first licence application was denied by the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission in 2022 for missing information, yet it listed in May 2024 via AltC, the SPAC co-led by Sam Altman, with no reactor built and no revenue. AI data-center power hype sent the stock up more than 1,000% from early 2024 at one point in 2025; in 2026 the market cap was around $10-11B, still without an operating plant.

near.what: NRC denied its first combined licence application for the Aurora reactor

companies.o: Open-banking API connecting Nigerian bank accounts to apps (Plaid for Africa)
companies.story: Okra pioneered open-banking APIs in Nigeria before the central bank's open-banking rules went live, raising about $16.5M. After a 2024 pivot into cloud services it closed in May 2025 and returned roughly $4-5.5M of unused cash to investors.

companies.o: Electric scooter maker selling direct to consumers from a mega-factory in Tamil Nadu
companies.story: Spun out of Ola by Bhavish Aggarwal, Ola Electric built a huge scooter factory and sold online to ride India's EV subsidy wave, briefly becoming the country's top e-two-wheeler seller. Its August 2024 Rs 6,145 crore IPO (~$734M at 83.7) listed flat at Rs 76 and hit the upper circuit for a market cap of about Rs 40,200 crore (~$4.8B). It then stumbled on service complaints, regulatory notices and lost market share to TVS, Bajaj and Ather, and the stock fell far below its issue price.

companies.o: AI 'digital workforce' automating hospital billing and admin tasks
companies.story: Olive raised about $852M, more than any health IT startup before it, to automate hospital revenue-cycle work, hitting a $4B valuation in 2021. Its products spread across too many tasks without delivering consistent results, and after failing to raise more it sold two units to Waystar and Humata Health and shut down on October 31, 2023.

companies.o: Fake cryptocurrency sold through multi-level marketing 'education packages'
companies.story: OneCoin claimed to be a bitcoin rival but had no real blockchain; it sold packages to millions of investors through MLM networks, raising about $4B according to US prosecutors. Founder Ruja Ignatova vanished in 2017 and remains on the FBI's most-wanted list; co-founder Sebastian Greenwood was sentenced to 20 years.

companies.o: Low-earth-orbit satellite constellation for global broadband
companies.story: OneWeb raised about $3.4B, largely from SoftBank, to build a LEO internet constellation ahead of SpaceX's Starlink. When SoftBank refused more money at the start of COVID it filed for Chapter 11 in March 2020; the UK government and Bharti bought it for $1B and it later merged with Eutelsat.

companies.o: Streamed high-end video games from the cloud to any screen
companies.story: OnLive launched cloud gaming in 2010, running games on its servers and streaming them to players, but needed costly dedicated hardware per concurrent user while few people subscribed. In 2012 it restructured through an assignment for the benefit of creditors that wiped out investors, and Sony bought its patents and shut it in 2015.

companies.o: Opera-founded mobile wallet and POS agent network in Nigeria and Egypt
companies.story: OPay launched as part of Opera's Nigerian super-app with ride-hailing (ORide), food and logistics. After Lagos banned bike-hailing in 2020 it shut the side bets and focused on payments and POS agents, then raised $400M at $2B led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 in 2021.

companies.o: AI lab behind ChatGPT and the GPT models
companies.story: OpenAI began as a nonprofit research lab in 2015, created a capped-profit arm to raise money from Microsoft, and launched ChatGPT in November 2022, the fastest-growing consumer app of its time. A 2025 funding round led by SoftBank valued it at $300B, and a share sale later that year reportedly valued it at $500B.

near.what: Board fired CEO Sam Altman; most staff threatened to quit for Microsoft until he was reinstated five days later

companies.o: Buys homes instantly with algorithmic offers and resells them
companies.story: Opendoor made instant cash offers on homes and resold them, going public in December 2020 through Chamath Palihapitiya's SPAC at about $4.8B. When Zillow tried the same model it shut its iBuying arm in 2021 after big losses, while Opendoor kept going despite heavy losses of its own in the housing downturn.

companies.o: Scottish small-launch startup building the low-carbon Prime rocket for a UK spaceport.
companies.story: Orbex raised about GBP138.5M (roughly $175M; GBP105M equity plus GBP33M grants) over a decade, much of it public, including GBP26M of UK government loans in 2025, but never flew its Prime rocket. After closing its Danish engine unit and cutting about 90 jobs in January 2026 and failing to close merger or takeover talks, it entered administration in February 2026 with most of its 163 staff made redundant.

companies.o: Building 'gas stations in space': standard refuelling ports (RAFTI) and fuel tankers for satellites.
companies.story: Orbit Fab bet that satellites will need refuelling and sold its RAFTI docking-and-fuel port as a standard, backed largely by US Space Force and other government contracts. It raised a $28.5M Series A in 2023, cut staff that year as space funding tightened, and in 2026 reportedly named a new CEO and closed a $20M Series B, with its first operational GEO refuelling still to prove the model.

companies.o: Opera-backed motorbike ride-hailing service in Lagos
companies.story: ORide was part of Opera's OPay super-app bet in Nigeria, funded by $170M raised in 2019, and flooded Lagos with subsidised bike rides against Gokada and Max. Lagos banned commercial motorbike hailing in most of the city in early 2020 and ORide shut in mid-2020, while OPay itself pivoted to payments and became a $2B unicorn.

companies.o: Deep-learning software for robot arms that pick and bag e-commerce items
companies.story: OSARO applied deep reinforcement learning to robotic piece-picking, selling software that turns standard arms into e-commerce pick-and-place and bagging stations. It raised a $16M Series B in 2019 and a $30M Series C led by Octave Ventures in 2021, bringing total funding to $67.5M, a modest sum next to the 2024-2026 robot-foundation-model rounds.

companies.o: Tech-first health insurer selling individual plans
companies.story: Oscar launched in 2013 to sell easy-to-use health plans on the new Affordable Care Act exchanges. It raised $1.4B in a March 2021 IPO at about $7.9B, then lost much of that value before reaching profitability years later.

companies.o: Low-code platform for building enterprise applications quickly
companies.story: OutSystems grew slowly for 17 years in Portugal before KKR and Goldman Sachs invested $360M in 2018, making it Portugal's first unicorn. A 2021 round valued it at $9.5B as low-code became a hot category.

companies.o: $99 Android-based TV game console funded on Kickstarter
companies.story: Ouya raised about $8.6M in Kickstarter preorders in 2012 for a cheap open console, one of the platform's biggest campaigns. Players bought few games and developers earned little; Razer acquired its software and team in 2015 and shut the store in 2019.

companies.o: AI digital pathology for cancer diagnosis
companies.story: Paige raised $190M before being acquired by Tempus. The price and closing year were not in the results.

companies.o: Data-integration software for intelligence agencies, militaries and enterprises
companies.story: Co-founded by Peter Thiel with early backing from the CIA's venture arm In-Q-Tel, Palantir sold to government agencies for years when most VCs avoided the sector. It went public by direct listing in September 2020 at about $21B and later became one of the most valuable US software companies.

companies.o: Personalized internet radio built on the Music Genome Project
companies.story: Pandora nearly died after the dot-com crash, with dozens of employees working unpaid for months before new funding arrived in 2004. Its licensed radio model avoided the lawsuits that killed Napster and Grooveshark; it went public in 2011 at about $2.6B and SiriusXM bought it for $3.5B in 2019.

companies.o: Agentic hiring platform connecting companies with recruiters
companies.story: Paraform raised a $40M Series B announced March 18, 2026, bringing total funding to $65M. The snippets name no lead investor.

companies.o: Conversational AI agent platform for enterprise customer service and contact centers
companies.story: Berlin-based Parloa went from a $21M Series A in 2023 to a $350M round in January 2026 at a $3B valuation led by General Catalyst. It became Europe's newest AI unicorn with its May 2025 Series C.

companies.o: Send money by email, built on eBay's marketplace
companies.story: Confinity and Elon Musk's X.com merged in 2000 to form PayPal, which grew virally on eBay with cash referral bonuses while fighting heavy fraud losses. It went public in early 2002 and was bought by eBay later that year for $1.5B.

companies.o: Developer-friendly online payments API for Nigerian businesses
companies.story: Paystack (YC W16) made it easy for Nigerian merchants to accept cards online and was backed by Stripe in its Series A. Stripe bought it in October 2020 for over $200M, the biggest African startup acquisition at the time, after only ~$10M raised.

companies.o: Mobile wallet and QR-code payments super app for Indian consumers and merchants
companies.story: Vijay Shekhar Sharma's Paytm wallet exploded after India's 2016 demonetisation and blanketed merchants with QR codes, reaching a $16B private valuation in 2019 backed by Alibaba/Ant, SoftBank and Berkshire Hathaway. Its November 2021 Rs 18,300 crore IPO (~$2.48B at 73.9), then India's largest, fell about 27% on debut to a market cap near Rs 1.01 lakh crore (~$13.7B), and the RBI's January 2024 curbs on Paytm Payments Bank hit it again.

companies.o: Istanbul mobile game studio behind Toon Blast and Toy Blast
companies.story: Peak Games started with Turkish card games and then hit global success with casual puzzlers Toy Blast and Toon Blast. Zynga bought it in 2020 for $1.8B, then Turkey's largest tech exit, and Peak alumni founded Dream Games.

companies.o: FDA-authorized prescription apps for addiction and insomnia
companies.story: Pear won the first FDA authorization for a prescription digital therapeutic, reSET for substance use disorder, in 2017 and went public via SPAC in 2021. Insurers rarely paid for the apps, so revenue stayed small, and it filed for bankruptcy in April 2023 and sold its assets for a few million dollars.

companies.o: Kickstarter-funded e-paper smartwatch
companies.story: Pebble set Kickstarter records in 2012 and 2015 with its smartwatch preorders, but struggled after Apple Watch launched and smartwatch demand fell short. Fitbit bought its software assets and hired staff in late 2016; Fitbit's filing showed it paid $23M, far below earlier reports of $40M.

companies.o: AI answer engine and AI browser
companies.story: Perplexity went from a $1B valuation in April 2024 to $20B by September 2025 through repeated rounds led by Daniel Gross, IVP and Accel. The lead of the $200M round at $20B was unclear in TechCrunch's report.

companies.o: All-in-one HR and payroll software for small and mid-sized European companies
companies.story: Personio targeted European SMEs that were too small for Workday but faced complex local labour and payroll rules. Its 2022 round valued it at $8.5B, making it one of Germany's most valuable software startups.

companies.o: Online pet supply store famous for its sock-puppet mascot
companies.story: Pets.com sold heavy, low-margin goods like pet food below cost and shipped them nationwide, spending big on Super Bowl-era advertising. It raised $82.5M in a February 2000 IPO at $11 a share, then announced its liquidation in November 2000, about 268 days later, with the stock at $0.19.

companies.o: Remote-driving and teleoperation startup for autonomous vehicles and forklifts
companies.story: Phantom Auto shut down in March 2024 after failing to raise new funding. It sold the remote-operation layer that AV makers were meant to need.

companies.o: Research-led startup building one general AI model to control any robot
companies.story: Founded in 2024 by robot-learning researchers including Sergey Levine, Chelsea Finn and Karol Hausman with investor Lachy Groom, Physical Intelligence builds no robots of its own and instead trains general vision-language-action models (pi0) on data from many machines. It went from a $70M seed to a $400M round at $2.4B in November 2024 (Bezos, Thrive, Lux) and $600M at $5.6B led by CapitalG in November 2025; Bloomberg reported talks in 2026 at $11B and later around $20B, not confirmed as closed.

companies.o: Low-priced online and offline test-prep coaching grown from a YouTube physics channel
companies.story: Alakh Pandey's free YouTube physics lessons became a company in 2020 that sold exam-prep courses for a fraction of Byju's prices, and it was profitable enough to raise little capital (a $100M Series A in 2022 made it a unicorn). While Byju's and Unacademy imploded after the pandemic boom, PhysicsWallah listed in November 2025 with a Rs 3,480 crore IPO (~$402M) and jumped ~33% on debut, touching a market cap of about $5B.

companies.o: App-only supermarket delivering free in fixed slots with small electric vans
companies.story: Picnic delivers groceries free in pre-set 20-minute windows on fixed neighbourhood routes, like a milkman, keeping vans full. It expanded slowly into Germany and France and raised €600M in 2022 and €355M in 2024 (Edeka-led), the opposite approach to 10-minute dark-store apps.

companies.o: Consumer AI video generation startup
companies.story: Pika raised an $80M Series B led by Spark Capital with Greycroft, Lightspeed and Jared Leto in 2024. No 2025 round was found in the results seen.

companies.o: Merchant payments company built on point-of-sale terminals and checkout EMI financing
companies.story: Pine Labs began in 1998 as a fuel-card loyalty business and became India's leading POS-terminal network, adding brand-funded EMI at checkout. It listed in November 2025 via a Rs 3,900 crore IPO (~$451M) at a ~9.5% premium (listing price Rs 242), giving a debut market cap of about Rs 27,788 crore (~$3.2B), well below the ~$5B private valuation it was reported at in 2021; by July 2026 the stock traded about 40% below its debut level.

companies.o: Managed vector database
companies.story: Pinecone raised a $100M Series B at a $750M valuation led by a16z in April 2023, riding the vector database boom. Later years not seen.

companies.o: Indian startup running a hyperspectral imaging satellite constellation that sees hundreds of colour bands.
companies.story: Founded by two BITS Pilani students in 2019, Pixxel launched six Firefly hyperspectral satellites from 2025, claiming the highest-resolution commercial hyperspectral constellation. It raised a $36M Series B led by Google in 2023 and a $100M Series C led by Temasek and Seraphim in September 2026, India's largest space-tech round, for about $195M in total; valuation was not disclosed.

companies.o: Operates the largest fleet of imaging satellites, photographing the whole Earth daily and selling the data.
companies.story: Three ex-NASA scientists started Planet in a Cupertino garage to image the entire planet every day with shoebox-sized 'Dove' satellites, and it listed via a SPAC in December 2021 at about $2.8B. The shares sank and it cut staff in 2023 and 2024, then rallied more than 500% from early 2025 as defense and sovereign demand grew and it reached its first full year of non-GAAP profitability, with its market value reported near $10-11.5B in 2026.

near.what: Shares near $2 and a second round of layoffs before the 2025 rebound

companies.o: Vision software for parcel-handling robots, with remote humans resolving the picks AI can't
companies.story: Plus One, founded by industrial-robot veteran Erik Nieves, sells vision software for parcel induction and depalletizing in which robots handle most picks and a remote 'crew chief' resolves the rare failures. It raised a $50M Series C in March 2023 led by Scale Venture Partners, bringing total funding to nearly $100M.

companies.o: AI browser for knowledge work, founded by a Perplexity Comet employee
companies.story: Polar raised a $5.7M seed led by Madrona in July 2026, with former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke as an angel. Its benchmark claims against OpenAI and Anthropic agents are self-reported.

companies.o: Online marketplace for comparing and buying insurance, plus Paisabazaar for loans
companies.story: Yashish Dahiya, Alok Bansal and Avaneesh Nirjar started Policybazaar in 2008 to let Indians compare insurance prices online, pairing the site with large call centres because buyers still wanted advice. PB Fintech listed in November 2021 with a Rs 5,625 crore IPO (~$761M at 73.9), opening about 17% above its Rs 980 issue price, and later turned profitable.

companies.o: Group travel and music-event experiences sold through creators and influencers
companies.story: Pollen raised a $150M Series C in 2021 betting on a post-COVID boom in festival and group-travel experiences. Heavy cash burn, mass layoffs and a scandal over taking staff and customer money without consent preceded its collapse into administration in August 2022.

companies.o: Builds frontier models for software engineering, sold to enterprises and governments
companies.story: Founded in 2023 by ex-GitHub CTO Jason Warner and Eiso Kant, Poolside trains its own models for coding using reinforcement learning from code execution and sells into enterprises and the public sector. After a $500M round at $3B in 2024 it planned a 2GW data-centre campus in Texas. In August 2026 Nvidia reportedly paid $6B for a non-exclusive licence to its 'model factory', hired 109 of its staff and invested $1B at a $12B pre-money valuation, a hybrid of investment and partial acqui-hire.

companies.o: Developer of Tolan, an AI alien companion app
companies.story: Portola raised a $20M Series A in July 2025 and $30M in October 2026 led by USV, Khosla Ventures and Homebrew, taking total funding to about $60M. The $120M valuation is a prior-round figure from TechCrunch.

companies.o: Mobile payments and 'click to buy' commerce platform
companies.story: Powa's founder claimed a $2.7B valuation in 2014 and announced big partnerships for its mobile payments and PowaTag products, but revenue never materialised. It went into administration in February 2016, one of the UK's biggest tech collapses of its era.

companies.o: Drone data and inspection services company that went bankrupt in 2023
companies.story: PrecisionHawk was one of the best-funded commercial drone companies of the 2010s, selling aerial data, analytics and inspection services to agriculture, energy and insurance customers. Services-heavy margins and commoditised drone hardware wore it down, and it filed for bankruptcy and shut down in December 2023.

companies.o: Members-only flash-sale site for discounted fashion brands
companies.story: Privalia copied France's vente-privée flash-sales model for Spain, Italy, Brazil and Mexico. Vente-privée bought it in 2016 for €500M (~$555M), while US flash-sale star Gilt Groupe sold that year for about $250M after reaching a $1B valuation.

companies.o: Amazon's in-house low-Earth-orbit broadband constellation, the main well-funded challenger to Starlink.
companies.story: Amazon announced Project Kuiper in 2019, won FCC approval for 3,236 satellites in 2020 on condition that half be launched by mid-2026, and committed more than $10B. It flew prototypes in 2023 and its first production satellites in April 2025, then rebranded the service Amazon Leo in late 2025; it is context for any satellite-broadband startup, since it shows the capital a late entrant needs even with a trillion-dollar parent.

companies.o: ML and LLM security platform that bought Laiyer AI (LLM Guard) and SydeLabs
companies.story: Protect AI acquired Laiyer AI in January 2024 and later SydeLabs, then was bought by Palo Alto Networks in 2025. Sources date the deal April or July 2025 and Forrester cites $650M, so price and date are the least consistent.

companies.o: Maker of battery-electric transit buses and EV batteries
companies.story: Proterra was a leader in US electric transit buses and went public via SPAC in 2021. Fixed-price bus contracts signed before supply-chain inflation turned unprofitable, and it filed for Chapter 11 in August 2023, selling its units separately.

companies.o: Low-cost bionic Ability Hand with touch feedback, sold to amputees and to robot makers
companies.story: Founded by University of Illinois PhD Aadeel Akhtar, PSYONIC makes the Ability Hand, a fast, impact-resistant bionic hand with touch feedback built to be far cheaper than rival prosthetics, and also sells it as a robot hand. It raised $3.1M through StartEngine and took a $1M Shark Tank deal in February 2024 from Kevin O'Leary, Lori Greiner and Daymond John at a pitched ~$50M valuation; by September 2025 it had raised over $10M in equity and grants and could make 150 hands a month.

companies.o: Online estate agent charging a fixed fee instead of commission
companies.story: Purplebricks listed on AIM in 2015 and reached a market value around £1.4B in 2018 with Axel Springer investing £125M. Expansion to the US and Australia failed and was shut in 2019, UK share stalled, and in 2023 the company was sold to Strike for £1.

companies.o: Open-source vector database
companies.story: Qdrant raised a $28M Series A led by Spark in January 2024 and later a $50M Series B led by Advance Venture Partners. Series B date was not in the snippet.

companies.o: AI code verification and quality platform
companies.story: Qodo raised a $40M Series A in September 2024 and a $70M Series B led by Qumra Capital in March 2026, bringing total funding to $120M.

companies.o: Canada's largest crypto exchange, until its founder died holding the keys
companies.story: QuadrigaCX collapsed after founder Gerald Cotten died in India in December 2018, supposedly the only person with access to cold wallets holding customer crypto; about C$215M was owed to roughly 76,000 users. Ontario's securities regulator later found the wallets were mostly empty and that Cotten had run a fraud, trading and losing client funds and inventing balances.

companies.o: Mobile-only streaming service of premium 10-minute shows
companies.story: Jeffrey Katzenberg and Meg Whitman raised $1.75B to make Hollywood-quality shows in 'quick bites' for phones only, with no sharing or TV casting at launch. It launched in April 2020 just as lockdowns kept people at home, signups stalled against free TikTok and YouTube, and it shut down after about six months in December 2020.

companies.o: AI radiology for chest X-ray and head CT, strong in emerging markets
companies.story: Qure.ai raised a $65M Series D in September 2024; a secondary table lists about $121M total raised. Only one source was seen.

companies.o: European local reviews site for restaurants and shops
companies.story: Qype built Europe's biggest Yelp-style reviews community across several countries. Yelp bought it in 2012 for about $50M in cash and stock to enter Europe and then folded the Qype brand into Yelp.

companies.o: Maker of the Rabbit R1 AI handheld built on a Large Action Model
companies.story: Rabbit unveiled the R1 at CES in January 2024 and raised $20M led by Khosla Ventures plus a $10M follow-on; reported funding exceeded $59M by late 2024. A March 2024 valuation near $125M is an aggregator estimate only.

companies.o: Generative AI for radiology report impressions and workflow
companies.story: Rad AI raised a $50M Series B led by Khosla Ventures in May 2024. It automates report writing rather than image reading.

companies.o: Banking-as-a-service APIs letting brands launch cards and accounts
companies.story: Railsr (formerly Railsbank) grew fast in the embedded-finance boom, providing accounts and cards to fintech brands. As fintech clients cut back and funding dried up, it entered administration in March 2023 and was sold via pre-pack to a consortium led by D Squared Capital.

companies.o: Licensed music streaming service from the founders of Skype
companies.story: Rdio launched a well-reviewed licensed streaming service before Spotify reached the US, but struggled with marketing and royalty costs as Spotify grew. It filed for bankruptcy in November 2015 and Pandora bought its key assets for $75M.

companies.o: AI deepfake detection expanding into financial-sector fraud
companies.story: New York-based Reality Defender raised an expanded $33M Series A to push into financial services. The snippet names no lead investor or date.

companies.o: Public AI drug discovery company that absorbed Exscientia
companies.story: Recursion merged with Exscientia (closing early 2025) targeting about $100M annual savings, then cut programmes and laid off about 20% of staff. Its market value has fallen since listing.

companies.o: Ex-DeepMind team pitching itself as America's open-weight frontier lab
companies.story: Founded in 2024 by DeepMind's Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou to build coding agents, Reflection repositioned after DeepSeek as 'America's open frontier lab'. Its valuation went from $545M in March 2025 to $8B in October 2025 (Nvidia-led $2B) and roughly $25-27.5B in an April 2026 $2.5B round, before it had shipped a flagship model. It released its first open-weight model, Beam, in October 2026 and reportedly signed a ~$6.3B GPU deal with SpaceX's Memphis data centre.

companies.o: AI platform for mobile game creative strategy and performance marketing
companies.story: Reforged Labs raised a $3.9M seed led by DCM in 2024 and shut down after three years. Its CEO said the gap it sold into was closing and the team chose to close rather than shrink.

companies.o: Multimodal model lab founded by ex-DeepMind and Google Brain researchers
companies.story: Reka built multimodal models with a small team of former DeepMind and Google researchers. Talks for Snowflake to buy it for about $1B collapsed in 2024, and co-founder Yi Tay returned to Google. In July 2025 Nvidia and Snowflake led a $110M round that tripled its valuation to just over $1B, keeping it independent but far smaller than the frontier labs.

companies.o: Rocket maker that tried to 3D-print almost an entire orbital rocket, then pivoted to the larger reusable Terran R.
companies.story: Relativity raised $650M at a $4.2B valuation in 2021 on the idea of 3D-printing rockets; its Terran 1 reached space in March 2023 but the upper stage failed, and the company retired it to build the bigger reusable Terran R. Cash ran low while it struggled to raise more, and in 2025 former Google CEO Eric Schmidt invested, took control and replaced co-founder Tim Ellis as CEO, with Terran R aimed at a 2026 debut and about $3B in launch contracts claimed.

near.what: Terran 1 upper stage failed on its only flight; the rocket was cancelled
Cash reserves ran low while it failed to raise enough for Terran R; rescued by Eric Schmidt taking control in 2025

companies.o: AI workflow automation startup
companies.story: Relay told users in July 2026 that the product was closing, with free access ending August 15 and paid access September 14. CEO Jacob Bank and several staff joined Google's Chrome team, which did not buy the product or brand.

companies.o: API platform for running open-source models
companies.story: A consolidation roundup says Cloudflare acquired Replicate at the start of 2026 to bolster its Workers platform. Nvidia had earlier invested; price not found.

companies.o: Browser-based coding platform with an AI agent that builds apps
companies.story: Replit raised $250M at a $3B valuation in September 2025 (Prysm Capital lead), then $400M at $9B about six months later. Sources disagree on round labels and on who led the second round.

companies.o: Collaborative factory robots Baxter and Sawyer from iRobot's co-founder
companies.story: Founded by iRobot co-founder Rodney Brooks, Rethink made friendly, cheap robots that could work beside people. Baxter was not precise enough for many factory tasks, rivals like Universal Robots won the market, and Rethink shut down in 2018 after an acquisition fell through.

companies.o: Open-source realtime JSON database
companies.story: RethinkDB built a well-loved open-source database but struggled to get developers to pay, while MongoDB won the market. It shut down in 2016; co-founder Slava Akhmechet later wrote that it chased technical correctness over what the market wanted, and the code was handed to the Linux Foundation.

companies.o: Multi-currency card and app that grew into a global financial super-app
companies.story: Revolut started with fee-free foreign exchange cards for travellers and stacked on trading, crypto and business accounts across dozens of countries. It was valued at $33B in 2021, $45B in a 2024 secondary and about $75B in 2025, and won a restricted UK banking licence in 2024 after years of regulatory delays.

companies.o: Harvard/Yale spinout making grippers and software for robotic piece-picking in warehouses
companies.story: RightHand was founded by researchers from Harvard's and Yale's grasping labs to automate 'each picking' of single items in e-commerce warehouses with compliant grippers plus vision and learning software. It raised a $66M Series C in 2022 and roughly $128M in total, and in 2025 took a strategic minority investment from industrial-automation giant Rockwell Automation, terms undisclosed.

companies.o: AI-native ERP and general ledger for mid-market accounting
companies.story: Rillet raised a $25M Series A from Sequoia in May 2025, a $70M Series B ten weeks later, and a $100M Series C at $1B in August 2026. Total raised is summed from the round amounts seen.

companies.o: Unified HR, payroll and IT platform for businesses
companies.story: After being pushed out of Zenefits, Parker Conrad started Rippling to tackle the same small-business HR market, this time charging for software and building payroll and IT tools on a single employee database. It reached a $13.5B valuation in 2024, several times what Zenefits was worth at its peak.

companies.o: Electric pickup, SUV and delivery-van maker backed by Amazon
companies.story: Rivian spent a decade in quiet development before Amazon led a $700M round in 2019 and ordered 100,000 electric delivery vans, giving it a guaranteed customer. Its November 2021 IPO raised about $11.9B, one of the largest US listings ever, though its value fell sharply as production ramped slowly.

companies.o: RISC-V AI chip startup acquired by Meta
companies.story: Meta reportedly paid about $2B for Rivos, a deal that reports say later stumbled, with over a quarter of the joiners laid off and a large-model training chip paused. The layoff accounts are partly anecdotal.

companies.o: UK AI contract review assistant that collapsed after a failed fundraise
companies.story: Robin AI went up for a distressed sale in October 2025 after failing to raise funding and laying off staff. Scissero bought its managed legal services arm in December 2025 (about 70-75 staff, no technology platform) and Microsoft hired former engineers in January 2026.

companies.o: Xiaomi-incubated robot-vacuum maker that overtook iRobot and listed in Shanghai
companies.story: Roborock started by building robot vacuums for Xiaomi's ecosystem, used that channel to scale manufacturing, then launched its own brand with lidar navigation and mopping features at lower prices than the Roomba. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in February 2020 and became one of the world's top robot-vacuum sellers, a key reason iRobot lost share.

companies.o: OHB-backed German small-launch company building RFA One, to fly from SaxaVord in Shetland.
companies.story: RFA, majority-owned by satellite maker OHB, lost its first-stage test article in a fire during a static-fire test at SaxaVord in August 2024. It shipped both stages of a new RFA One to Shetland in early 2026 and targeted a summer 2026 maiden flight, but as of September 2026 it was still preparing, funded partly by ESA Boost! contracts (about EUR11.7M for two demo flights) and a shared German government commitment.

companies.o: Small-satellite launcher (Electron) turned end-to-end space company building the medium-lift Neutron rocket and satellites.
companies.story: Peter Beck founded Rocket Lab in New Zealand in 2006 and its Electron became the most-flown small launcher after SpaceX's rockets; it listed via a SPAC with Vector Acquisition in August 2021 at about a $4.1B valuation. It bought component makers and grew a spacecraft business, and by 2026 its market value was reported at $44-67B while the reusable Neutron rocket, its main bet, had still not flown and slipped toward late 2026 or 2027.

companies.o: Agentic AI platform for investment banks and financial services
companies.story: Rogo raised a $160M Series D in April 2026 led by Kleiner Perkins at about $2B, bringing total funding past $300M. Sources disagree on whether the $75M Series C was Oct 2025 or Jan 2026.

companies.o: Fitness and running-tracking apps
companies.story: Four Austrians built a family of running and fitness apps with tens of millions of downloads. Adidas bought Runtastic in 2015 for €220M (~$244M) to own a digital fitness platform.

companies.o: AI video generation and creative tools company
companies.story: Runway raised a $315M Series E at a $5.3B valuation led by General Atlantic, up from $3.3B at its Series D the previous April.

companies.o: Ilya Sutskever's lab building 'safe superintelligence' with no product before the goal is reached
companies.story: Founded in June 2024 by OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy, SSI raised $1B at $5B within months and $2B at $32B in 2025 without releasing any model or product. Meta tried to buy it in 2025 and instead hired CEO Daniel Gross, leaving Sutskever as CEO. A reported Nvidia-led strategic investment of about $5B in July 2026 is unconfirmed by the company, and no product had shipped as of mid-2026.

companies.o: Tokyo lab building nature-inspired, efficient AI models for Japan
companies.story: Founded in 2023 by Transformer co-author Llion Jones and ex-Google researcher David Ha, Sakana skips brute-force scaling for techniques like evolutionary model merging and its 'AI Scientist'. Japanese banks and corporates backed it heavily, and a November 2025 Series B (reported as about $135M, while the company cited ¥32B) valued it at about $2.65B, making it Japan's most valuable unicorn.

companies.o: CRM delivered as a cloud subscription instead of installed software
companies.story: Founded in 1999 at the peak of the dot-com bubble, Salesforce sold CRM software over the internet by subscription under a 'No Software' slogan. It survived the crash and raised $110M in a 2004 IPO, becoming the template for SaaS companies.

companies.o: Dataflow AI chips and inference cloud
companies.story: SambaNova hit a $5B valuation in a 2021 SoftBank-led round, then Intel signed a non-binding term sheet near $1.6B in December 2025. That deal reportedly collapsed in January 2026 and the two pivoted to a Xeon inference partnership.

companies.o: Canadian general-purpose humanoid maker that pivoted to selling its robot AI for existing arms
companies.story: Sanctuary, co-founded by D-Wave's Geordie Rose and Suzanne Gildert, bet on human-like hands and teleoperation-trained AI and unveiled the Phoenix humanoid in 2023 after raising about $140M including Canadian government money. As far better-funded US and Chinese rivals pulled ahead, two co-founders left, about 30 staff were laid off in November 2024 and the board pushed out CEO Rose; in 2026 it pivoted to deploying its Carbon AI on existing industrial arms rather than selling humanoids.

near.what: Two co-founders left, ~30 layoffs, board pushed out CEO Geordie Rose amid fundraising trouble

companies.o: Canadian startup building compact, low-cost dexterous robot hands for humanoids and arms
companies.story: Sarcomere Dynamics makes the Artus line of dexterous robot hands, pitching human-like finger dexterity at a fraction of the price of research hands like Shadow's, for humanoid makers and robot-arm users. It is an early-stage component supplier riding demand from the humanoid boom; funding amounts were not found in public sources.

companies.o: Autonomous surface vessels for naval defense
companies.story: Saronic raised a $600M Series C, then a $1.75B Series D dated 31 March 2026 in one table. Leads were not named in the snippets.

companies.o: Bengaluru lab building Indian-language and sovereign foundation models
companies.story: Founded in 2023 by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar, Sarvam was picked in April 2025 to build India's sovereign LLM under the IndiaAI Mission. Early open models drew criticism for low adoption, but in June 2026 it closed the first $234M of a $300M Series B at a $1.5B post-money valuation with Nvidia, Amazon and HCLTech, taking most of the money raised by Indian-language AI companies that year.

companies.o: Argentine-founded maker and operator of low-cost sub-metre imaging satellites.
companies.story: Emiliano Kargieman founded Satellogic in Buenos Aires in 2010 to build cheap imaging satellites in-house, and it listed via a SPAC with Cantor's CF Acquisition Corp V in January 2022 at about $850M. The stock collapsed with other space SPACs, it later moved its legal home to the US to chase American defense work, and analysts still call it a speculative stock with small revenue.

companies.o: Mobile payment network linked to bank accounts, bypassing card fees for merchants
companies.story: Satispay lets Italians pay shops from an app linked to their bank account, with far lower merchant fees than cards, in one of Europe's most cash-heavy countries. A €320M round led by Addition in 2022 put its valuation around €1B, Italy's first fintech unicorn.

companies.o: Human-labeled training data for AI models
companies.story: Y Combinator company Scale AI supplied labeled data first to self-driving companies and then to AI labs, reaching a $13.8B valuation in 2024. In June 2025 Meta invested about $14.3B for 49% of the company and hired founder Alexandr Wang to lead its superintelligence effort, the largest of the 'acquihire-style' AI deals.

companies.o: App for sharing anonymous posts with friends and friends-of-friends
companies.story: Secret went viral in Silicon Valley in 2014 as an anonymous gossip app, raising about $35M at a valuation over $100M. Engagement fell and bullying concerns grew, and in April 2015 its founder shut it down and returned remaining cash to investors.

companies.o: MLOps model deployment pioneer
companies.story: TrueFoundry acquired MLOps pioneer Seldon in June 2026, part of a wave of inference and MLOps consolidation. Terms were not found.

companies.o: Kenyan on-demand delivery and freight marketplace for businesses
companies.story: Sendy matched businesses with motorbike and truck drivers and raised over $26M, including a $20M Series B co-led by Toyota Tsusho. It cut staff twice in 2022 and shut its supply (food distribution) pivot, then ran out of money and entered administration with an asset sale in 2023.

companies.o: Sidewalk delivery robots spun out of Postmates, delivering for Uber Eats
companies.story: Serve began as Postmates' robotics unit and was spun out in 2021 after Uber bought Postmates, keeping Uber as a partner and shareholder for Uber Eats deliveries in Los Angeles. It went public through a reverse merger and uplisted to Nasdaq in April 2024; an Nvidia stake sent the stock soaring, and it raised $86M in December 2024 to build a fleet of 2,000 robots, despite 2024 revenue of only about $1.8M.

companies.o: Marketplace for AI compute capacity
companies.story: SF Compute raised $40M in equity at a $300M valuation, led by DCVC and Wing, with Electric Capital and Alt Capital returning. Round date was not in the snippet.

companies.o: London maker of the human-like Shadow Dexterous Hand used by research labs worldwide
companies.story: Shadow grew out of a hobbyist robotics group started by Richard Greenhill in 1987 and became known for the Shadow Dexterous Hand, a 20-plus-motor human-sized hand sold mainly to research labs at a very high price. OpenAI used it for its 2018-2019 Dactyl experiments, including solving a Rubik's Cube one-handed, showing the gap between impressive hand hardware and a mass market, which Shadow has served as a small, long-lived specialist rather than a venture-scale company.

companies.o: Autonomy software (Hivemind) and V-BAT drones for defense

rounds.lead: Advent International, JPMorgan Security and Resiliency Initiative

companies.story: Shield AI raised $240M at $5.3B in March 2025, then a Series G in March 2026 at $12.7B post-money, co-led by Advent and JPMorgan's Security and Resiliency Initiative (reported $1.5B-$2B). Valuation more than doubled in a year.

companies.o: Software that lets any merchant set up an online store
companies.story: Tobias Lütke built Shopify after finding existing e-commerce software too poor for his own snowboard shop. It listed in New York and Toronto in May 2015, raising $131M, and grew into Canada's most valuable tech company as small merchants moved online.

companies.o: App that picks up, packs and ships any item for you
companies.story: Shyp sent couriers to collect items, packed them in a warehouse and shipped them via carriers, expanding to several cities at a $250M valuation. Consumer orders were too infrequent and costly to serve, a pivot to e-commerce returns came too late, and it shut down in March 2018 after raising about $62M.

companies.o: Peer-to-peer ridesharing app that pioneered letting ordinary drivers give rides
companies.story: Sidecar was among the first apps to let regular drivers offer rides, before Uber and Lyft adopted the model. Outspent by both rivals, it pivoted to deliveries, then shut down on December 31, 2015 after raising about $35M-$39M; GM bought its assets and hired about 20 staff for less than that amount.

companies.o: Bret Taylor's agentic customer experience platform for enterprise brands
companies.story: Sierra builds AI agents that handle customer service for large brands and raised $175M in Oct 2024 (total $285M), $350M in Sep 2025 at $10B, then $950M in May 2026 led by Tiger Global and GV. Reported valuation for the 2026 round varies between more than $15B and $15.8B.

companies.o: Low-power global network for cheap IoT sensor connectivity
companies.story: Sigfox raised €150M in 2016, then France's largest tech round, to build a global '0G' network for IoT devices. Volumes stayed far below forecasts as telcos pushed NB-IoT/LTE-M and LoRa spread; it entered receivership in January 2022 and was bought by Singapore's UnaBiz.

companies.o: Computer-use agent for macOS with Windows planned
companies.story: Simular released a macOS computer-use agent and raised $21.5M from Felicis in December 2025, with Windows coming.

companies.o: Generative AI underwriting assistant for insurers
companies.story: Sixfold completed a $30M Series B led by Brewer Lane in January 2026 and launched an AI Underwriter for P&C insurers. HQ country is not confirmed in the snippets.

companies.o: Carnegie Mellon spinout building a general 'brain' model that runs on any robot body
companies.story: CMU professors Deepak Pathak and Abhinav Gupta founded Skild in 2023 to train one foundation model that can control robots of any shape. A $300M Series A in July 2024 valued it at $1.5B (Lightspeed, Coatue, SoftBank, Bezos), and in January 2026 it raised about $1.4B led by SoftBank with Nvidia's NVentures at more than $14B, over triple its value seven months earlier.

companies.o: US maker of autonomous drones that quit consumers to sell to militaries, police and utilities
companies.story: Founded by MIT and Google X alumni, Skydio started with self-flying consumer camera drones but could not beat DJI on price, so it exited consumer in 2023 to focus on defense, public safety and infrastructure inspection. China sanctioned it in October 2024, cutting off its battery supplier, but US bans on Chinese drones turned into a tailwind: it raised $110M at $4.4B in April 2026 and pledged $3.5B for US drone manufacturing.

companies.o: Marketplace and AI analytics for satellite imagery
companies.story: SkyFi closed a $12.7M Series A in January 2026, reportedly co-led by Buoyant Ventures and IronGate Capital. It aggregates 50+ imagery partners.

companies.o: Free internet voice and video calls using peer-to-peer technology
companies.story: Built by Kazaa's founders with Estonian engineers who wrote the P2P code, Skype offered free calls between computers and paid calls to phones. eBay bought it in 2005 for $2.6B and Microsoft paid $8.5B in 2011; its alumni seeded Estonia's startup scene (Wise, Bolt).

companies.o: Hyderabad startup building the Vikram family of small-satellite rockets; flew India's first private rocket (2022) and first private orbital launch (2026).
companies.story: Founded in 2018 by former ISRO scientists Pawan Kumar Chandana and Naga Bharath Daka, Skyroot bet that a private company could build orbital rockets in a country where launch had been an ISRO monopoly; its suborbital Vikram-S became India's first privately built rocket to fly in November 2022. A $60M round co-led by GIC and Sherpalo in May 2026 valued it at about $1.1B (reported as pre-money; ~$160M raised in total), and on 18 July 2026 Vikram-1 reached orbit on its maiden flight, the first private orbital launch from India. The 2023 Temasek round was a pre-Series C (mapped to C); the Series A amount ($11M) comes from an Entrackr funding tally.

companies.o: Team messaging app born from a failed online game
companies.story: Stewart Butterfield's company Tiny Speck, started in Vancouver, built the online game Glitch, which failed in 2012; its internal chat tool became Slack. Slack spread team by team, went public by direct listing in 2019 and was bought by Salesforce for $27.7B in 2021.

companies.o: Barcelona mobile game studio behind Dragon City and Monster Legends
companies.story: Social Point built free-to-play hits Dragon City and Monster Legends on Facebook and then mobile. Take-Two Interactive bought it in 2017 for $250M ($175M cash plus stock), one of Spain's largest tech exits at the time.

companies.o: Maker of cylindrical CIGS thin-film solar panels designed for flat commercial rooftops.
companies.story: Solyndra bet that tube-shaped CIGS panels would beat conventional silicon on rooftops, raised close to $1 billion of private equity (backers included Argonaut and the Walton-linked Madrone) and in 2009 won the first Recovery Act loan guarantee, $535 million (about $527 million drawn), to build a new Fremont factory; total raised here sums ~$1B private plus the drawn DOE loan. Its December 2009 IPO filing came with auditor going-concern doubts and was pulled in June 2010 in favor of $175 million of notes from existing investors, and as silicon panel prices collapsed it filed for bankruptcy on 1 September 2011, laying off about 1,100 workers and becoming a political symbol of the stimulus (DOJ declined criminal charges in 2015).

companies.o: Tech-run apartment-hotel brand leasing whole buildings for short stays
companies.story: Started in Montreal as Flatbook, Sonder signed long leases on apartment buildings and rented units like hotel rooms, going public via SPAC in 2022. Fixed lease costs weighed on it for years; after Marriott ended a 2024 licensing partnership on November 7, 2025, Sonder stopped operations immediately and filed for Chapter 7 liquidation, with some guests asked to leave on short notice.

companies.o: Affordable solar-panelled electric car (the Sion), funded by pre-orders
companies.story: Sono gathered tens of thousands of reservations and community funding for the Sion and listed on Nasdaq in 2021. Without the capital to reach mass production it cancelled the car in early 2023 and filed for insolvency in May 2023, keeping only a small solar-kit business for buses.

companies.o: The Arab world's largest e-commerce marketplace, later Amazon.ae
companies.story: Souq grew out of Jordanian web group Maktoob and built its own delivery and cash-on-delivery network across the Gulf and Egypt. Valued around $1B in 2016 as the region's first unicorn, it was bought by Amazon in 2017 for about $580M.

companies.o: Builds reusable rockets and spacecraft to slash the cost of reaching orbit, with the long-term aim of making life multiplanetary.
companies.story: Elon Musk founded SpaceX in 2002 to cut launch costs and eventually reach Mars, a plan most of the aerospace establishment considered unrealistic; its first three Falcon 1 launches failed (the third in August 2008) and the company survived on a $20M Founders Fund round and a NASA cargo contract. It went on to land and re-fly orbital boosters, bought xAI in February 2026 in a deal valuing SpaceX at about $1T, and listed on Nasdaq (SPCX) on June 12, 2026, raising about $75B at $135/share (about $1.77T valuation) in the largest IPO in history. peak_valuation_usd is the roughly $2.1T market cap reported at the first-day close (later peaks not checked); the 2015 Google/Fidelity round was reported at a $10-12B valuation.

near.what: Third consecutive Falcon 1 failure in August 2008 (stage separation timing error) put NASA contract prospects and the company's cash in doubt; a $20M Founders Fund investment arrived the same month and the fourth flight reached orbit in September 2008.
NASA Commercial Resupply Services contract (about $1.6B for 12 cargo flights) awarded in December 2008 kept the company alive.

companies.o: AI language tutor that teaches speaking
companies.story: Speak raised a $78M Series C in December 2024 led by Accel at a $1B valuation, six months after a $20M Series B extension at $500M.

companies.o: AI contract drafting and review tool for lawyers
companies.story: Spellbook raised a $50M Series B in October 2025 led by Keith Rabois at Khosla Ventures at a $350M valuation. One source also reports $40M in debt financing from RBCx.

companies.o: Nanosatellite data company selling weather, ship and aircraft tracking data from its own constellation.
companies.story: Spire went public via a SPAC in 2021 at about $1.6B on the promise of selling satellite data as a subscription. By 2024-25 it had to restate several years of accounts, fell out of NYSE filing compliance, and its lender could demand repayment when buyer Kpler stalled on a deal for its maritime unit; Spire sued, and in April 2025 closed the sale for about $233.5M plus a $7.5M fee, using it to retire all its debt.
