companies.o: Freemium music streaming licensed from the record labels
companies.story: Spotify launched in Sweden in 2008, where piracy (The Pirate Bay, Kazaa) had gutted music sales, offering labels a legal alternative and equity stakes. It took three years to get US licences, then won globally and did a direct listing on the NYSE in 2018 at about $26.5B.

companies.o: App delivering chef-cooked meals from its own kitchens in under 20 minutes
companies.story: Sprig owned everything from cooking to delivery, which made each meal expensive to produce as restaurant marketplaces like DoorDash and Uber Eats grew. Reportedly burning $850,000 a month and unable to find a buyer, it shut down in May 2017 after raising about $57M.

companies.o: Open-source image generation company behind Stable Diffusion
companies.story: CEO Emad Mostaque resigned in March 2024 amid investor quarrels and senior departures, and Bloomberg reported it had explored a sale. In June 2024 it raised about $80M from Sean Parker, Greycroft, Coatue and others and named Prem Akkaraju CEO.

companies.o: Autonomous trucking startup founded by ex-Argo AI founders, backed by SoftBank
companies.story: Stack AV is run by founders of the shuttered Argo AI and was reported to raise a $1B Series A backed by SoftBank (CB Insights dates it Sept 2023). It is a second-generation bet on the same team after the Argo shutdown.

companies.o: Builds Otter servicing spacecraft that dock with satellites to extend their life, inspect or deorbit them.
companies.story: Founded by two ex-Blue Origin engineers, Starfish flew a small Otter Pup demonstrator in 2023 that hit thruster problems before it could dock, then rebuilt and won life-extension, inspection and deorbit contracts from commercial operators, NASA, the Space Development Agency ($52.5M) and Space Force ($54.5M). It raised $29M in 2024 and a Series B of more than $100M led by Point72 Ventures in April 2026.

companies.o: SpaceX's low-Earth-orbit satellite constellation selling broadband internet directly to consumers, businesses and governments worldwide.
companies.story: Starlink is a business line inside SpaceX (not a separate company), announced in 2015 and funded from SpaceX's own balance sheet, so it has no separate rounds or valuation. It sounded doomed because every earlier LEO broadband constellation (Iridium, Globalstar, Orbcomm, Teledesic) went bankrupt, and Musk himself framed the goal as simply avoiding bankruptcy; cheap launches on SpaceX's own reusable Falcon 9 changed the math. It grew to about $11.4B revenue in 2025 and 13.6M consumer subscribers by September 30, 2026, and was the main engine behind SpaceX's June 2026 IPO (no separate Starlink listing).

dismissed.quote_or_fact: Headline: "Elon Musk's Starlink risks being another satellite flop"

dismissed.who: History of LEO constellations, as cited by Musk (Satellite 2020)
dismissed.quote_or_fact: Paraphrase: Musk noted that essentially every prior low-Earth-orbit constellation had gone bankrupt and said Starlink's goal was to be the first not to.

companies.o: Six-wheeled sidewalk robots for autonomous last-mile deliveries
companies.story: Skype co-founders Ahti Heinla and Janus Friis started Starship to make deliveries with small sidewalk robots, built in Estonia. It found traction on US university campuses and European suburbs where routes are short and predictable, and has completed millions of deliveries.

companies.o: Autonomous trucks with remote human drivers for tricky stretches
companies.story: Starsky combined highway autonomy with remote teleoperators and in 2019 ran a truck with no one on board on a Florida highway. Its founder later wrote that investors wanted flashier AI progress than safety work and that the technology was further off than the industry claimed; it shut down in March 2020.

companies.o: Online alternative-MBA program for working professionals
companies.story: Stoa offered a cohort-based online alternative to the MBA for Indian professionals during the post-pandemic upskilling boom. It shut down in November 2024 without disclosing specific reasons, one of about a dozen funded Indian startups Inc42 counted as closing that year.

companies.o: Building Nova, a fully reusable rocket including a reusable upper stage.
companies.story: Former Blue Origin engineers Andy Lapsa and Tom Feldman founded Stoke to make both stages of a rocket reusable, a problem even SpaceX had not solved for upper stages. It raised a $510M Series D in October 2025 led by Thomas Tull's fund (plus $100M SVB debt) and extended it to $860M in February 2026, for $1.34B raised in total; valuation was not disclosed and Nova's first launch from Cape Canaveral's LC-14 was still pending.

companies.o: Developer-first API for accepting and moving money online.
companies.story: Founded in 2010 in Palo Alto by Irish brothers Patrick and John Collison (then about 21 and 19), Stripe set out to rebuild online payments, a field dominated by banks, processors and PayPal, as a few lines of developer code, backed by Y Combinator and a $2M round from Peter Thiel, Elon Musk, Sequoia and Andreessen Horowitz. It climbed to a $95B private valuation in 2021, reset to $50B in its 2023 $6.5B Series I, then hit $106.7B and $159B (peak, private, February 2026 tender offer led by Thrive, Coatue and a16z) while staying private. Total raised of ~$9.4B is CB Insights' tally; trackers range from $8.1B to $9.8B.

companies.o: German student social network modelled on Facebook
companies.story: StudiVZ copied Facebook's design for German-speaking students before Facebook launched in German, and publisher Holtzbrinck bought it in January 2007 for about €85M (~$116M). Once Facebook localised, users left; the network shrank for a decade and filed for insolvency in 2017.

companies.o: GenAI startup building AI agents to automate customer-query resolution
companies.story: subtl.ai raised about $200K (INR 1.8 Cr) from angels and built AI agents for customer-query redressal. It shut down in 2025 after failing to raise further funds.

companies.o: Voice-based AI assistant for clinicians
companies.story: Suki raised a $70M Series D in October 2024 led by Hedosophia, with Venrock and March Capital; Reuters reported a roughly $500M valuation. Sacra estimates about $168M raised in total, which is a secondary estimate.

companies.o: AI music generation app
companies.story: Suno raised $250M at $2.45B and then $400M at $5.4B post-money, the latter led by Bond Capital with IVP, Forerunner and USV. It is positioned as the ElevenLabs rival in AI music.

companies.o: Mobile game studio of small autonomous teams (Clash of Clans, Brawl Stars)
companies.story: Supercell kills most games in testing and lets tiny teams ship only big hits like Hay Day and Clash of Clans. SoftBank bought 51% for $1.5B in 2013 and Tencent bought 84% in 2016 at a $10.2B valuation.

companies.o: Food delivery app with its own rider fleet, later adding Instamart quick commerce
companies.story: Swiggy launched in Bengaluru in 2014 with its own delivery fleet, so restaurants without riders could deliver, and it raised over $3.5B from Naspers/Prosus, SoftBank and Invesco to reach a $10.7B private valuation in 2022. Its November 2024 Rs 11,327 crore IPO (~$1.35B) was one of India's largest that year, and the stock rose on debut to a market cap of about $12.3B. It remains loss-making as it spends heavily on Instamart to fight Blinkit and Zepto.

companies.o: App-booked shared buses on fixed commuter routes in emerging-market cities
companies.story: Swvl offered cheap, reliable bus seats for Cairo commuters and expanded to Kenya, Pakistan, Latin America and Europe, listing via SPAC in March 2022 at about $1.5B. It then cut over half its staff, exited markets and failed acquisitions; by March 2023 its shares were down over 99%, leaving a market value near $9M.

companies.o: Grocery-wholesaler spinout automating whole distribution centres, with Walmart as anchor customer
companies.story: Symbotic was founded by Rick Cohen, owner of C&S Wholesale Grocers, and spent over a decade building robot-run distribution-centre systems with his own capital before going public in 2022 through a SoftBank-sponsored SPAC. Its fortunes are tied to Walmart, which committed to install the system across its regional centres; in January 2025 Symbotic also bought Walmart's in-house robotics unit, while a late-2024 accounting restatement showed the risks of that concentration.

companies.o: Buy-now-pay-later and shopping app for Saudi Arabia and the UAE
companies.story: Tabby launched in the UAE in 2019 with interest-free pay-in-4 and moved its HQ to Riyadh as Saudi Arabia pushed digital payments. It became a unicorn in 2023 and was valued at $3.3B in 2025, while African BNPL Lipa Later went into administration.

companies.o: Decades-old private fusion company (hydrogen-boron) that agreed to merge with Trump Media in 2025.
companies.story: Founded in 1998 as Tri Alpha Energy, TAE spent more than two decades and over $1.3B from backers including Google and Chevron pursuing aneutronic hydrogen-boron fusion without a commercial reactor. In December 2025 it agreed to an all-stock merger with Donald Trump's loss-making Trump Media & Technology Group valuing the combined company at more than $6B, with each side owning about half and Trump Media advancing up to $300M in cash; it planned to start building its first plant in 2026.

companies.o: Restaurant delivery service using bike couriers in European cities
companies.story: Take Eat Easy expanded to cities in Belgium, France, Spain and Germany but could not close a new round against far better-funded Deliveroo, Foodora and Uber Eats. It entered receivership in July 2016, leaving couriers and restaurants unpaid; its founder's public post-mortem became a classic.

companies.o: Gulf food and grocery delivery leader
companies.story: Founded in Kuwait in 2004, long before smartphones, Talabat was sold to Rocket Internet in 2015 for $170M and then folded into Delivery Hero. In December 2024 it listed in Dubai raising about $2B at roughly $10.2B, the world's biggest tech IPO that year.

companies.o: AI scribe for European clinicians
companies.story: Tandem raised a $50M Series A in mid-2025 led by Kinnevik with Northzone and others. It is pushing into the NHS.

companies.o: Marketplace buying produce from smallholder farmers and supplying businesses, with a sister farmer-lending platform (TaniFund)
companies.story: TaniHub bought produce directly from Indonesian farmers to sell to businesses and households, and ran TaniFund to lend to farmers. After the business wound down, prosecutors alleged irregularities and breaches of investment rules in about $25M of funding channelled into TaniHub and TaniFund between 2019 and 2023, and in 2025 arrested former CEO Ivan Arie Setiawan, a former board member and a former MDI Ventures CEO. Exact shutdown year and total funding are not confirmed by the sources collected.

companies.o: Planned low-earth-orbit satellite internet constellation backed by Craig McCaw and Bill Gates
companies.story: Teledesic planned hundreds of low-orbit satellites to deliver global broadband, essentially Starlink two decades early, with backing from Craig McCaw and Bill Gates. Launch costs were far too high, Iridium's 1999 bankruptcy scared investors, and Teledesic suspended its satellite work in 2002.

companies.o: Open-source LLM gateway, observability and optimization stack
companies.story: TensorZero archived its GitHub repo on June 12, 2026 and, per one article, returned unused capital to investors after a $7.3M FirstMark-led seed. The article frames it as proof open-source LLMOps struggles to survive; the exact cause was not stated.

companies.o: Telefónica's Spanish-language internet portal and ISP of the dot-com boom
companies.story: Terra listed in Madrid and on Nasdaq in November 1999 and its shares soared more than tenfold within months; in 2000 it bought US portal Lycos for $12.5B in stock. When the bubble burst the value evaporated and Telefónica reabsorbed Terra in 2005 at a fraction of its peak.

companies.o: Small-satellite manufacturer that listed via SPAC, booked a giant constellation order that never paid, and was sold cheaply to Lockheed Martin.
companies.story: Terran Orbital built small satellites for the US military and went public via SPAC in 2022 at about $1.58B, then announced a $2.4B order for 300 satellites from Rivada that depended on Rivada raising funds it never secured. Burning cash and carrying heavy debt, it was bought by its biggest customer and shareholder Lockheed Martin in October 2024 for about $450M including debt, roughly $0.25 a share.

companies.o: Electric car maker that started with a high-priced sports car to fund a path to mass-market EVs, batteries and energy storage.
companies.story: Tesla bet that a startup could build electric cars from scratch when no new US automaker had succeeded in decades and EVs were seen as slow, short-range niche products; it began with the expensive Roadster to fund cheaper models. Musk supplied about $6.5M of the 2004 $7.5M Series A, Daimler bought a roughly 10% stake for about $50M in May 2009, a $465M DOE loan was approved in June 2009 (repaid in May 2013, years early), and Tesla listed on June 29, 2010 at $17/share, raising $226M. Market cap at listing and peak market cap were not verified in this session, so those fields are null.

near.what: During the 2008 financial crisis Tesla nearly ran out of cash while the Roadster ramped; Musk put in more of his own money and a round closed in December 2008, before the 2009 Daimler investment and DOE loan.
Model 3 'production hell' in 2017-2018; Musk later said the company came close to bankruptcy during the ramp.

companies.o: Cruise founder Kyle Vogt's household chore robot startup, valued in billions before shipping
companies.story: After leaving Cruise in late 2023, Kyle Vogt started The Bot Company in 2024 with ex-Tesla AI staff to build a robot that does household chores, raising $150M before showing a product. A March 2025 round led by Greenoaks valued it at $2B, and Bloomberg reported in October 2025 that it was raising about $250M at over $4B led by Eclipse, still with no public product or revenue.

companies.o: Weather data and insurance tools for farmers
companies.story: Ex-Google employees started WeatherBill to sell weather insurance, then focused on farmers using weather and soil data. Monsanto bought it for about $930M in 2013, one of the first big agtech exits.

companies.o: Early social network of user home pages and chat rooms
companies.story: Founded by two Cornell students, theglobe.com set a record when its November 1998 IPO priced at $9 and closed its first day at $63.50, a roughly 606% jump. Ad revenue collapsed with the dot-com bust and it shut its social network in 2001, years before Facebook made the idea work.

companies.o: API letting Nigerian fintech wallets send money to each other
companies.story: Thepeer raised a $2.1M seed in 2022 to connect wallets across Nigerian fintechs. Its founders said they never found product-market fit, acquisition talks failed, and it shut in April 2024, returning remaining capital to investors.

companies.o: Promised hundreds of lab tests from a few drops of finger-prick blood on its own Edison device.
companies.story: Elizabeth Holmes's Theranos claimed its Edison device could run a full panel of lab tests from a finger-prick, reaching a ~$9B private valuation in 2014 and a Walgreens retail rollout. A WSJ investigation in October 2015 revealed the tech did not work as claimed, followed by CMS lab sanctions in 2016 and SEC charges in March 2018 alleging a fraud that raised over $700M from investors. The company dissolved in September 2018 and Holmes was later criminally convicted.

near.what: WSJ (John Carreyrou) October 2015 exposé reported Theranos's own device was unreliable and most tests ran on commercial analyzers
CMS sanctions after lab inspection; Holmes barred from operating a lab and Walgreens partnership unwound
SEC charged Theranos, Holmes and Balwani with 'massive fraud' in March; company dissolved in September

dismissed.who: Jina Choi, SEC San Francisco Regional Office director
dismissed.quote_or_fact: "The Theranos story is an important lesson for Silicon Valley"
Paraphrase: his October 2015 reporting showed Theranos ran most of its tests on modified third-party machines rather than its proprietary device, triggering the collapse.

companies.o: Mira Murati's AI lab that raised a record $2B seed before shipping a product
companies.story: Founded in February 2025 by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, it raised the largest seed round ever ($2B at $12B) and launched Tinker, a fine-tuning API. The founding team then scattered: co-founder Andrew Tulloch left for Meta in October 2025, CTO Barret Zoph and Luke Metz returned to OpenAI in January 2026, and Lilian Weng stepped down in July 2026. A planned round at up to $50B never closed; in November 2026 it was reported raising about $5B at a $40B pre-money valuation, with Nvidia supplying part.

companies.o: Shared e-scooter and e-bike operator across European cities
companies.story: Tier raced Lime, Voi, Bird and Dott across Europe and hit a $2B valuation in 2021. City tenders, bans like Paris's 2023 vote and price wars squeezed margins; in 2024 it merged into rival Dott at a fraction of its peak value.

companies.o: Open-model inference and GPU cloud
companies.story: Together AI went from $3.3B in February 2025 to reported talks near $1B at $7.5B around April 2026. Nvidia is among investors; no closed round with a named lead was seen.

companies.o: UK spherical-tokamak fusion company that also sells its high-temperature superconducting magnet technology.
companies.story: Spun out of the UK's Culham fusion lab ecosystem in 2009, Tokamak Energy built compact spherical tokamaks and reached 100 million degrees in its ST40 device in 2022. To fund a long road to power plants, it split out a business selling high-temperature superconducting magnets for other uses and raised $125M in late 2024.

companies.o: AI storytelling and slide-generation app that pivoted away from presentations
companies.story: Tome raised about $81M (Coatue, Greylock, Lightspeed, 8VC, GV) and reportedly hit a ~$300M valuation, then shut its presentation product on April 30, 2025. The team concluded a horizontal consumer slide tool could not become a business and moved to the AI CRM Lightfield; the Tome brand went to AngelList.

companies.o: Weather intelligence platform building an AI-native weather satellite constellation
companies.story: Tomorrow.io raised a $175M Series F in February 2026 led by Stonecourt Capital and HarbourVest at a reported valuation above $1B, extended by $35M from Pitango in May 2026 to $210M.

companies.o: Business travel booking and management platform for companies
companies.story: TravelPerk survived COVID wiping out business travel, then rode the rebound to a $1.3B valuation in a SoftBank-led round in 2022. It raised a further $200M in 2025 and kept expanding in the US.

companies.o: Turkey's largest e-commerce marketplace, majority-owned by Alibaba
companies.story: Demet Mutlu started Trendyol as a fashion flash-sales site and turned it into Turkey's dominant marketplace with its own delivery and food/grocery arms. Alibaba bought a majority in 2018 and a $1.5B round in 2021 valued it at $16.5B, Turkey's most valuable startup.

companies.o: Space-defense startup building Jackal autonomous spacecraft that approach and inspect other satellites.
companies.story: Founded in 2022 by former US Space Force officers, True Anomaly flew its first two Jackal spacecraft in 2024 on a mission that only partly worked, then rode the defense-tech boom and the Golden Dome missile-shield push. It raised a $260M Series C led by Accel in April 2025 and, per Bloomberg, $650M at a $2.2B valuation in April 2026, taking total funding past $1B.

companies.o: Global mobile network and eSIM provider for travellers and IoT
companies.story: Truphone was an early eSIM and international mobile network largely funded by investors linked to Roman Abramovich. After UK sanctions on Abramovich in 2022 froze its funding and customers, the business was sold in September 2022 for £1.

companies.o: Invite-only Spanish social network popular with teenagers
companies.story: Founded by American Zaryn Dentzel in Madrid, Tuenti was Spain's biggest social network for teens and Telefónica bought it in 2010 for about €70M (~$93M). Facebook overtook it within a few years and Telefónica turned Tuenti into a mobile operator brand, closing the social network in 2016.

companies.o: Autonomous long-haul trucking company that wound down its US operations
companies.story: TuSimple decided in December 2023 to end operations and kept a skeleton US team to wind down in Q1 2024, laying off 150 more staff. It is a listed-company AV truck failure alongside Embark.

companies.o: B2B platform sourcing produce from farmers and supplying Nairobi's informal kiosks
companies.story: Twiga raised over $160M (reports range to $185M) to digitise fresh-food supply to Kenyan mama-mboga kiosks, including a $50M Series C led by Creadev. It cut a third of staff in 2022, moved asset-light in 2025 amid allegations of a 'soft liquidation', and the operating entity entered administration in August 2026.

companies.o: South African digital bank onboarding customers through supermarket kiosks
companies.story: TymeBank launched in 2019 with kiosks in Pick n Pay and Boxer stores, signing up millions of low-income South Africans, and expanded to the Philippines as GoTyme. Brazil's Nubank led a $250M Series D in December 2024 at a $1.5B valuation.

companies.o: App to hail a ride from a nearby driver
companies.story: Uber began as a black-car service and expanded into cheap peer-to-peer rides after Sidecar and Lyft proved drivers with personal cars would work, raising tens of billions to subsidize growth worldwide. It retreated from China, Russia and Southeast Asia by selling to local rivals, went public in May 2019 at $82.4B, and turned consistently profitable years later.

companies.o: Gut microbiome testing kits sold to consumers and billed to insurers
companies.story: uBiome started with crowdfunding for at-home microbiome kits and raised an $83M Series C in 2018 at a $600M valuation. After an FBI raid in April 2019 over its insurance billing practices it went bankrupt that year, and its co-founders were later indicted on fraud charges.

companies.o: Shenzhen robot maker whose Walker humanoids work on Chinese EV production lines
companies.story: UBTech sold educational and consumer robots for a decade before becoming, in December 2023, the first humanoid-robot company listed in Hong Kong despite years of losses. Its Walker S humanoids were piloted in factories of BYD, Geely, FAW-Volkswagen and others, and it reported more than 800M yuan (~$112M) of Walker orders from early 2025 to November 2025 as Walker S2 entered mass production.

companies.o: Robotic process automation software that automates repetitive office tasks
companies.story: Daniel Dines started UiPath as an outsourcing shop in Bucharest before pivoting to automation software, later moving headquarters to New York. It reached a $35B private valuation and listed on the NYSE in April 2021 at about $29B, Romania's biggest tech success.

companies.o: B2B wholesale app supplying stock and credit to small Indonesian mom-and-pop retailers
companies.story: Ula supplied inventory to small warung shops through a B2B ordering app, one of several heavily funded Indonesian bets on digitising traditional retail. In 2023 it announced a temporary suspension of its business and then gradually shut down operations as the region's funding drought left thin-margin wholesale models unable to raise more. Funding totals are not confirmed by the sources collected.

companies.o: Chinese maker of cheap robot dogs and humanoids that had a record Shanghai IPO
companies.story: Wang Xingxing started Unitree in 2016 to sell legged robots far cheaper than Boston Dynamics, and its robot dogs and the G1 humanoid (priced from about $16,000) made it profitable and famous through viral dancing demos. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on 19 August 2026, raising about 6.1B yuan at a 61B-yuan (~$8.5B) valuation with retail demand over 8,000x oversubscribed; shares opened up 629%, briefly valuing it near 445B yuan (~$62B).

companies.o: Danish pioneer of affordable collaborative robot arms, bought by Teradyne
companies.story: Three University of Southern Denmark researchers founded Universal Robots to make light, cheap robot arms that small factories could program without specialists and run safely next to workers. It became the market leader in 'cobots', beating Rethink Robotics, and test-equipment maker Teradyne bought it in 2015 for $285M plus up to $65M in earn-outs; it went on to sell tens of thousands of arms.

companies.o: Toronto at-memory AI inference chip startup
companies.story: After failing to raise funds, Untether AI wound down in 2025 and AMD hired its engineering team without buying the company's assets. Product supply and support for existing customers ended.

companies.o: AI platform that turns idle contractor databases into booked jobs for home-services providers
companies.story: Dallas-based UpSmith raised a $10M Series A led by SemperVirens, its largest round yet. The snippets give no date.

companies.o: Marketplace for trained, standardised at-home services from salon to repairs
companies.story: Launched as UrbanClap in 2014, it trained and certified its own service pros (beauticians, cleaners, electricians) instead of running a loose lead-gen listing, the model that killed Homejoy in the US. It became a unicorn in 2021 at about $2.1B and listed in September 2025 with a Rs 1,900 crore IPO (about $220M at 86.5 INR/USD) that was ~104x subscribed; shares jumped ~58-62% on debut to a market cap near Rs 23,955 crore (~$2.77B).

companies.o: Free one-hour delivery of electronics, books and snacks in New York and London
companies.story: Urbanfetch competed head-on with Kozmo, offering free one-hour delivery in Manhattan and London. It closed its consumer delivery business in 2000 after merger talks with Kozmo collapsed, months before Kozmo itself shut down.

companies.o: Design-led direct-to-consumer e-bikes with proprietary parts
companies.story: VanMoof sold sleek e-bikes direct with custom parts only it could repair, and raised $128M in 2021 during the pandemic bike boom. Repair backlogs, supply-chain costs and selling bikes below cost drained cash; it went bankrupt in July 2023 and was bought by Lavoie, a McLaren Applied company.

companies.o: Makes drugs and materials in microgravity on small free-flying satellites and returns them to Earth in reentry capsules.
companies.story: Founded by ex-SpaceX engineer Will Bruey and Founders Fund partner Delian Asparouhov, Varda's first capsule, W-1, crystallised the HIV drug ritonavir in orbit in 2023 but sat in space for months waiting for US reentry approvals before landing in Utah in February 2024. It paid the bills partly with Air Force hypersonic reentry testing, and raised a $187M Series C in 2025 and a $251M Series D at about a $1.6B valuation in 2026 (roughly $598M raised in total).

near.what: W-1 capsule stranded in orbit for months after the FAA denied a reentry licence; landed February 2024

companies.o: Building commercial space stations (Haven-1, then Haven-2) funded largely by crypto billionaire Jed McCaleb.
companies.story: Ripple and Stellar co-founder Jed McCaleb started Vast in 2021 and put in the bulk of more than $1B of private capital before it took outside money. It flew a Haven Demo pathfinder in late 2025, slipped Haven-1 from May 2026 to Q1 2027 for more ground testing, and in March 2026 raised $500M ($300M Series A equity plus $200M debt) to build Haven-2 as an ISS successor; valuation was not disclosed.

companies.o: Maker of Vy, a computer-use agent operating a remote Mac
companies.story: Anthropic acquired Vercept in February 2026 and shut the Vy product on March 25. Deal terms were not in the sources seen.

companies.o: All-in-one fraud detection against bots, duplicate accounts and fraudsters
companies.story: Austin-based Verisoul, founded in 2022, raised an $8.8M Series A for fraud prevention. The snippet does not name the lead or the date.

companies.o: AI agents that work on mortgage decisions for lenders
companies.story: Vesta raised a $30M Series B led by Conversion Capital with Citi Ventures, a16z and three lender customers investing. The snippet gives no date and HQ is not confirmed.

companies.o: Brain-inspired AGI lab that pivoted to robot automation and sold to Alphabet's Intrinsic
companies.story: Vicarious raised roughly $250M from backers including Peter Thiel, Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg and Jeff Bezos to build human-like AI modeled on the brain, and famously claimed to have broken CAPTCHAs in 2013. With no AGI product, it pivoted to selling AI-driven robotic packing and kitting systems, and Alphabet's robotics unit Intrinsic acquired it in 2022 on undisclosed terms.

companies.o: Peer-to-peer marketplace for second-hand clothes with no seller fees
companies.story: Vinted began in Lithuania in 2008, moved fees from sellers to buyers and built integrated shipping, then won France, Germany and much of Europe. Valued at €3.5B in 2021, it turned profitable in 2023 and a 2024 secondary valued it at €5B (~$5.4B).

companies.o: Air-launched LauncherOne rockets from a modified Boeing 747 to put small satellites in orbit from anywhere.
companies.story: Spun out of Branson's Virgin Galactic, Virgin Orbit bet that launching rockets from a 747 ('Cosmic Girl') would make small-satellite launch flexible and responsive, and it went public via SPAC in December 2021 at a $3.7B valuation (the SPAC deal value), though heavy redemptions left only ~$228M of an expected up to $483M. After spending more than $1B, its January 2023 mission from Cornwall (the first UK orbital attempt) failed, financing talks collapsed, and it filed Chapter 11 in April 2023. Its assets were auctioned in May 2023 for roughly $36M to Rocket Lab, Stratolaunch and Launcher/Vast.

near.what: First LauncherOne test flight failed to reach space on 25 May 2020
SPAC redemptions cut expected proceeds of up to $483M to about $228M
9 January 2023 launch from Spaceport Cornwall failed to reach orbit; operations suspended in March and Chapter 11 filed 4 April

companies.o: AI-driven stroke detection and care coordination
companies.story: Viz.ai raised a $100M Series D in April 2022 with CRV, GV, Insight Partners and Tiger Global, for about $171M total per one secondary table. No later round surfaced.

companies.o: Multicopter electric air taxi for short urban flights
companies.story: Volocopter aimed to fly air taxis at the 2024 Paris Olympics but missed certification and the demo. It filed for insolvency in December 2024 after failing to raise more and was bought in early 2025 by China's Wanfeng group (owner of Diamond Aircraft) for a small sum.

companies.o: Australian digital-only bank that shut after failing to raise a A$200M Series F
companies.story: Volt was an Australian digital-only bank that raised almost A$85M in 2021 (about US$64M at 0.75) and went back to market in early 2022 for a A$200M Series F. When that raise failed, the board closed the business in June 2022 and handed back its banking licence, with about A$113M of deposits from some 6,000 customers returned or moved to NAB.

companies.o: Purpose-built electric trucks for city deliveries
companies.story: Volta Trucks designed the Volta Zero city truck and began production in Austria in 2023. When its battery supplier Proterra filed for bankruptcy, production stalled and Volta filed for bankruptcy in October 2023.

companies.o: Toronto-listed crypto broker paying yield on customer deposits
companies.story: Voyager lent customer crypto to firms including hedge fund Three Arrows Capital, which defaulted on a loan of roughly $650M in 2022. It filed for bankruptcy in July 2022; a sale to FTX died with FTX's collapse and a later deal with Binance.US also fell through, leaving it to liquidate.

companies.o: Generative-AI and simulation-first driverless truck developer
companies.story: Waabi raised a $200M Series B in June 2024 led by Uber and Khosla Ventures, bringing total funding to $280M, with Nvidia, Porsche and Volvo's venture arm. Later 2026 coverage reports a larger Uber-linked raise whose details are inconsistent across sources.

companies.o: Mobile app for buying and selling second-hand goods locally
companies.story: Wallapop won Spain's second-hand market and in 2016 absorbed the Spanish operations of rival Letgo, which then focused (and failed) in the US. It added shipping and a protection fee model and raised €157M in 2021 at about €690M (~$815M) from Naver-backed Korelya.

companies.o: On-demand laundry and dry-cleaning pickup and delivery
companies.story: Washio was one of the 'Uber for X' startups, picking up laundry by app and returning it cleaned. Delivery costs on low-ticket orders never worked out, and it shut down in August 2016 after raising about $17M.

companies.o: AI decision software for military planning
companies.story: Watchtower raised a $35M seed led by Shield Capital and Conviction with Founders Fund; DIU selected it in January 2026.

companies.o: Social platform where millions write and read serialized fiction
companies.story: Wattpad built a huge community of mostly young readers and writers sharing serialized stories, then turned hit stories into books, films and TV. South Korea's Naver bought it in 2021 for about US$600M.

companies.o: Low-fee mobile money app charging a flat 1% to send in Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire

rounds.lead: Sequoia Heritage, Founders Fund, Ribbit Capital, Stripe

companies.story: Wave attacked telco mobile money (Orange Money) with free cash-in/out and a flat 1% send fee, forcing Orange to cut prices. Its $200M Series A at $1.7B in 2021 was then the largest Series A for an African fintech, making it Francophone Africa's first unicorn.

companies.o: End-to-end embodied AI driving software sold to automakers and robotaxi fleets
companies.story: Wayve raised about $1B led by SoftBank in 2024, then a $1.2B Series D in February 2026 at $8.6B post-money with Uber commitments taking it to about $1.5B. Mercedes, Nissan and Stellantis joined the round.

companies.o: Crowdsourced real-time traffic and navigation app
companies.story: Waze turned drivers' phones into traffic sensors and let users edit the map, building data Google and Apple lacked. After talks with Facebook and Apple, Google bought it in June 2013 for about $1.1B, having raised about $67M.

companies.o: Canadian app for automated investing, trading, crypto and tax filing
companies.story: Wealthsimple started as a low-fee robo-advisor backed by Power Corporation and expanded into commission-free trading, crypto and tax filing for Canadians. A C$750M round in 2021 valued it at C$5B (about US$4B), and it pulled out of the US and UK to focus on Canada.

companies.o: Online grocery store that built its own automated warehouses and delivery fleet
companies.story: Webvan spent heavily on automated warehouses and its own trucks before proving demand, raising about $800M including a $375M IPO in 1999. It bought rival HomeGrocer for $1.2B in stock in 2000, but losses of roughly $830M forced it to shut down in June 2001 and lay off about 2,000 people.

companies.o: Digital insurance platform combining broker network and its own insurer
companies.story: Wefox raised over $1B to digitise insurance distribution in Europe, reaching a $4.5B valuation in 2022. Heavy losses led to the founder-CEO stepping down in 2023 and in 2024 it sold off country units and needed an emergency recapitalisation.

companies.o: Privacy-focused personal finance and budgeting site
companies.story: Wesabe launched before Mint with a similar money-management idea but required more manual work from users, partly to protect privacy. Co-founder Marc Hedlund later wrote that Mint won because it was simply easier to use; Wesabe shut down in 2010, a year after Mint sold to Intuit.

companies.o: Coworking company that leased offices long-term and rented desks short-term
companies.story: WeWork signed long leases and rented desks short-term, pitching itself as a tech company; SoftBank's January 2019 investment valued it at $47B. Its 2019 IPO filing exposed huge losses and governance problems, the IPO was pulled and founder Adam Neumann ousted; after a 2021 SPAC listing at about $9B it filed for Chapter 11 in November 2023, wiping out shareholders before emerging under new owners in 2024.

companies.o: Mapping data for informal minibus-taxi networks in emerging-market cities
companies.story: WhereIsMyTransport mapped the informal minibus and paratransit routes that most commuters in African and Latin American cities rely on, selling data and a commuter app. It was among the high-profile African closures of 2023 as venture funding dried up.

companies.o: Rocket Internet's Airbnb clone for European apartment rentals
companies.story: Rocket Internet launched Wimdu in 2011 with a $90M Series A, then one of Europe's largest, to beat Airbnb to Europe. Airbnb responded by buying another German clone and expanding aggressively; Wimdu merged with 9flats in 2016 and shut in 2018 amid Berlin's short-term rental restrictions.

companies.o: AI coding assistant and agentic code editor
companies.story: Windsurf began as GPU startup Exafunction, pivoted to the Codeium coding assistant and raised $243M at a $1.25B valuation. A roughly $3B sale to OpenAI collapsed in July 2025; days later Google paid $2.4B in license fees and compensation to hire CEO Varun Mohan and key researchers, and Cognition bought the remaining company and product.

companies.o: Alphabet's drone delivery unit, scaling with Walmart in US suburbs
companies.story: Wing began in 2012 as a Google X moonshot and became its own Alphabet company in 2018, the first US drone operator to win FAA air-carrier certification for deliveries. After years of small pilots in Virginia, Texas and Australia, it moved to partner-led scale, with Walmart announcing in 2025 an expansion to about 100 more stores across several US metro areas. It is context rather than a venture comparable, since Alphabet funds it.

companies.o: Payment processor that rose into the DAX before a €1.9B accounting fraud
companies.story: Wirecard replaced Commerzbank in Germany's DAX index in 2018 at a market value around €24B (~$28B). After years of FT reporting dismissed by regulators, auditors could not find €1.9B of cash in June 2020; the company filed for insolvency within days and its CEO was arrested.

companies.o: Cheap, transparent international money transfers (formerly TransferWise)
companies.story: Estonian founders Kristo Käärmann and Taavet Hinrikus built TransferWise to avoid hidden bank FX mark-ups by matching flows between countries. It was profitable before going public and did a direct listing in London in 2021 at about £8.75B (~$11B).

companies.o: Drag-and-drop website builder for small businesses
companies.story: Wix started as a Flash-based site builder and rebuilt on HTML5 as Flash died, converting free users into premium plans at scale. It listed on Nasdaq in November 2013, raising about $127M, and grew into a multi-billion-dollar company with hundreds of millions of registered users.

companies.o: Agentless cloud security platform scanning entire cloud environments
companies.story: Wiz's founders had sold Adallom to Microsoft and built Wiz into the fastest software company to $100M ARR. After rejecting a $23B Google offer in 2024, it agreed in March 2025 to be acquired by Google for $32B in cash, Israel's largest ever tech deal.

companies.o: Food and retail delivery app focused on smaller European cities
companies.story: Wolt won the Nordics, Baltics and Central Europe by going to cities competitors ignored and obsessing over service. DoorDash agreed to buy it in November 2021 for €7B (~$8.1B) in stock, its biggest international bet; the value fell with DoorDash's share price before closing in 2022.

companies.o: Algorithmic short-term payday lender approving loans in minutes
companies.story: Wonga became the UK's best-known payday lender with automated underwriting and high interest rates. After the FCA capped costs and forced it in 2014 to write off £220M of loans for 330,000 customers, a flood of compensation claims pushed it into administration in August 2018.

companies.o: Cloud HR and finance software for large enterprises
companies.story: PeopleSoft founder Dave Duffield and Aneel Bhusri started Workday after Oracle's hostile takeover of PeopleSoft, rebuilding HR software for the cloud. It went public in October 2012, raising about $637M, and became a standard for large-company HR systems.

companies.o: Fei-Fei Li's lab building 'world models' that generate explorable 3D worlds
companies.story: Founded in 2024 by ImageNet creator Fei-Fei Li with Justin Johnson, Ben Mildenhall and Christoph Lassner, World Labs raised $230M at about $1B to build models that understand and generate 3D space. AMD, which already trained and served its models on AMD GPUs, agreed in September 2026 to buy it for about $8.2B in stock, with Li becoming AMD's chief scientist; the deal closed in November 2026.

companies.o: Enterprise generative AI platform that began with marketing copy
companies.story: Writer raised a $200M Series C at $1.9B in November 2024 co-led by Premji Invest, Radical Ventures and ICONIQ Growth, taking total funding to $326M. Salesforce, Adobe, Citi, IBM and Workday participated.

companies.o: Small Chongqing dockless bike-sharing startup with 1,200 bikes
companies.story: Wukong launched about 1,200 bikes in hilly Chongqing with only mechanical locks and no GPS tracking. Within about five months roughly 90% of the bikes had disappeared, presumed stolen, and it shut down in June 2017, widely called the first failure of China's bike-sharing boom; the founder reportedly lost over 1M yuan.

companies.o: High-temperature gas-cooled small reactor and TRISO fuel developer backed by Amazon.
companies.story: X-energy agreed in 2022 to go public via Ares Acquisition Corp at about $2B, but the SPAC deal was terminated in 2023 amid tough markets. It won US Department of Energy demonstration funding for a plant with Dow in Texas and in October 2024 raised a $500M Series C-1 anchored by Amazon, which plans to use its reactors.

near.what: $2B SPAC merger with Ares Acquisition Corp terminated

companies.o: Elon Musk's AI lab behind Grok, merged with X and then acquired by SpaceX
companies.story: Founded by Elon Musk in 2023, xAI built the Colossus supercomputer in Memphis in months and shipped Grok into X. It absorbed X in March 2025, raised at a $230B valuation in January 2026 while reportedly burning about $1B a month, and in February 2026 was folded into SpaceX in an all-stock deal valuing xAI at $250B. SpaceX then listed in June 2026 in a record $75B IPO at about $1.77T, so xAI's investors exited through Musk's rocket company rather than on xAI's own numbers.

companies.o: AI drug discovery company launched with a $1B Series A
companies.story: Xaira secured a $1B Series A led by Arch Venture Partners and Foresite Capital. The year was not given in the snippet.

companies.o: App-only Australian challenger bank that won a full banking licence then handed it back
companies.story: Xinja built an app-only neobank and won a full Australian banking licence, attracting 37,884 customers with more than A$252M in deposits. A promised A$433M investment from Dubai-based World Investments was paused, and with COVID-19 hitting capital markets it could not raise enough to keep operating. In December 2020 it returned 99.97% of deposits (the rest moved to NAB) and APRA revoked its licence.

companies.o: Earth mapping for AI with its own satellite constellation
companies.story: Xoople raised a $130M Series B in April 2026 and is partnering with L3Harris on sensors for its constellation.

companies.o: Turkey's pioneering online food ordering platform
companies.story: Nevzat Aydın launched Yemeksepeti for web food ordering in 2001, a decade before smartphones, and built a profitable marketplace across Turkey and the Gulf. Delivery Hero bought it in 2015 for $589M, a record Turkish internet deal at the time.

companies.o: Anonymous, location-based message board popular on college campuses
companies.story: Yik Yak spread across US campuses in 2014 and raised about $73M at a valuation reported near $400M. Bullying and threats led schools to ban it, a move away from anonymity alienated users, and in 2017 it shut down after Square paid about $1M to hire its engineers.

companies.o: Online retailer of designer fashion that merged with Net-a-Porter
companies.story: Federico Marchetti launched YOOX in Bologna in 2000 selling off-season designer clothes online, survived the dot-com crash and listed in Milan in 2009. It merged with Net-a-Porter in 2015 and Richemont bought out the rest in 2018; Richemont later sold the business to Mytheresa in 2025 at a steep loss.

companies.o: Crowdsourced platform to compare 500+ AI model answers, with votes rewarded
companies.story: Yupp launched in June 2025 and raised a $33M seed led by Chris Dixon at a16z crypto, reaching 1.3M signups and a few AI-lab customers. It shut down in March 2026 because the founders could not find strong enough product-market fit.

companies.o: Crowd platform collecting human preferences to evaluate and tune LLMs
companies.story: Yupp shut down in March 2026 after raising $33M with backing from a16z crypto's Chris Dixon, despite 1.3M sign-ups. Coverage cites quality-control problems and an inability to match established enterprise vendors' scale and integrations.

companies.o: Online shoe and fashion retailer with free delivery and returns, started as a Zappos copy
companies.story: Backed by the Samwer brothers' Rocket Internet, Zalando cloned Zappos for Germany in 2008 and expanded across Europe with free returns and local payment methods like pay-on-invoice. It listed in Frankfurt in 2014 at about €5.3B (~$7B) and became Europe's largest online fashion platform.

companies.o: Pursues a magnet-free sheared-flow Z-pinch fusion design aimed at cheaper, smaller reactors.
companies.story: Zap spun out of University of Washington research to skip the giant magnets most fusion designs need, using a sheared-flow Z-pinch instead. It raised a $160M Series C and later a $130M round disclosed in an SEC filing, about $327M in total per PitchBook, while working toward scientific breakeven.

companies.o: Free HR software paid for by health-insurance broker commissions
companies.story: Zenefits gave small businesses free HR software and earned broker commissions on their health insurance, reaching a $4.5B valuation in 2015. In 2016 it emerged that founder Parker Conrad had built a tool to let staff skip California's required broker-licensing training; he resigned, its valuation was cut, and TriNet bought it in 2022.

companies.o: Online video lessons and exam prep for Indonesian school students
companies.story: Zenius was one of Indonesia's oldest online-learning brands for school students and scaled during the pandemic edtech boom. As the funding winter hit, it went through layoffs and in January 2024 said it would temporarily shut down operations, as reported in e27's roundup of the least-funded month of 2023. Funding totals are not confirmed by the sources collected.

companies.o: 10-minute grocery and essentials delivery from a dense network of dark stores
companies.story: Founded in 2021 by teenage Stanford dropouts Aadit Palicha and Kaivalya Vohra, Zepto bet on 10-minute delivery from dark stores in dense Indian cities just as Gorillas, Getir and JOKR were retreating from the US and Europe. It reached a $7B private valuation and SEBI approved its IPO on 8 May 2026, but the listing was postponed and it raised over Rs 1,000 crore in a pre-IPO placement instead (per August 2026 reports).

companies.o: Buy-now-pay-later and checkout EMI platform for Indians without credit cards
companies.story: Goldman Sachs- and Zip-backed ZestMoney offered BNPL and EMI credit at online checkouts and was valued at about $445-450M in 2021. A roughly $200-300M sale to PhonePe collapsed in 2023 over due diligence and bad-loan concerns, the founders resigned, and the company announced it would wind down in December 2023 after RBI tightened rules on fintech credit lines. DMI Group bought the remains in a January 2024 distress sale for an undisclosed sum.

companies.o: Tsinghua spinout behind the GLM models, the first of China's 'AI tigers' to go public
companies.story: Spun out of Tsinghua University's knowledge-engineering lab in 2019, Zhipu sold its GLM models heavily to government and state-owned customers and was added to the US Entity List in January 2025. It listed in Hong Kong on 8 January 2026, raising about $558M and closing its debut at about HK$55.5B ($7.1B). By June 2026 the shares were up about 10x, a market value of about HK$580B (about $74B at 7.8 HKD/USD), overtaking MiniMax.

companies.o: Fashion marketplace that pivoted into B2B supply-chain software and sourcing for Asian apparel makers

rounds.lead: Burda Principal Investments, Sequoia Capital India
Burda Principal Investments, Sofina, Sequoia Capital India

companies.story: Zilingo started as a consumer fashion marketplace and pivoted to B2B software and sourcing for apparel makers, raising a $226M Series D in 2019 at a reported ~$970M valuation. In 2022 a fundraise surfaced questions about its accounting, CEO Ankiti Bose was suspended and then fired, a management buyout failed, and the company went into liquidation under creditors Varde and Indies Capital.

companies.o: Autonomous drone delivery network that started with blood in Rwanda and now delivers for Walmart
companies.story: Zipline launched in 2016 flying blood to rural Rwandan clinics under a government contract, proving its fixed-wing drones over millions of flights before tackling US home delivery, where most drone startups had stalled. It raised $330M at $4.2B in 2023, over $600M at $7.6B led by Valor in January 2026, and in November 2026 $1.5B at a $21.5B post-money valuation alongside a national Walmart deal for 300 more sites.

companies.o: Restaurant discovery site turned India's largest food delivery app

rounds.lead: Info Edge, Vy Capital, Sequoia Capital

companies.story: Started in 2008 as Foodiebay, a site of scanned restaurant menus backed early by Info Edge, it pivoted into food delivery in 2015 and fought Swiggy to a duopoly after rivals like TinyOwl and Foodpanda India collapsed. Its July 2021 Rs 9,375 crore IPO (~$1.27B at 73.9) was ~38x subscribed and the stock closed day one up ~66% at a market cap of about Rs 98,700 crore (~$13.4B). It bought Blinkit in 2022 and renamed itself Eternal in 2025.

companies.o: UK property listings portal with free home valuations
companies.story: Alex Chesterman launched Zoopla in 2007 with free home-value estimates and became the No. 2 UK property portal, listing in London in 2014 at about £919M (~$1.5B). Silver Lake bought its parent ZPG in 2018 for £2.2B (~$2.9B); Chesterman's next company, Cazoo, collapsed in 2024.

companies.o: Pizza delivery company that used robots and ovens in moving trucks
companies.story: Zume made pizzas with robots and baked them in ovens inside delivery trucks, then took $375M from SoftBank in 2018 at a reported $2.25B valuation. The pizza oven-trucks never worked well enough, so in January 2020 it stopped making pizza, cut half its staff and pivoted to compostable food packaging, before shutting down and liquidating in June 2023 after raising about $445M.

companies.o: Industrial-scale mealworm farming for animal feed and fertiliser
companies.story: Ÿnsect raised one of the largest agri-food rounds ever ($372M Series C in 2020) to build a giant automated insect farm in Amiens. The plant overran costs while insect meal stayed pricier than fishmeal and soy; it entered receivership in 2024 and was ordered into liquidation in 2025.

home_services_marketplace.idea: App marketplace for booking cleaners, beauticians, plumbers and other home-service pros
home_services_marketplace.lesson: Homejoy shut in 2015 amid worker-classification lawsuits and weak repeat bookings, while Urban Company trained and certified its own pros, standardised pricing and listed in India in 2025.

quick_commerce_dark_stores.idea: Groceries and essentials delivered in 10-30 minutes from dark stores
quick_commerce_dark_stores.lesson: Kozmo (2001), Europe's Gorillas and Getir and LatAm's JOKR burned out on delivery costs in low-density or high-wage cities, while Zepto and Blinkit made 10-minute dark stores work in dense Indian cities with cheap riders and high order frequency.

dockless_bike_sharing.idea: Dockless app-unlocked shared bicycles parked anywhere
dockless_bike_sharing.lesson: The bikes were nearly identical; ofo, Bluegogo and Wukong died in China's 2017-18 subsidy war, while Mobike sold to Meituan for about $2.7B and Hellobike survived with Ant Financial backing.

ride_hailing.idea: App-based ride hailing with independent drivers
ride_hailing.lesson: Uber sold its China arm to Didi in 2016 and its Southeast Asia arm to Grab in 2018, and Korea's Tada was legislated out in 2020: local champions with local payments, vehicle types and regulator relationships won their home markets.

group_buying_daily_deals.idea: Daily group-buying deals on local restaurants and services
group_buying_daily_deals.lesson: Daily deals faded in the US (Groupon, LivingSocial) and ended in Korea's 2024 TMON/WeMakePrice payment collapse, while Meituan won China's 'thousand-group war' and turned deals into high-frequency food delivery and local services.

online_grocery.idea: Online supermarket with its own warehouses delivering scheduled grocery orders
online_grocery.lesson: Webvan died in 2001 building warehouses ahead of demand, and later inventory-led grocers lived or died on order density and access to capital: BigBasket sold to Tata in 2021, while Missfresh, Honestbee and Merqueo ran out of money.

anything_delivery.idea: On-demand delivery of anything from local stores
anything_delivery.lesson: Delivering 'anything' worked where it grew into a super-app with food and payments density (Rappi, Glovo, Postmates' sale to Uber), while Dunzo, squeezed by better-funded quick-commerce rivals, collapsed in 2024-25.

neobank.idea: App-only consumer bank with no branches
neobank.lesson: Nubank won Brazil by attacking a concentrated, high-fee banking market with a free credit card, while Australia's fully licensed Xinja and Volt could not raise follow-on capital in an already competitive market and handed back deposits in 2020 and 2022.

bnpl.idea: Buy now, pay later instalments at online and in-store checkout
bnpl.lesson: Afterpay sold to Block for about US$29B in 2022 after winning early, while later entrants Openpay (2023), Laybuy (2024) and India's ZestMoney failed once interest rates and regulation tightened.

online_used_cars.idea: Buy and sell inspected used cars online with delivery and financing
online_used_cars.lesson: Inventory-heavy online car retailers in the US and UK (Beepi, Shift, Vroom, Cazoo) collapsed when capital got expensive, while Kavak and Cars24 became unicorns in markets where low-trust informal dealing left more room for a certified retailer.

edtech_boom_bust.idea: Online test prep, tutoring and K-12 learning apps
edtech_boom_bust.lesson: The pandemic edtech boom ended in collapse for Byju's, 2U, Lido and Zenius and in China's 2021 ban on for-profit tutoring, while PhysicsWallah, built on low-price YouTube teaching, listed in India in 2025.

food_delivery.idea: Restaurant food-delivery marketplace with its own rider fleet
food_delivery.lesson: Food delivery consolidated to one or two winners per market: Zomato and Swiggy absorbed India's field (TinyOwl and Foodpanda India sold or shut), Meituan out-scaled Alibaba's Ele.me, iFood dominates Brazil and Baemin dominates Korea.

b2b_informal_retail.idea: B2B app supplying inventory and credit to small corner shops (kiranas, warungs, tiendas, dukas)
b2b_informal_retail.lesson: Supplying small shops is thin-margin and capital-hungry: Frubana and Ula shut and Twiga shrank when funding dried up, while Udaan survived only by raising repeatedly and cutting categories.

lease_arbitrage.idea: Lease office space long, fit it out, and rent desks short as flexible coworking
lease_arbitrage.lesson: WeWork went bankrupt in 2023 on long fixed leases and China's Ucommune shrank after its 2020 listing, while India's Awfis listed in 2024 by relying on landlord-funded, revenue-share 'managed aggregation' deals.

dockless_scooters.idea: Shared dockless e-scooters and e-bikes rented by the minute
dockless_scooters.lesson: Bird went bankrupt in 2023 and Latin America's Grin/Grow collapsed in 2020, while Lime reached profitability and India's Yulu survived by renting low-speed e-bikes to delivery riders.

ev_startups.idea: New electric-car maker building its own vehicles
ev_startups.lesson: Byton, WM Motor, HiPhi and Jiyue died like Fisker and Canoo in the US, while Nio, Li Auto and Xpeng survived China's EV price war by reaching volume and landing state or strategic capital in time.

ev_two_wheelers.idea: Electric scooter maker selling direct to consumers
ev_two_wheelers.lesson: Ather's slower, product-first build kept gaining share, while Ola Electric's subsidy-fuelled rush lost market share and most of its value after its 2024 listing.

cloud_kitchens.idea: Delivery-only kitchens running virtual restaurant brands
cloud_kitchens.lesson: Delivery-only kitchen landlords like Kitchen United closed or shrank, while Rebel Foods survived in India by owning its own food brands (Faasos, Behrouz) on top of Zomato and Swiggy demand.

crypto_exchange.lesson: FTX and QuadrigaCX collapsed through fraud, Zipmex froze withdrawals in 2022 and WazirX lost about $230M to a 2024 hack, while Coinbase listed in 2021 and Bitso grew into Latin America's largest exchange.

online_furniture.idea: Online-first furniture and home decor brand or marketplace
online_furniture.lesson: Made.com (UK) and Fabelio (Indonesia) collapsed in 2022, while Wayfair, Pepperfry and Castlery kept operating, the latter two adding physical showrooms.

homegrown_social_apps.idea: National messaging or social app built to beat a global incumbent
homegrown_social_apps.lesson: Hike and Koo died fighting WhatsApp and Twitter/X head-on, while Kakao and LINE won because they reached Korea and Japan before WhatsApp and built payments and services on top.

ten_minute_grocery.idea: Groceries delivered in 10-15 minutes from neighbourhood dark stores
ten_minute_grocery.lesson: 10-minute delivery worked in dense, lower-wage Istanbul and Indian metros (Getir Turkey, Zepto, Blinkit) but collapsed across Western Europe and the US once cheap capital ended, because wages and low order density made most orders loss-making; Getir quit every market outside Turkey by 2024.

food_delivery_wars.lesson: Food delivery is winner-take-most city by city: whoever reached order density first (Talabat, Yemeksepeti, Lieferando in Germany, Glovo in Spain, Wolt in the Nordics) won, while late or sub-scale entrants (Take Eat Easy, Deliveroo in Germany and Spain, Jumia Food) exited.

ride_hailing_local_champions.lesson: Local champions beat Uber where they adapted faster to cash payments, licensed drivers and local regulation (Careem, Cabify, Bolt, DiDi, Grab); several ended up selling to Uber or swapping equity with it rather than fighting to the end.

mass_transit_buses.idea: Tech-run bus networks booked by app
mass_transit_buses.lesson: FlixBus won by running an asset-light intercity network for existing bus operators right after German deregulation, while subsidised urban shuttle startups (Swvl, Ford's Chariot, Bridj) burned cash and shut or shrank.

mobile_money.idea: Phone-based money transfers and payments through agent networks
mobile_money.lesson: Mobile money exploded where banks were scarce and a dominant telco or agent network existed (Kenya, Senegal, Nigeria) and flopped where banks already served people: the same M-Pesa product reached about 76,000 active users in South Africa and was shut in 2016.

online_car_retail.idea: Buy and sell used cars online with home delivery
online_car_retail.lesson: Holding car inventory needs cheap capital: Auto1 (B2B wholesale first, fast turnover) survived, Cazoo and Vroom collapsed when rates rose, and Carvana came close to failing before recovering.

evtol_air_taxi.lesson: Certification took far longer and more cash than SPAC-era plans assumed; US players with deep strategic backers survived while Germany's two leaders (Lilium, Volocopter) ran out of money in 2024-25.

battery_gigafactory.lesson: CATL scaled with China's supply chain and huge domestic EV demand, while Western newcomers hit production-yield problems and capital gaps: Britishvolt never built its plant and Northvolt went bankrupt after raising over $15B.

vertical_farming.idea: Indoor vertical farms growing produce near cities
vertical_farming.lesson: The idea failed in every market: when energy prices rose after 2022, indoor farms in Europe (Infarm) and the US (AeroFarms, Bowery, Plenty) could not make produce cheaply enough and collapsed.

social_network_clones.idea: Social network for friends and classmates
social_network_clones.lesson: Local Facebook-style networks won their countries first and sold well (StudiVZ €85M, Tuenti €70M, Hyves €44M), but all lost to Facebook within a few years of it launching in their language; Russia's VKontakte was the rare survivor.

used_goods_marketplace.idea: App for buying and selling second-hand goods
used_goods_marketplace.lesson: Second-hand marketplaces win on local density or a niche (Wallapop in Spain, Vinted in fashion with buyer-paid fees); Barcelona-built Letgo spent close to $1B on the US with TV ads and lost to OfferUp and Facebook Marketplace.

online_fashion.lesson: Online fashion failed in 2000 when broadband and logistics were missing (Boo.com) and worked a decade later with free returns and local payment methods (Zappos, Zalando, ASOS); luxury marketplace Farfetch later collapsed under acquisitions and losses.

payments_infra.lesson: Processors that built their own stack and grew with internet merchants won (Adyen, Stripe, Paystack, Flutterwave), while Wirecard faked growth through partners and collapsed in 2020.

transit_navigation_apps.lesson: Apps with crowdsourced data sold to strategic buyers for about $1B (Waze to Google, Moovit to Intel), while Citymapper stayed independent without a working revenue model and sold quietly to Via in 2023.

digital_insurers.lesson: Insurtechs that controlled claims costs and sold through employers (Alan) kept growing, while fast-growing consumer and broker models with weak loss ratios needed rescues (Wefox) or failed (Luko).

energy_supplier_disruptors.lesson: Both UK challengers launched in 2015; Octopus hedged and built its own Kraken software platform and absorbed rivals, while unhedged Bulb collapsed when gas prices spiked in 2021.

music_streaming.idea: Music on demand over the internet
music_streaming.lesson: Licensed streaming won where it gave labels an alternative to piracy (Spotify in Sweden, Anghami in the Arab world), while P2P services (Kazaa, Napster) were sued out of existence and Rdio ran out of cash in 2015.

digital_freight.idea: Apps matching shippers with trucks and couriers
digital_freight.lesson: Digital freight brokers mostly died when freight rates and funding fell (Sendy, Fetchr, US-based Convoy), while India's BlackBuck reached an IPO by charging truckers for software and payments.

regional_amazon.idea: A regional 'Amazon' everything-store with its own logistics
regional_amazon.lesson: Regional e-commerce leaders that built their own delivery and cash-on-delivery (Souq, Flipkart, MercadoLibre) won or sold to Amazon and Walmart, while under-funded rivals were sold cheaply (Konga) or collapsed (Copia).

vacation_rentals.idea: Marketplace for renting private homes to travellers
vacation_rentals.lesson: Rocket Internet's Wimdu launched with a $90M Series A to beat Airbnb to Europe, but Airbnb bought a German clone, localised fast and won; Wimdu shut in 2018.

meal_kits.idea: Subscription boxes of recipes and pre-portioned ingredients
meal_kits.lesson: HelloFresh spread across many markets and cut marketing costs with scale, while single-market Blue Apron shrank after its 2017 IPO and sold for $103M in 2023.

scooter_sharing.lesson: After the 2018-21 land grab, operators that cut costs and won city tenders (Lime, Voi) reached profitability, while Bird went bankrupt in 2023 and Tier merged into Dott in 2024.

online_tutoring.lesson: Pandemic demand made GoStudent and BYJU'S giants, but BYJU'S then imploded and GoStudent shrank, while Nigeria's Edukoya shut in 2025 because poor connectivity and devices made live tutoring hard to scale.

leo_satellite_broadband.lesson: OneWeb went bankrupt in 2020 when its main investor stopped funding it, while SpaceX's Starlink used its own reusable rockets to launch satellites far more cheaply.

online_pet_supplies.idea: Sell pet food and supplies online with home delivery
online_pet_supplies.lesson: Pets.com shipped heavy, low-margin goods below cost in 2000, while Chewy launched in 2011 with cheaper logistics, repeat Autoship subscriptions and service-led loyalty, and sold to PetSmart for $3.35B.

instant_delivery.idea: Deliver convenience goods to your door in under an hour
instant_delivery.lesson: Kozmo and Urbanfetch delivered small orders free and burned out in 2001, while Gopuff owned its inventory for retail margins, charged delivery fees and grew slowly from college towns before raising at $15B.

social_network.idea: Online social network of real friends
social_network.lesson: theglobe.com was too early, Friendster's site slowed to a crawl as it grew, and Myspace filled with spam after selling to News Corp, while Facebook expanded campus by campus on reliable infrastructure.

group_buying.idea: Daily group-buying discounts at local merchants
group_buying.lesson: Groupon and LivingSocial faded as merchants tired of deep discounts, while China's Meituan survived a brutal group-buying price war by turning its merchant network into food delivery.

personal_finance_app.idea: Aggregate all your bank accounts into one budgeting app
personal_finance_app.lesson: Mint synced accounts automatically and sold to Intuit for $170M in 2009, while privacy-focused Wesabe required more manual work and shut down in 2010.

cloud_gaming.idea: Stream video games from cloud servers instead of local consoles
cloud_gaming.lesson: OnLive sold consumer subscriptions on costly per-user server hardware and collapsed in 2012, while Gaikai sold demo streaming to publishers and was bought by Sony for $380M the same year.

ai_coding_assistant.idea: AI that writes and completes code for programmers
ai_coding_assistant.lesson: Kite launched before large language models were good enough and shut in 2022, while Cursor and Windsurf arrived with GPT-4-class models; Windsurf, dependent on outside model providers, was split between Google and Cognition in 2025.

ai_lab_exits.idea: Independent AI model lab or AI-native product company
ai_lab_exits.lesson: Labs without distribution or a clear enterprise niche (Inflection, Adept, Character.AI, Covariant) let Big Tech hire their founders through licensing deals in 2024, while OpenAI's consumer breakout and Cohere's enterprise focus let them keep raising independently.

mobile_photo_sharing.idea: Mobile app for sharing photos with friends
mobile_photo_sharing.lesson: Color raised $41M before launch for a confusing proximity-based app and ended in an acquihire, while Instagram shipped one simple feature and sold to Facebook for $1B 18 months after launch.

smart_wearables.lesson: Fitbit won with reliable hardware and retail distribution and IPO'd in 2015, while Jawbone's faulty bands and lawsuits ended in liquidation and Pebble sold its assets to Fitbit for $23M.

satellite_internet.idea: Constellations of low-orbit satellites for global connectivity
satellite_internet.lesson: Iridium and Teledesic failed in the late 1990s when launch and handset costs were too high, while SpaceX cut launch costs with reusable rockets and made Starlink work two decades later.

space_as_a_service.idea: Rent space short-term to users (desks, apartments) at scale
space_as_a_service.lesson: WeWork and Sonder signed long fixed leases and rented space short-term, which collapsed when demand fell, while Airbnb ran an asset-light marketplace of hosts' homes and owned no leases.

crypto_custody.idea: Hold and grow retail customers' crypto deposits
crypto_custody.lesson: Platforms that lent out, traded or misused customer deposits (QuadrigaCX, Celsius, BlockFi, Voyager, FTX) collapsed, while Coinbase, which held assets in custody under US regulation, survived every crash.

chef_meal_delivery.idea: Deliver freshly cooked meals on demand
chef_meal_delivery.lesson: Sprig and Munchery cooked every meal in their own kitchens and died of high costs, while DoorDash and Deliveroo only delivered restaurants' food and India's Rebel Foods ran many brands out of shared cloud kitchens.

autonomous_driving.lesson: Argo depended on two automaker backers who pulled out in 2022 and Cruise was shut by GM after a 2023 crash, while Aurora narrowed to highway trucking and launched driverless commercial runs in Texas in 2025.

hr_benefits_platform.idea: All-in-one HR, payroll and benefits software for small businesses
hr_benefits_platform.lesson: Zenefits gave software away and relied on insurance-broker commissions, which led to a licensing scandal, while the same founder's Rippling charged for software built on one employee database and became worth several times more.
